nodes.name: Jacobian G, variance V and covariance Omega
nodes.statement_short: G is the target's Jacobian at the true parameter, V = diag(V_k / v_k), Omega the duplicated block covariance.

nodes.statement:
For any non-decreasing sequence $(\ell_n)$ with $\ell_n\le n$, under
Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, for each $k$,
\[
  U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_n,k}
  = (n-\ell_n)\big[-(1-\alpha)v_k + o(1)\big]
    + (M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_n,k})
    + \ell_n\big(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n,k} - \hat{\rho}_{n,k}\big).
\]
nodes.name: Additive decomposition of the $U$-increment
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the U-increment into negative drift, assignment-martingale increment and target-change term.
nodes.label: lem:diff_U_decomp

nodes.statement:
Expanding $U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_n,k}$ from Definition~\ref{def:U} and grouping the
target terms around $v_k$,
$U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_n,k}
 = (n-\ell_n)\big[-(1-\alpha)v_k - (\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-v_k)
   + \frac{\alpha}{n-\ell_n}\sum_{m=\ell_n}^{n-1}(\hat{\rho}_{m,k}-v_k)\big]
   + M_{n,k}-M_{\ell_n,k} + \ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n,k}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k})$.
By Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN}, $\hat{\rho}_n\to v$, so both $\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-v_k$ and
the Cesàro average $\frac1{n-\ell_n}\sum_{m=\ell_n}^{n-1}(\hat{\rho}_{m,k}-v_k)$
are $o(1)$ (treating separately the bounded and diverging cases of $\ell_n$).

\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.diff\_U\_decomp}. The exact $M$-explicit identity is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.auxU\_sub}; the $o(1)$ remainder $\alpha\sum_{[\ell_n,n)}(\hat\rho_m-v)
-(n-\ell_n)(\hat\rho_n-v)$ is made rigorous as ``for every $\varepsilon>0$, eventually
$|\cdot|\le\varepsilon(n-\ell_n)$'', its first term controlled by the windowed Cesàro bound
\texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_sum\_Ico\_sub\_le\_of\_tendsto} (valid for an arbitrary window, bounded or
diverging) and its second by $\hat\rho_n\to v$.
nodes.name: Proof of Additive decomposition of the $U$-increment
nodes.statement_short: Expand the U-difference around v_k and use convergence of the plug-in target.

nodes.statement:
Under Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B} there is a constant $C\ge0$ with, for any
non-decreasing $(\ell_n)$, $\ell_n\le n$,
\[
  \big|\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n} - \hat{\rho}_n)\big|
  \le o(1)(n-\ell_n) + C\|Q_n - Q_{\ell_n}\| + o_p(\sqrt n).
\]
nodes.name: Control of $\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)$
nodes.statement_short: Bound the target-change term by o(1)(n-ell) plus C times the Q-increment plus o_p(sqrt n).
nodes.label: lem:ell_rho_control

nodes.statement:
By Corollary~\ref{cor:mart_Op}, $Q_{n,k}=O_p(\sqrt n)$, hence
$\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\theta_k = Q_{n,k}/N_{n,k} + o_p(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}) = O_p(n^{-1/2})$
using $N_{n,k}\sim v_k n$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_error_Q}). The Taylor expansion of
$\Target$ gives $\hat{\rho}_n - v = G(\estParams_n-\Params)+O_p(1/n)$ and similarly
at $\ell_n$; subtracting,
$\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)
 = \ell_n G(\estParams_{\ell_n}-\estParams_n) + O_p(1)$, so
$|\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)| \le C\ell_n\|\estParams_{\ell_n}-\estParams_n\| + O_p(1)$.
Writing the estimator difference through $Q$ (splitting into the increment
$\sum_{j=\ell_n+1}^n$ and the reweighting of $\sum_{j\le\ell_n}$) and bounding
each piece using $N_{n,k}-N_{\ell_n,k}\le n-\ell_n$ and the SLLN, the three
resulting terms are respectively $C\|Q_n-Q_{\ell_n}\|$, $o(1)(n-\ell_n)$ and
$o_p(\sqrt n)$.

\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.ell\_rho\_control} produces the bound in the shape
$\ell_n|\hat\rho_{\ell_n,k}-\hat\rho_{n,k}| \le V_\rho(n-\ell_n)+W_\rho$ with $V_\rho=o_p(1)$,
$W_\rho=o_p(\sqrt n)$, which is what the drift-sign step consumes. The Condition-\textbf{B} input
enters as the single hypothesis \texttt{hlip} (the target is Lipschitz near $\Params$, so
$|\hat\rho_{\ell,k}-\hat\rho_{n,k}|\le L\sum_{k'}|\hat\theta_{\ell,k'}-\hat\theta_{n,k'}|$
eventually) --- mirroring how \texttt{clt\_rho} takes the derivative as a hypothesis. The
estimator-increment control $\ell|\hat\theta_{\ell,k'}-\hat\theta_{n,k'}|\le g_{k'}(n-\ell)+h_{k'}
|Q_{n,k'}-Q_{\ell,k'}|$ is \texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_estimator\_diff\_le}; the coefficients are
$g_{k'}=o_p(1)$ (from the Doob-maximal bound \texttt{isBigOpOne\_sup'\_abs\_div\_sqrt} and the a.s.\
bound \texttt{isBigOpOne\_of\_ae\_bounded}) and the reweighting coefficient
$h_{k'}=\ell_n/(N_{n,k'}+1)$, which is only \emph{bounded in probability} ($O_p(1)$, converging a.s.\
to $1/v_{k'}$, again via \texttt{isBigOpOne\_of\_ae\_bounded}), not by a uniform constant; it
therefore enters the $o_p$ bookkeeping through $O_p\cdot o_p=o_p$
(\texttt{IsBigOpOne.mul\_littleOp}). The $Q$-increment control
$|Q_{n,k'}-Q_{\ell,k'}|\le Q_v(n-\ell)+Q_w$ is \texttt{qm\_increments\_resp}.
nodes.name: Proof of Control of $\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)$
nodes.statement_short: Taylor-expand the target, express estimator differences through Q, and bound three resulting terms.

nodes.statement:
Under Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, for the hitting time $\ell_{n,k}$,
\[
  \|Q_n - Q_{\ell_{n,k}}\| \le o_p(1)(n-\ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt n),
  \qquad
  |M_{n,k} - M_{\ell_{n,k},k}| \le o_p(1)(n-\ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt n).
\]
nodes.name: $Q$- and $M$-increments are $o_p(\sqrt n)$ plus drift
nodes.statement_short: Increments of Q and M since the hitting time are o_p(1)(n-ell)+o_p(sqrt n).
nodes.label: lem:QM_increments

nodes.statement:
Pick $L_n\to\infty$ with $L_n = o(n)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal_dyadic} bound the two maximal quantities
$\E[\max_{m\le L_n}\|Q_n-Q_{n-m}\|]\le 2\sqrt{L_n C_0}$ and
$\E[\max_{L_n\le m<n}\frac{\|Q_n-Q_{n-m}\|}{m}]\le 3\sqrt{C_0/L_n}$; by
Lemma~\ref{lem:expectation_to_O} these are $O_p(\sqrt{L_n})=o_p(\sqrt n)$ and
$O_p(1/\sqrt{L_n})=o_p(1)$ respectively. Plugging into the deterministic
inequality of Lemma~\ref{lem:increment_control} gives the bound for $Q$; the same
argument applied to $M$ gives the second bound.

\emph{Formalization.} The two maximal quantities are formalized as \texttt{wmaxSeq} and
\texttt{vmaxSeq} (with the concrete window $L_n=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor$), and the two $o_p$ statements
are \texttt{AlphaRAR.isLittleOpOne\_wmaxSeq\_div\_sqrt} ($o_p(\sqrt n)$) and
\texttt{AlphaRAR.isLittleOpOne\_vmaxSeq} ($o_p(1)$), proved from the \emph{vector} maximal bounds
(Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal_pi}) and Markov's inequality. The deterministic increment control is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.norm\_increment\_le\_vmaxSeq\_wmaxSeq}. For $Q$ (the response martingale, a
square-integrable family) the $o_p$ statements are \texttt{AlphaRAR.qm\_increments\_resp}; for the
scalar assignment martingale $M$ (bounded increments $|\Delta M|\le1$) they are
\texttt{AlphaRAR.qm\_increments\_of\_bdd} (via the singleton family $\{M\}$).
nodes.name: Proof of $Q$- and $M$-increments are $o_p(\sqrt n)$ plus drift
nodes.statement_short: Maximal bounds over a window L_n = o(n), Markov, and the deterministic increment control.

nodes.statement:
Under Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, for every $k$,
\[
  U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} \le o_p(\sqrt n),
  \qquad
  U_{n,k} - U_{\ell_{n,k},k} \le O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})\ \text{a.s.}
\]
The $o_p(\sqrt n)$ half is formalized (generically) as \texttt{AlphaRAR.isLittleOpOne\_max\_of\_decomp};
the a.s.\ $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ half is formalized (for the $\aRTS$ objects, inline) inside
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_dev\_upper} --- the $U$-increment decomposition \texttt{diff\_U\_decomp} with
$\varepsilon=(1-\alpha)v_k/2$ makes the drift $\le0$, and the $M$- and $\rho$-differences are
$O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ a.s.\ by the assignment-martingale LIL (Cor.~\ref{cor:llil_nat}) and the
plug-in-target rate (Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_rate}).
nodes.name: Upper bound on the $U$-increment
nodes.label: lem:U_increment_bound

nodes.statement:
From Lemma~\ref{lem:ell_rho_control} and the $Q$-bound of
Lemma~\ref{lem:QM_increments},
$|\ell_{n,k}(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k}}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k})| \le o_p(1)(n-\ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt n)$.
Substituting this and the $M$-bound into the decomposition of
Lemma~\ref{lem:diff_U_decomp},
$U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_{n,k},k} = (n-\ell_{n,k})[-(1-\alpha)v_k+o_p(1)] + o_p(\sqrt n)
 \le o_p(\sqrt n)$, since the drift coefficient is $\le0$ and $n-\ell_{n,k}\ge0$.
For the a.s.\ bound, Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN} gives $n(\hat{\rho}_n-v)=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$,
hence $\ell_{n,k}(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k}}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k})=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$,
and the LIL for the martingale $M$ gives $M_{n,k}=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$; the same
substitution yields the second inequality.
nodes.name: Proof of Upper bound on the $U$-increment
nodes.statement_short: Substitute the increment bounds into the U-decomposition; the drift coefficient is nonpositive.

nodes.statement:
Under the generic conditions and Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, for every $k$,
\begin{align*}
  |N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}| &= o_p(\sqrt n), &
  |N_{n,k} - n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}| &= O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})\ \text{a.s.}, \\
  N_{n,k} - n v_k &= O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})\ \text{a.s.}
\end{align*}
\emph{Formalization.} The generic $o_p(\sqrt n)$ assembly is \texttt{AlphaRAR.prop\_dev}: for a finite
family with $\sum_k \mathrm{Dev}_k = 0$ (\texttt{sum\_count\_sub\_smul\_eq\_zero}), the generic
inequality \eqref{eq:generic_ineq}, and the $U$-increment decomposition (drift $-(1-\alpha)v_k$, the
$M$- and $\rho$-terms increment-controlled by \texttt{qm\_increments\_of\_bdd} and
\texttt{ell\_rho\_control}, and an $o_p(1)$ perturbation from \texttt{diff\_U\_decomp}), it yields
$\mathrm{Dev}_k=o_p(\sqrt n)$ via the drift-sign lemma
\texttt{isLittleOpOne\_max\_div\_sqrt\_of\_drift} and the simplex reverse step
\texttt{isLittleOpOne\_dev\_of\_sum\_zero}. The concrete paper-form statement
$|N_{n,k}-n\hat\rho_{n,k}|=o_p(\sqrt n)$ is \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_prop\_dev}, the full, self-contained
$\aRTS$ instantiation: from the $\aRTS$ design bundle (an \texttt{IsAlgEnvSeq} sequence, Condition
\textbf{A} $Y\in L^2$, a continuous simplex-valued target $\Target$, the algorithm-level predicate
\texttt{IsARTS} --- whence the throttle via \texttt{throttle\_of\_isARTS} ---, $\alpha\in[0,1)$,
Condition \textbf{B} ($\Target$ Lipschitz near $\Params$ and non-sparsity $0<v_k$), and the
$\mathrm{thm{:}LLN}$ consistencies $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$ and $\estParams_n\to\Params$), it discharges
\emph{every} hypothesis of \texttt{prop\_dev} internally: the generic inequality via
\texttt{generic\_ineq\_of\_hitting} (a.e., from the throttle), the smallness via
\texttt{preliminary\_small}, the $M$-increment via the seam $M=\texttt{assignMart}$
(\texttt{assignMart\_eq\_assignMG}) and \texttt{qm\_increments\_of\_bdd}, the \texttt{diff\_U\_decomp}
perturbation shown $o_p$ (a.e.\ $\to0$ by $\hat\rho_n\to v$), and the plug-in-target increment control
(Lemma~\ref{lem:ell_rho_control}) via \texttt{ell\_rho\_control}, whose $g$- and $h$-coefficients are
the random-hitting-time bounds \texttt{aRTS\_g\_littleOp} ($O_p\cdot o_p=o_p$, Doob running-max plus
$\sqrt n/(N_n+1)\to0$) and \texttt{aRTS\_h\_bigOp} (a.s.\ bounded). All random-hitting-time terms are
made measurable by \texttt{measurable\_eval\_of\_le}.

The two a.s.\ $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ statements are also formalized, as
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_prop\_dev\_ae} ($N_{n,k}-n\hat\rho_{n,k}=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ a.s.) and
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_count\_sub\_smul\_ae} ($N_{n,k}-nv_k=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ a.s.). The a.s.\
route is \emph{simpler} than the $o_p$ one --- it bypasses the entire \texttt{ell\_rho\_control} /
\texttt{vmaxSeq} maximal-inequality machinery, resting instead on two pointwise a.s.\ loglog rates:
the assignment-martingale LIL
\texttt{AlphaRAR.ae\_eventually\_abs\_assignMart\_le\_sqrt\_nat\_mul\_loglog} ($M_{n,k}=O(\sqrt{n\log
\log n})$ a.s.) and the plug-in-target rate \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_rho\_rate}
($\hat\rho_{n,k}-v_k=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n}/n)$ a.s.). For each arm, \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_dev\_upper}
combines the key inequality \eqref{eq:generic_ineq}, the smallness $\le 0$
(\texttt{preliminary\_small}), and the $U$-increment decomposition \texttt{diff\_U\_decomp} with
$\varepsilon=(1-\alpha)v_k/2$ (so the drift is $\le0$): the $M$- and $\rho$-differences at the random
time $\ell_{n,k}\le n$ are controlled uniformly by
\texttt{AlphaRAR.exists\_forall\_le\_mul\_sqrt\_mul\_log\_log}
(``$O(\sqrt{m\log\log m})$ at every $m\le n$ is $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$''), giving a one-sided
$N_{n,k}-n\hat\rho_{n,k}\le O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$; the reverse step
\texttt{AlphaRAR.isBigO\_of\_forall\_upper\_of\_sum\_zero} (using $\sum_k \mathrm{Dev}_k=0$) upgrades it
to the two-sided bound, and $N_{n,k}-nv_k$ adds $n(\hat\rho_{n,k}-v_k)$ via
\texttt{AlphaRAR.isBigO\_natMul\_sqrt\_mul\_log\_log}.
nodes.name: Deviation between proportions and plug-in target
nodes.statement_short: Counts deviate from n times the plug-in target by o_p(sqrt n) and O(sqrt(n log log n)) a.s.
nodes.label: lem:prop_dev

nodes.statement:
The generic inequality \eqref{eq:generic_ineq} together with
\eqref{eq:generic_small} and Lemma~\ref{lem:U_increment_bound} gives the one-sided
bounds $N_{n,k}-n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \le o_p(\sqrt n)$ and $\le O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$
a.s. The reverse inequality follows from $\sum_j N_{n,j}=n$, $\sum_j\hat{\rho}_{n,j}=1$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:counts_sum}): $n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-N_{n,k}=\sum_{j\ne k}(N_{n,j}-n\hat{\rho}_{n,j})$,
which inherits the same one-sided bounds. Combining gives the absolute-value
statements. The last line adds $n(\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-v_k)=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ from
Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN}.
nodes.name: Proof of Deviation between proportions and plug-in target
nodes.statement_short: One-sided bounds from the generic inequality, reversed using the simplex constraints.

nodes.statement:
Consider any RAR procedure whose pull counts are \emph{regular}: for every $k$ there is a
deterministic sequence $c_{k,n}\to\infty$ with
\[
  \frac{N_{n,k}}{c_{k,n}}\xrightarrow{a.s.}1 .
\]
Under Condition~\textbf{A}, with $D_n := \mathrm{diag}(\sqrt{N_{n,1}},\dots,\sqrt{N_{n,K}})$,
\[
  D_n(\estParams_n - \Params) \eqdist \mathcal{N}\!\big(0, \mathrm{diag}(V_1,\dots,V_K)\big).
\]
No positivity of the limiting proportions is required, so this covers \emph{sparse} arms $v_k=0$.
nodes.section: 7.3 Joint central limit theorem for the estimators
nodes.name: Componentwise joint CLT
nodes.statement_short: Joint CLT for the self-normalized estimator errors whenever pull counts are regular.
nodes.label: lem:componentwise

nodes.statement:
The weaker hypothesis ``$N_{n,k}\to\infty$ a.s.'' does \emph{not} suffice when the index is chosen
adaptively. Take one arm with i.i.d.\ $\mathcal N(\theta,V)$ responses; by the law of the iterated
logarithm $\limsup_m S_m/\sqrt{Vm}=+\infty$ a.s., so an algorithm may pull the arm until
$S_M/\sqrt{VM}>1$, then pause it for the next $M$ rounds, and repeat forever. Then
$N_{n,k}\to\infty$, yet during every pause $Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{V N_{n,k}}=S_M/\sqrt{VM}>1$ is frozen
above its typical value on a positive fraction of rounds, so no $\mathcal N(0,1)$ limit is possible.
This is why the statement is formulated with the regularity $N_{n,k}/c_{k,n}\to1$, which is exactly
what the Slutsky step consumes.
nodes.section: 7.3 Joint central limit theorem for the estimators
nodes.name: The regularity hypothesis is necessary
nodes.label: rem:componentwise_regularity

nodes.statement:
Normalize arm $k$ by the \emph{deterministic} $\sqrt{c_{k,n}}$. By the Cramér--Wold device it
suffices to treat a scalar projection $\sum_k w_k Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{c_{k,n}}$; since the arm indicators
are disjoint, this is again a single martingale-difference array (row $n$ has increments
$\sum_k (w_k/\sqrt{c_{k,n}})X_{i,k}(\xi_{i,k}-\theta_k)$), whose predictable variation is
$\sum_k w_k^2 V_k N_{n,k}/c_{k,n}\to\sum_k w_k^2V_k$ by regularity, and which satisfies the
conditional Lindeberg condition since $c_{k,n}\to\infty$. Theorem~\ref{thm:mart_clt} and
Cramér--Wold give $(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{c_{k,n}})_k\eqdist\mathcal N(0,\mathrm{diag}(V_k))$. The
coordinatewise scaling $\sqrt{c_{k,n}/N_{n,k}}\to1$ in probability, so multivariate Slutsky
transfers the limit to the self-normalized vector $(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{N_{n,k}})_k$. Finally the Bahadur
identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator_bahadur}) and one more Slutsky step give the statement for
$D_n(\estParams_n-\Params)$.

\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.estimatorError\_joint\_tendsto\_multivariateGaussian}. The key
device is that the weighted martingale array \texttt{AlphaRAR.wArray} carries \emph{row-dependent}
weights $w^{(n)}_k = w_k/\sqrt{c_{k,n}}$, so one array covers both a common normalizer and per-arm
ones; the Cramér--Wold projection is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.wLinComb\_scaled\_tendsto\_gaussianReal}. Taking $c_{k,n}=n$ (with
$N_{n,k}/n\to v_k>0$) recovers Corollary~\ref{cor:mart_clt_componentwise}; taking per-arm $c_{k,n}$
with limit $1$ gives the sparse form used in Chapter~\ref{chap:forced}. Note that a linear
combination of \emph{random-time} sums is not itself a random-time sum, so the Anscombe route
(Lemma~\ref{lem:anscombe_clt}) does not jointify; the martingale-array route above does, precisely
because the arm indicators are disjoint.
nodes.section: 7.3 Joint central limit theorem for the estimators
nodes.name: Proof of Componentwise joint CLT
nodes.statement_short: Cramer-Wold on a weighted martingale array with deterministic normalizers, martingale CLT, then Slutsky and the Bahadur identity.

nodes.statement:
Suppose $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$ a.s.\ with $v_k>0$ for every arm $k$. Then, under
Condition~\textbf{A}, $\sqrt n(\estParams_n - \Params)\eqdist\mathcal{N}(0,V)$ with
$V=\mathrm{diag}(V_1/v_1,\dots,V_K/v_K)$.
nodes.name: CLT for the estimator
assumptions: Suppose $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$ a.s.\ with $v_k>0$ for every arm $k$
nodes.label: lem:clt_theta

nodes.statement:
Exactly as in Corollary~\ref{cor:mart_clt_componentwise}, but with the deterministic
normalization $\sqrt n$ in place of $D_n=\mathrm{diag}(\sqrt{N_{n,k}})$. By the Bahadur
identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator_bahadur}), coordinate $k$ of
$\sqrt n(\estParams_n-\Params)$ is
$(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{N_{n,k}})\cdot\sqrt{nN_{n,k}}/(N_{n,k}+1)
 + (\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k)\sqrt n/(N_{n,k}+1)$. The self-normalized martingale vector
$(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{N_{n,k}})_k$ converges to $\mathcal N(0,\mathrm{diag}(V_k))$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_clt_joint_selfnorm}); the multiplicative factor tends to $1/\sqrt{v_k}$ and
the additive one to $0$ in probability. Multivariate Slutsky then gives the diagonal rescaling
$\mathrm{diag}(1/\sqrt{v_k})$ of the Gaussian, whose covariance is $\mathrm{diag}(V_k/v_k)=V$.
nodes.name: Proof of CLT for the estimator
nodes.statement_short: Bahadur identity, joint self-normalized CLT and Slutsky with deterministic sqrt(n) scaling.

nodes.statement: Under the standing hypotheses, $\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n - v)\eqdist\mathcal{N}(0,GVG^\top)$.
nodes.name: CLT for the plug-in target
nodes.label: lem:clt_rho

nodes.statement:
By the Taylor expansion (as in Lemma~\ref{lem:ell_rho_control}),
$\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v)=G\sqrt n(\estParams_n-\Params)+O_p(1/\sqrt n)$. Apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_theta} and Slutsky.

\emph{Formalization.} The delta method is assembled in
\texttt{AlphaRAR.clt\_rho}. First, Mathlib's product-space Slutsky lemma
(\texttt{TendstoInDistribution.continuous\_comp\_prodMk\_of\_tendstoInMeasure\_const}) with
$g(x,r)=Gx+r$ combines the estimator
CLT (Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_theta}) with the fact that the first-order remainder
$\sqrt n(\Target(\estParams_n)-\Target(\Params))-G\sqrt n(\estParams_n-\Params)=\sqrt n\,\varphi(\estParams_n-\Params)$
tends to $0$ in probability, and the limiting law is the linear pushforward of the estimator's Gaussian
(\texttt{AlphaRAR.multivariateGaussian\_map\_matrix}, giving the covariance $GVG^\top$). The
remainder-in-probability is discharged by \texttt{MeasureTheory.tendstoInMeasure\_smul\_littleO\_of\_tight}
(an abstract $\varepsilon$--$\delta$ lemma: if $X_n=a_n\cdot S_n$ is tight, $S_n\to0$ in probability and
$\varphi=o(\|\cdot\|)$ at the origin, then $a_n\cdot\varphi(S_n)\to0$ in probability), whose tightness
input is supplied from the estimator CLT via
\texttt{MeasureTheory.tight\_of\_tendsto\_probabilityMeasure} (portmanteau plus continuity from above of
the limit Gaussian over $\{\|x\|\ge j\}\downarrow\emptyset$). The differentiability of $\Target$ at
$\Params$ (Jacobian $G$; Condition~\textbf{B}) and the a.s.\ consistency $\estParams_n\to\Params$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN}) enter as the hypotheses \texttt{hTderiv} and \texttt{hcons}.
nodes.name: Proof of CLT for the plug-in target
nodes.statement_short: Delta method: Taylor expansion plus the estimator CLT and Slutsky.

nodes.name: Asymptotic normality
nodes.statement_short: Deviation of counts from plug-in targets is o_p(sqrt n); estimators and proportions are jointly asymptotically normal.
assumptions: Under the generic conditions and Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}
nodes.label: thm:normality

nodes.statement:
Part (i) is Lemma~\ref{lem:prop_dev}. For (ii), the marginal CLT for
$\estParams_n$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_theta}. By part (i),
$\sqrt n(N_n/n-\hat{\rho}_n)=o_p(1)$, so $\sqrt n(N_n/n-v)$ and
$\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v)$ have the same limit $\mathcal{N}(0,GVG^\top)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_rho}) and are asymptotically equal; the joint vector
$(\sqrt n(N_n/n-v),\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v))$ therefore equals
$(\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v),\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v))+o_p(1)$, which converges to
$\mathcal{N}(0,\Omega)$ by Slutsky.

\emph{Formalization.} Part (ii) is fully formalized for the $\aRTS$ design. The generic joint
statement is \texttt{AlphaRAR.clt\_joint}: it takes the proportion-deviation fact
$\sqrt n(N_n/n-\hat{\rho}_n)\to_p 0$ of part (i) as a hypothesis and assembles the joint CLT from
\texttt{AlphaRAR.clt\_rho}. The joint vector is the image of $\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v)$ under the
duplication map $x\mapsto(x,x)$ (the stacked matrix $[I;I]$) up to an $o_p(1)$ remainder, so the
same product-space Slutsky lemma as in Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_rho} applies, and the limiting covariance
$[I;I]\,GVG^\top\,[I;I]^\top$ is the block matrix $\Omega$ via the rectangular Gaussian pushforward
\texttt{AlphaRAR.multivariateGaussian\_map\_matrix}. The self-contained $\aRTS$ instantiation is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_clt\_joint}: from the same design bundle as \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev} plus the
Condition-\textbf{B} differentiability of $\Target$ at $\Params$ (Jacobian $G$, exactly the
\texttt{clt\_rho} input), it \emph{discharges} the proportion-deviation hypothesis of
\texttt{clt\_joint} from \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_prop\_dev} --- via the generic bridge
\texttt{AlphaRAR.tendstoInMeasure\_toLp\_of\_forall\_isLittleOpOne} (coordinatewise $o_p(1)$ gives
vector convergence in measure) and the $\sqrt n$-scaling identity
$\sqrt n(N_{n,k}/n-v_k)-\sqrt n(\hat\rho_{n,k}-v_k)=(N_{n,k}-n\hat\rho_{n,k})/\sqrt n$ --- and derives
the $\mathrm{thm{:}LLN}$ consistencies as in \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev}. Part (i) is fully formalized:
the $o_p(\sqrt n)$ statement is \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev} and the two a.s.\ $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$
statements are \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev\_ae} and \texttt{aRTS\_count\_sub\_smul\_ae}
(Lemma~\ref{lem:prop_dev}). Both parts of the theorem are therefore complete for the $\aRTS$ design.
nodes.name: Proof of Asymptotic normality
nodes.statement_short: Part (i) is the deviation lemma; part (ii) combines the estimator and target CLTs with Slutsky.

nodes.statement:
When the arm responses belong to one-parameter exponential families with mean
parameter, Proposition~\ref{prop:exp_fam} gives $V_k = I_k(\theta_k)^{-1}$, so the
asymptotic variance $GVG^\top$ of $N_n/n$ equals the lower bound
$G\,I(\Params)^{-1}G^\top$ of \cite{hu2006asymptotically}, with
$I(\Params)=\mathrm{diag}(v_1 I_1(\theta_1),\dots,v_K I_K(\theta_K))$. Hence every
$\aRTS$ design is asymptotically efficient.
nodes.name: Asymptotic efficiency
nodes.label: rem:efficiency

nodes.name: Exploration schedule
nodes.label: def:exploration_schedule

nodes.name: Choice of exploration schedule
nodes.label: ex:h_choice

nodes.statement:
For a schedule $h$ and $m\ge1$,
\[
  \mathbf{U}_m := \{ j\in[K] : N_{m,j} \le h(m)\}, \qquad
  \mathbf{S}_m := \argmin_{j\in\mathbf{U}_m} N_{m,j}.
\]
nodes.name: Under-sampled and least-sampled sets
nodes.label: def:underexplored_sets

nodes.statement:
Fix $\alpha\in[0,1)$ and a schedule $h$. A RAR procedure is in the $\aRTSFE$
family if its allocation probabilities obey:
\begin{align}
  \textbf{(Forced exploration)}\quad
    &\mathbf{U}_m\ne\emptyset \Rightarrow \forall a\in\mathbf{S}_m:\ p_{m+1,a}=\tfrac{1}{|\mathbf{S}_m|}; \\
  \textbf{(Otherwise)}\quad
    &\mathbf{U}_m=\emptyset \Rightarrow p_{m+1}\ \text{satisfies the throttling condition \eqref{eq:throttle}.} \end{align}
Like \texttt{AlphaRAR.IsARTS}, the Lean predicate \texttt{AlphaRAR.IsARTSFE} is stated on
\emph{histories}, so it is a property of the algorithm alone; \texttt{throttle\_of\_isARTSFE} and
\texttt{fe\_of\_isARTSFE} transport it to the process. It weakens \eqref{eq:fe_phase} to
$a\notin\mathbf{S}_m\Rightarrow p_{m+1,a}=0$: uniformity on $\mathbf{S}_m$ is never used, only that
no other arm can be drawn.
nodes.name: $\aRTSFE$ family
nodes.statement_short: aRTS with forced exploration: least-sampled under-explored arms are forced; otherwise the throttle applies.
nodes.label: def:aRTSFE

nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Forced exploration)}\quad
    &\mathbf{U}_m\ne\emptyset \Rightarrow \forall a\in\mathbf{S}_m:\ p_{m+1,a}=\tfrac{1}{|\mathbf{S}_m|};
nodes.name: Forced-exploration phase rule
nodes.label: eq:fe_phase

nodes.statement:
\textbf{(Otherwise)}\quad
    &\mathbf{U}_m=\emptyset \Rightarrow p_{m+1}\ \text{satisfies the throttling condition \eqref{eq:throttle}.}
nodes.name: Throttle outside forced exploration
nodes.label: eq:fe_otherwise

nodes.statement:
The full D-Tracking algorithm of \cite{garivier2016optimal} is the $\aRTSFE$
member with $\alpha=0$ (up to the choice of $h$).
nodes.name: Full D-Tracking is an aRTS-FE member
nodes.label: rem:d_tracking_fe

nodes.statement:
For $k\in[K]$ and $n\ge1$,
\[
  \ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}} := \max\Big\{ m\le n :
    \tfrac{N_{m,k}}{m}\le\hat{\rho}_{m,k}
    \ \text{or}\ \big(\mathbf{U}_m\ne\emptyset\ \text{and}\ k\in\argmin_{j\in\mathbf{U}_m}N_{m,j}\big)\Big\}.
\]
It is the last time before $n$ at which arm $k$ is under-sampled or is a
least-sampled arm among the under-explored set.
nodes.name: $\aRTSFE$ last hitting time
nodes.statement_short: Last time arm k is under-sampled or a least-sampled under-explored arm.
nodes.label: def:hitting_fe

nodes.statement:
For an $\aRTSFE$ design and $m$ with $\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}} < m \le n$,
we have $\frac{N_{m,k}}{m} > \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$ and
$\big(\mathbf{U}_m=\emptyset\ \text{or}\ k\notin\argmin_{j\in\mathbf{U}_m}N_{m,j}\big)$;
consequently $p_{m+1,k}\le\alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$ (equal to $0$ during a forced
exploration step in which $k$ is not least-sampled).
nodes.name: Sign after the $\aRTSFE$ hitting time
nodes.label: lem:hitting_fe_sign

nodes.statement:
By maximality of $\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}}$, neither disjunct in
Definition~\ref{def:hitting_fe} holds at such $m$. If $\mathbf{U}_m\ne\emptyset$
then $k\notin\argmin_{j\in\mathbf{U}_m}N_{m,j}$, so \eqref{eq:fe_phase} gives
$p_{m+1,k}=0\le\alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$. If $\mathbf{U}_m=\emptyset$ then
\eqref{eq:fe_otherwise} and the over-sampling $N_{m,k}/m>\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$ give
$p_{m+1,k}\le\alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$.
nodes.name: Proof of Sign after the $\aRTSFE$ hitting time
nodes.statement_short: Maximality excludes both disjuncts; then forced exploration or the throttle applies.

nodes.statement:
For any $\aRTSFE$ design, the generic conditions
(Definition~\ref{def:generic_cond}) hold with $\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}}$.
nodes.name: $\aRTSFE$ satisfies the generic conditions
nodes.label: lem:preliminary_fe

nodes.statement:
(i) Monotonicity and $\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}}\le n$ are immediate. (ii) The
telescoping identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:U_telescope}, whose proof only uses the
increment of $U$) combined with Lemma~\ref{lem:hitting_fe_sign} — every
intermediate $p_{m,k}-\alpha\hat{\rho}_{m-1,k}\le0$ — gives inequality
\eqref{eq:generic_ineq}. (iii) At $m=\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}}$, either
$N_{m,k}/m\le\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$, giving $N_{m,k}-m\hat{\rho}_{m,k}\le0$, or $k$ is
least-sampled in $\mathbf{U}_m$, giving
$N_{\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}},k}-\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}}\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}},k}
 \le N_{\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}},k}\le h(\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}})=o(n)$
by Definition~\ref{def:exploration_schedule}. (The paper bounds this by $o(\sqrt n)$ using
condition (ii); $o(n)$ is all the consistency direction needs, and the $\sqrt n$-scaled direction
gets a sharper bound from Remark~\ref{rem:sparse_clt_fix}.)
nodes.name: Proof of $\aRTSFE$ satisfies the generic conditions
nodes.statement_short: Verify the three generic conditions for the FE hitting time.

nodes.statement:
Under Conditions~\textbf{A}--\textbf{B}, Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:normality} hold for every design in the $\aRTSFE$ family.
nodes.name: Validity under forced exploration
nodes.statement_short: Both main theorems hold for every aRTS-FE design under Conditions A-B.
conclusions: Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN} and Theorem~\ref{thm:normality} hold for every design in the $\aRTSFE$ family
nodes.label: thm:forced_valid

nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:preliminary_fe} the $\aRTSFE$ design satisfies the generic
conditions with $\ell^{\mathrm{FE}}$; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:generic_main}.

\emph{Formalization.} Both directions are \emph{direct reuses} of abstract-hitting-time theorems
with the forced-exploration hitting predicate \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFEUnder}
(``under-sampled or under-explored''); the design enters as the history-level predicate
\texttt{AlphaRAR.IsARTSFE} (Definition~\ref{def:aRTSFE}), whose throttle field is transported to
the process by \texttt{AlphaRAR.throttle\_of\_isARTSFE}, and the only new ingredients are the
forced-exploration smallness lemmas. So each of the five declarations mentions only the design, the
environment and the schedule --- no process-level throttle hypothesis --- exactly as on the
$\aRTS$ side. The consistency direction
($N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$, $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to v_k$) is \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_proportion\_tendsto}
(reusing \texttt{AlphaRAR.consistency\_of\_hitting}), whose smallness is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_smallness} ($N_\ell-\ell\hat\rho_\ell\le(h(\ell))^+=o(n)$). The
asymptotic-normality direction (Theorem~\ref{thm:normality}) is: the $o_p(\sqrt n)$ deviation
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_prop\_dev} (reusing \texttt{AlphaRAR.prop\_dev\_of\_hitting}, smallness
\texttt{aRTSFE\_smallness\_op}), the a.s.\ $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ deviations
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_prop\_dev\_ae} and \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_count\_sub\_smul\_ae} (reusing
\texttt{prop\_dev\_ae\_of\_hitting}/\texttt{count\_sub\_smul\_ae\_of\_hitting}, smallness
\texttt{aRTSFE\_smallness\_upper}), and the joint CLT \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_clt\_joint} (reusing
\texttt{AlphaRAR.clt\_joint\_of\_hitting}). Each abstract-hitting-time theorem is the generalisation
of the corresponding \texttt{aRTS} theorem to an arbitrary measurable hitting predicate, with the
throttle and smallness taken as hypotheses.

Neither $\sqrt n$-scaled smallness lemma uses condition (ii): under Condition~\textbf{B} forced
exploration eventually stops firing (\texttt{AlphaRAR.eventually\_sched\_lt\_pullCount}, the single-arm
form of \texttt{AlphaRAR.underExplored\_eventually\_empty}), so past that time the hitting predicate
can only fire through its under-sampling clause and the gap is bounded by a path constant
(\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_gap\_le\_sum\_of\_not\_underExplored}) --- which is $o(\sqrt n)$ and
$O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ for free. The Condition~\textbf{B} input is the consistency direction of
this same theorem, so there is no circularity: it needs only $h(n)=o(n)$.
nodes.name: Proof of Validity under forced exploration
nodes.statement_short: The FE design satisfies the generic conditions; apply the generic theorem.

nodes.statement:
For any $\aRTSFE$ design, $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ a.s.\ for every $k\in[K]$ (no
assumption on the target).
nodes.name: Forced exploration prevents starvation
nodes.label: lem:fe_no_starvation

nodes.statement:
Suppose for contradiction that some arm $i$ stalls: $N_{n,i}=M$ for all $n\ge N$.
Since $h(n)\to\infty$, enlarge $N$ so that $h(n)\ge M$ for $n\ge N$. Then for
$n\ge N$, $N_{n,i}\le h(n)$ gives $i\in\mathbf{U}_n\ne\emptyset$, so the arm
$I_{n+1}$ selected by forced exploration is a least-sampled arm of $\mathbf{U}_n$,
whence $N_{n,I_{n+1}}\le N_{n,i}=M$ and $N_{n+1,I_{n+1}}\le M+1$. The potential
$D(n):=\sum_j (M+1-N_{n,j})^+$ then satisfies $D(n+1)-D(n)=-1$ for all $n\ge N$,
so $D$ becomes negative, contradicting $D\ge0$. Hence every arm is sampled
infinitely often.

\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_no\_starvation}, whose deterministic potential-function
core is \texttt{AlphaRAR.no\_starvation\_pathwise}. It weakens ``$i$ stalls at $M$'' to ``$N_{n,i}<B$
for all $n$'' (arm $k$ monotone but bounded), and the action-level forced-exploration rule enters as
the a.s.\ hypothesis \texttt{hfe} (when some arm is under-explored, $A_m$ is a least-sampled
under-explored arm). The potential $D(n)=\sum_j(B+1-N_{n,j})$ is $\N$-valued (truncated subtraction is
the positive part), so $D(n+1)+1=D(n)$ for $n\ge N_1$ forces $t\le D(N_1)$ for all $t$, a contradiction.
nodes.name: Proof of Forced exploration prevents starvation
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction via a potential function that decreases by one each round.

nodes.statement:
Under Condition~\textbf{A} only, any $\aRTSFE$ design satisfies, for every $k$,
\[
  N_{n,k}\xrightarrow{a.s.}+\infty,\qquad
  \frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\xrightarrow{a.s.}v_k,\qquad
  \estParams_n-\Params = O\!\Big(\sqrt{\tfrac{\log\log N_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}}}\Big)\ \text{a.s.}
\]
nodes.name: Consistency and rate for sparse targets
nodes.statement_short: For aRTS-FE under Condition A only: all arms sampled infinitely often, proportions consistent, LIL rate in N.
nodes.label: thm:sparse_rate

nodes.statement:
The first statement is Lemma~\ref{lem:fe_no_starvation}. Given it, every arm's
estimator converges: $\hat{\theta}_{n,k}\to\theta_k$ by the SLLN, so
$\hat{\rho}_n\to v$ by continuity of $\Target$; the matching argument (as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:match}, using Lemma~\ref{lem:convergence} and the generic
inequality valid by Lemma~\ref{lem:preliminary_fe}) gives $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$,
allowing $v_k=0$. The rate is the LIL for the martingale $Q_{\cdot,k}$ scaled by
its own sample size $N_{n,k}$, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_LIL} but without
dividing by $n$.

\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_sparse\_rate}. All three statements flow from
no-starvation (\texttt{aRTSFE\_no\_starvation}, $N_{n,k}\to\infty$): it makes every arm sampled
infinitely often, so $\hat\theta\to\theta$ (\texttt{estimator\_ae\_tendsto\_of\_pullCount\_atTop},
\emph{no positivity}), whence $\hat\rho\to T(\theta)$, and the matching
\texttt{consistency\_of\_hitting} (which never uses positivity, so allows $v_k=0$) gives
$N_{n,k}/n\to T(\theta)_k$. The $N$-scaled rate is \texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_estimator\_sub\_le\_rate\_loglog\_N},
which combines the exact Bahadur identity \texttt{estimator\_sub\_eq} with the subsampled loglog LIL
\texttt{abs\_respMart\_le\_sqrt\_nat\_mul\_loglog} (this uses \emph{only} $N_{n,k}\to\infty$).
nodes.name: Proof of Consistency and rate for sparse targets
nodes.statement_short: No-starvation, SLLN and continuity, the matching argument, and the LIL scaled by N.

nodes.statement:
Under Condition~\textbf{A} only, any $\aRTSFE$ design satisfies
\[
  D_n(\estParams_n-\Params)\eqdist\mathcal{N}\!\big(0,\mathrm{diag}(V_1,\dots,V_K)\big),
  \qquad D_n=\mathrm{diag}(\sqrt{N_{n,1}},\dots,\sqrt{N_{n,K}}).
\]
nodes.name: Componentwise CLT for sparse targets
nodes.statement_short: Componentwise CLT normalized by sqrt(N_{n,k}) for aRTS-FE designs, valid for sparse targets.
nodes.label: cor:sparse_clt

nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:fe_no_starvation}, $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ for all $k$. Given the regularity of the
pull counts, Lemma~\ref{lem:componentwise} applies and gives the statement.

\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_sparse\_clt}. Arms are split by a predicate
$\mathrm{FEfed}$:
\begin{itemize}
  \item if arm $k$ is eventually fed \emph{only} by forced exploration, then its count is regular
    against the \emph{deterministic} schedule, $N_{n,k}/h(n)\to1$
    (\texttt{AlphaRAR.pullCount\_div\_sched\_tendsto\_one});
  \item otherwise arm $k$ has a positive limiting proportion $v_k>0$ with $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$, so it
    is regular against $v_kn$.
\end{itemize}
Both are then covered by the single per-arm normalizer $c_{k,n}=h(n)$ or $v_kn$, which is what
\texttt{estimatorError\_joint\_tendsto\_multivariateGaussian} consumes (at $v\equiv1$). The split is
unavoidable: not every arm can be forced-exploration-fed, since $\sum_kN_{n,k}=n$ while
$K\,h(n)=o(n)$.

The regularity for a forced-exploration-fed arm comes from a two-sided bound. \emph{Upper}
(\texttt{pullCount\_le\_sched\_of\_fe\_only}): at a forced-exploration round the selected arm is
itself under-explored, so one pull leaves it at $h(m)+1\le h(n)+1$. \emph{Lower}
(\texttt{pullCount\_ge\_min\_sched\_of\_fe}): the selected arm is a \emph{least-sampled}
under-explored arm, hence sits at the global minimum, so the potential
$D(m)=\sum_j(L-N_{m,j})^+$ drops by exactly one per round while the minimum stays below $L$; since
$D\le K L$ this can persist for at most $KL$ rounds, so within any longer window the minimum has
reached $L$ or forced exploration stopped firing (which already means every count exceeds $h$). This
is the same potential-function device as Lemma~\ref{lem:fe_no_starvation}. A mild regularity of $h$
itself is assumed (\texttt{hshift}: shifting the argument by the $O(h(n))$ catch-up window does not
change $h$ to first order), satisfied by $h(n)=(n^{1/3}-K/2)^+$.
nodes.name: Proof of Componentwise CLT for sparse targets
nodes.statement_short: No-starvation plus the componentwise CLT under regular counts; Lean splits arms by how they are fed.

nodes.statement:
The hypothesis that a sparse arm is eventually fed only by forced exploration is a genuine
restriction, not an artifact. Since $T\ge0$ and $T(\Params)_k=0$, the point $\Params$ minimises
$T_k$, so $\nabla T_k(\Params)=0$ and $T(\estParams_n)_k=O(\|\estParams_n-\Params\|^2)$. A design
that \emph{chases} its target then allocates arm $k$ about $n\,T(\estParams_n)_k\asymp n/N_{n,k}$
pulls, i.e.\ $N_{n,k}\asymp\sqrt n$ --- which dominates $h(n)=o(\sqrt n)$. For such designs (e.g.\ the
distance-based example, where $\delta_{m,k}=(\hat\rho_{m,k}-N_{m,k}/m)^+>0$ keeps feeding arm $k$)
forced exploration does \emph{not} set the scale, and whether $N_{n,k}/\sqrt n$ converges is a
delicate question about the feedback between the estimator's own fluctuations and the sampling rate.
By Remark~\ref{rem:componentwise_regularity} the conclusion cannot be obtained from
$N_{n,k}\to\infty$ alone, so this case is genuinely open.
nodes.name: Scope of the sparse CLT
nodes.label: rem:sparse_clt_scope

nodes.statement:
The hypothesis discussed in Remark~\ref{rem:sparse_clt_scope} can be \emph{discharged} rather than
assumed, at the price of reversing condition (ii) of Definition~\ref{def:exploration_schedule}.
Replacing $h(n)=o(\sqrt n)$ by $\sqrt{n\log\log n}\ll h(n)=o(n)$ puts a sparse arm in the
forced-exploration-dominated regime, where its count is regular against the deterministic schedule.
Condition (ii) is in any case not needed elsewhere: under Condition~\textbf{B} forced exploration
switches itself off (\texttt{AlphaRAR.underExplored\_eventually\_empty}), so $h(n)=o(n)$ suffices for
the whole $\sqrt n$-theory --- and this is how Theorem~\ref{thm:forced_valid} is actually proved
here, so no declaration of the formalization assumes $h(n)=o(\sqrt n)$. The reversed condition is satisfiable precisely where (ii) fails, e.g.\
$h(n)=n^{2/3}$ (\texttt{AlphaRAR.sched23\_satisfies\_schedule\_hypotheses}).

\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_sparse\_clt\_of\_contDiffAt}: the conclusion of
Corollary~\ref{cor:sparse_clt} with the forced-exploration-fed hypothesis replaced by the reversed
schedule condition and $C^2$ smoothness of $T$ at $\Params$. This is a deviation from the paper, not
a formalization of it; the argument is written up in \texttt{maths/sparse-clt-fix.md}.
nodes.name: Removing the forced-exploration-fed hypothesis
nodes.label: rem:sparse_clt_fix

nodes.statement:
The normalization in Corollary~\ref{cor:sparse_clt} is componentwise (by
$\sqrt{N_{n,k}}$) rather than by $\sqrt n$, which is what makes it meaningful when
$v_k=0$. When $v\in(0,1)^K$ it recovers the classical result of
\cite{hu2006asymptotically}.
nodes.name: Componentwise normalization of the sparse CLT
nodes.label: rem:sparse_normalization

nodes.statement:
Consider $K$ Bernoulli arms and the homogeneity test
\[
  \mathcal{H}_0 : \forall k,\ \theta_k = \theta_1
  \qquad\text{against}\qquad
  \mathcal{H}_1 : \exists i,j,\ \theta_i \ne \theta_j.
\]
nodes.name: Homogeneity test
nodes.statement_short: Null hypothesis of equal Bernoulli means across all arms against some pair differing.

nodes.statement:
Let $S_{n,k} := N_{n,k}\hat{\theta}_{n,k}$ and
$\tilde{\theta}_n := \sum_{k=1}^K \frac{N_{n,k}}{n}\hat{\theta}_{n,k}$ be the
pooled estimator. The \emph{Pearson chi-square statistic} is
\[
  \mathcal{X}_n := \sum_{k=1}^K \frac{(S_{n,k} - N_{n,k}\tilde{\theta}_n)^2}
                                        {N_{n,k}\tilde{\theta}_n(1-\tilde{\theta}_n)}.
\]
nodes.name: Pearson statistic
nodes.statement_short: Pearson chi-square homogeneity statistic computed from adaptively collected data.
nodes.label: def:pearson_stat

nodes.statement:
With $Y_n := (\sqrt{N_{n,k}}(\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\theta))_{k\in[K]}$ and
$s_n := (\sqrt{\omega_{n,k}})_{k\in[K]}$ where $\omega_{n,k}:=N_{n,k}/n$, under
$\mathcal{H}_0$ (common value $\theta$),
\[
  \mathcal{X}_n = \frac{1}{\tilde{\theta}_n(1-\tilde{\theta}_n)}\,
                  Y_n^\top\,(I - s_n s_n^\top)\,Y_n.
\]
nodes.name: Quadratic-form rewriting
nodes.label: lem:pearson_quadform

nodes.statement:
Under $\mathcal{H}_0$, $\sqrt{N_{n,k}}(\tilde{\theta}_n-\theta)
 = \sqrt{\omega_{n,k}}\sum_j\sqrt{\omega_{n,j}}[Y_n]_j$, so
$\sqrt{N_{n,k}}(\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\tilde{\theta}_n) = [Y_n - s_n s_n^\top Y_n]_k$.
Substituting $S_{n,k}-N_{n,k}\tilde{\theta}_n = N_{n,k}(\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\tilde{\theta}_n)$
into Definition~\ref{def:pearson_stat} gives the quadratic form.
nodes.name: Proof of Quadratic-form rewriting
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the centred estimators through the projection I - s s^T.

nodes.statement:
For a unit vector $s\in\R^K$ (here $s=(\sqrt{v_1},\dots,\sqrt{v_K})$ with
$\sum_k v_k=1$), the matrix $I - s s^\top$ is an orthogonal projection of rank
$K-1$.
nodes.name: Idempotent projection
conclusions: the matrix $I - s s^\top$ is an orthogonal projection of rank $K-1$
nodes.label: lem:projection

nodes.statement:
$s^\top s = \sum_k v_k = 1$, so $(I-ss^\top)^2 = I - 2ss^\top + s(s^\top s)s^\top
 = I - ss^\top$, and it is symmetric; its trace $K-1$ equals its rank.
nodes.name: Proof of Idempotent projection
nodes.statement_short: Direct check of idempotence, symmetry and trace.

nodes.statement:
Consider a RAR procedure with $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ a.s.\ for all $k$ (in
particular any $\aRTS$ design under Condition~\textbf{B}, or any $\aRTSFE$
design). Under $\mathcal{H}_0$,
\[
  \mathcal{X}_n \eqdist \chi^2_{K-1}.
\]
nodes.name: Asymptotic null distribution of the Pearson statistic
nodes.statement_short: Under homogeneity the Pearson statistic is asymptotically chi-square with K-1 degrees of freedom.
assumptions: Consider a RAR procedure with $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ a.s.\ for all $k$
nodes.label: lem:pearson

nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:componentwise}, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{\theta(1-\theta)}}Y_n
\eqdist\mathcal{N}(0,I_K)$ (Bernoulli variance $V_k=\theta(1-\theta)$ under
$\mathcal{H}_0$). By Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN}, $\tilde{\theta}_n\to\theta$ and
$s_n\to s=(\sqrt{v_1},\dots,\sqrt{v_K})$, so $I-s_ns_n^\top\to I-ss^\top$, an
orthogonal projection of rank $K-1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}. Slutsky's
lemma and Lemma~\ref{lem:pearson_quadform} give
$\mathcal{X}_n\eqdist Z^\top(I-ss^\top)Z$ with $Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_K)$, which is
$\chi^2_{K-1}$.
nodes.name: Proof of Asymptotic null distribution of the Pearson statistic
nodes.statement_short: Componentwise CLT, consistency of the weights, Slutsky and the projection lemma.

nodes.statement:
Lemma~\ref{lem:pearson} shows that rejecting $\mathcal{H}_0$ when $\mathcal{X}_n$
exceeds the $0.95$-quantile of $\chi^2_{K-1}$ is asymptotically a level-$0.05$
test, valid for all $\aRTS$ designs (under Condition~\textbf{B}) and all
$\aRTSFE$ designs.
nodes.name: Asymptotic level of the Pearson test
nodes.label: rem:test_level

nodes.statement:
$X_n = o_p(a_n)$ if and only if $X_n/a_n = o_p(1)$, and $X_n = O_p(a_n)$ if and
only if $X_n/a_n = O_p(1)$.
nodes.name: Reduction to order one
conclusions: $X_n = o_p(a_n)$ if and only if $X_n/a_n = o_p(1)$
$X_n = O_p(a_n)$ if and only if $X_n/a_n = O_p(1)$
nodes.label: lem:op_factor

nodes.statement:
Unfold Definition~\ref{def:op_Op}: both sides are the same statement about the
sequence $|X_n|/a_n$.
nodes.name: Proof of Reduction to order one
nodes.statement_short: Unfold the definitions.

nodes.statement:
If $X_n \to 0$ in probability (in particular, if $X_n \to 0$ a.s.), then
$X_n = o_p(1)$. If $X_n \to c$ in distribution for some random variable, then
$X_n = O_p(1)$.
nodes.name: Convergence in probability gives $o_p$
nodes.label: lem:op_of_tendsto

nodes.statement:
The first statement is the definition of convergence in probability. For the
second, convergence in distribution implies tightness of the laws
($\{X_n\}$ is uniformly tight), which is exactly $O_p(1)$.
nodes.name: Proof of Convergence in probability gives $o_p$
nodes.statement_short: Definition of convergence in probability; convergence in distribution implies tightness.

nodes.name: Arithmetic of stochastic orders
nodes.label: lem:op_arith

nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:op_factor} reduce to $a_n = 1$. Then (i)--(ii) are union bounds
on the events $\{|X_n| > \varepsilon\}$, $\{|Y_n| > \varepsilon\}$; (iii) follows
by conditioning on the tightness of $X_n$: for $\eta$ pick $M$ with
$\sup_n \Prob(|X_n|>M)\le\eta$, then $\Prob(|X_nY_n|>\varepsilon)\le\eta
+\Prob(|Y_n|>\varepsilon/M)$; (iv) is immediate from boundedness of $c_n$.
nodes.name: Proof of Arithmetic of stochastic orders
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to rate one, then union bounds and tightness.

nodes.statement:
If $X_n \eqdist X$ (convergence in distribution) and $R_n = o_p(1)$, then
$X_n + R_n \eqdist X$. More generally, if $(X_n) \eqdist X$ and $Y_n \to c$ in
probability for a constant $c$, then $(X_n, Y_n) \eqdist (X, c)$.
nodes.name: Slutsky bridge
nodes.label: lem:op_slutsky

nodes.statement:
This is Slutsky's theorem, available in Mathlib as
\texttt{TendstoInDistribution.prodMk\_of\_tendstoInMeasure\_const}, combined with
the continuous mapping theorem \texttt{TendstoInDistribution.continuous\_comp}
applied to addition.
nodes.name: Proof of Slutsky bridge
nodes.statement_short: Slutsky's theorem plus the continuous mapping theorem in Mathlib.

nodes.statement:
Let $(M_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a square-integrable $(\filt_n)$-martingale with $M_0 = 0$.
Its \emph{predictable quadratic variation} is
$\langle M\rangle := \mathrm{predictablePart}(M^2)$, the predictable part of the
submartingale $M^2$ in the Doob decomposition. Equivalently,
$\langle M\rangle_0 = 0$ and
$\langle M\rangle_n = \sum_{i=1}^n \E[(\Delta M_i)^2 \mid \filt_{i-1}]$.
nodes.name: Predictable quadratic variation
nodes.label: def:pred_qv

nodes.statement:
For a square-integrable martingale $M$ with $M_0=0$,
$\langle M\rangle_n - \langle M\rangle_{n-1} = \E[(\Delta M_n)^2\mid\filt_{n-1}]$,
and $\langle M\rangle$ is nondecreasing and predictable.
nodes.name: Increment of the quadratic variation
nodes.label: lem:qv_incr

nodes.statement:
The Doob decomposition of the submartingale $M^2$ has predictable part with
increments $\E[M_n^2 - M_{n-1}^2\mid\filt_{n-1}]
= \E[(\Delta M_n)^2\mid\filt_{n-1}]$, using that $M$ is a martingale so the cross
term $\E[2M_{n-1}\Delta M_n\mid\filt_{n-1}]=0$. Nonnegativity of the increments
gives monotonicity.
nodes.name: Proof of Increment of the quadratic variation
nodes.statement_short: Doob decomposition of M^2; the cross term vanishes.

nodes.statement: If $|\Delta M_i|\le c$ a.s., then $\langle M\rangle_n \le c^2 n$ a.s.
nodes.name: Linear bound on $\langle M\rangle$ for bounded increments
nodes.label: lem:qv_linear_bound

nodes.statement:
Each increment satisfies $\langle M\rangle_{k+1}-\langle M\rangle_k
= \E[(\Delta M_k)^2\mid\filt_k] \le \E[c^2\mid\filt_k] = c^2$; telescoping from
$\langle M\rangle_0 = 0$ gives $\langle M\rangle_n \le c^2 n$.
nodes.name: Proof of Linear bound on $\langle M\rangle$ for bounded increments
nodes.statement_short: Bound each increment by c^2 and telescope.

nodes.statement: $M^2 - \langle M\rangle$ is an $(\filt_n)$-martingale.
nodes.name: $M^2 - \langle M\rangle$ is a martingale
nodes.label: lem:qv_mart

nodes.statement:
This is the martingale part in the Doob decomposition of $M^2$
(\texttt{martingale\_martingalePart}).
nodes.name: Proof of $M^2 - \langle M\rangle$ is a martingale
nodes.statement_short: Martingale part of the Doob decomposition.

nodes.statement:
Call a process $A$ a \emph{compensator} of $M^2$ if $M^2 - A$ is an $(\filt_n)$-martingale, $A$ is
predictable, $A_0 = 0$, and each $A_n$ is integrable. Then $\langle M\rangle$ is a compensator of
$M^2$, and any compensator $A$ of $M^2$ is indistinguishable from it:
$\P[\forall n,\ A_n = \langle M\rangle_n] = 1$. So Definition~\ref{def:pred_qv}, which is a
formula, defines the object the name describes, and does so up to the a.s.\ equality of paths that
is the best any statement about conditional expectations can offer.
nodes.name: $\langle M\rangle$ is the unique compensator
nodes.label: lem:qv_unique

nodes.statement:
Existence is Lemma~\ref{lem:qv_mart} together with the predictability of the Doob predictable part
(Lemma~\ref{lem:qv_incr}). For uniqueness, $M^2 = (M^2 - A) + A$ exhibits $M^2$ as a martingale
plus a predictable process null at $0$, and the Doob decomposition is unique up to null sets
(\texttt{predictablePart\_add\_ae\_eq}), so $A_n = \langle M\rangle_n$ a.s.\ for each fixed $n$;
the index set is countable, so the countably many exceptional sets union to a null set.
nodes.name: Proof of $\langle M\rangle$ is the unique compensator
nodes.statement_short: Existence from the Doob decomposition; uniqueness up to countably many null sets.

nodes.statement:
For a square-integrable martingale $M$ with $M_0 = 0$ and every $n$,
$\E[M_n^2] = \E[\langle M\rangle_n]$.
nodes.name: Expected quadratic variation equals second moment
assumptions: For a square-integrable martingale $M$ with $M_0 = 0$ and every $n$
nodes.label: lem:qv_second_moment

nodes.name: Proof of Expected quadratic variation equals second moment
nodes.statement_short: M^2 - <M> is a martingale started at 0.

nodes.statement:
Let $M$ be a square-integrable martingale with $M_0 = 0$. If every increment has
second moment $\E[(\Delta M_{n+1})^2] \le \sigma^2$, then $\E[M_n^2] \le \sigma^2 n$.
nodes.name: Martingale $L^2$ growth
assumptions: Let $M$ be a square-integrable martingale with $M_0 = 0$
every increment has second moment $\E[(\Delta M_{n+1})^2] \le \sigma^2$
nodes.label: lem:mart_sq_growth

nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:qv_second_moment}, $\E[M_n^2] = \E[\langle M\rangle_n]$.
Telescoping and Lemma~\ref{lem:qv_incr},
$\E[\langle M\rangle_n] = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\E[(\Delta M_{i+1})^2] \le n\sigma^2$.
nodes.name: Proof of Martingale $L^2$ growth
nodes.statement_short: Expected quadratic variation equals the second moment; telescope the increments.

nodes.statement:
Let $M, N$ be square-integrable martingales such that
$\E[\Delta M_i\, \Delta N_i \mid \filt_{i-1}] = 0$ for all $i$ (e.g.\ if
$\Delta M_i\, \Delta N_i = 0$ a.s.). Then $MN$ is a martingale, so the cross
variation vanishes, and $\langle M + N\rangle = \langle M\rangle + \langle N\rangle$.
nodes.name: Orthogonal martingales
nodes.label: lem:qv_orthogonal

nodes.statement:
$\E[\Delta(MN)_i\mid\filt_{i-1}] = M_{i-1}\E[\Delta N_i\mid\cdot]
+ N_{i-1}\E[\Delta M_i\mid\cdot] + \E[\Delta M_i\Delta N_i\mid\cdot] = 0$, so $MN$
is a martingale (\texttt{martingale\_mul}). For additivity, expand
$(M+N)^2 = M^2 + N^2 + 2MN$; the predictable part is linear and the predictable
part of the martingale $MN$ vanishes, so
$\langle M+N\rangle = \langle M\rangle + \langle N\rangle$.
nodes.name: Proof of Orthogonal martingales
nodes.statement_short: Expand the increment of MN; additivity from linearity of the predictable part.

nodes.statement:
Let $f : \R^K \to \R^d$ be $C^2$ on a convex open set $\hilb$, and suppose
$\|\mathrm{D}^2 f(z)\| \le C$ for all $z$ in a convex neighborhood of $y \in \hilb$.
Then for $x$ in that neighborhood,
\[
  \big\| f(x) - f(y) - \mathrm{D}f(y)(x - y) \big\| \le \tfrac{C}{2}\,\|x - y\|^2.
\]
nodes.name: First-order expansion with quadratic remainder
nodes.label: lem:taylor_first_order

nodes.statement:
Apply the mean-value / Taylor formula to $t \mapsto f(y + t(x-y))$ on $[0,1]$:
$f(x) - f(y) - \mathrm{D}f(y)(x-y)
= \int_0^1 (1-t)\, \mathrm{D}^2 f(y + t(x-y))[x-y, x-y]\, dt$, and bound the
integrand by $C\|x-y\|^2$.

\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.norm\_sub\_fderiv\_le\_mul\_sq} states the equivalent bound
$\|f(x)-f(y)-\mathrm{D}f(y)(x-y)\| \le K\|x-y\|^2$ under the (weaker, and here more convenient)
hypothesis that the derivative is $K$-Lipschitz relative to $y$ on a convex set,
$\|\mathrm{D}f(z)-\mathrm{D}f(y)\| \le K\|z-y\|$ --- which the second-derivative bound
$\|\mathrm{D}^2 f\|\le C$ supplies with $K = C$ by the mean value inequality. The proof applies the
mean value inequality \texttt{Convex.norm\_image\_sub\_le\_of\_norm\_hasFDerivWithin\_le'} on the
segment $[y,x]$, where $\|\mathrm{D}f(z)-\mathrm{D}f(y)\|\le K\|z-y\|\le K\|x-y\|$ gives the constant.
nodes.name: Proof of First-order expansion with quadratic remainder
nodes.statement_short: Integral form of the Taylor remainder along the segment.

nodes.statement:
Under Condition~\textbf{B}, there is a constant $C$ and a neighborhood of
$\Params$ on which
$\big\|\Target(x) - \Target(\Params) - G(x - \Params)\big\| \le C\|x - \Params\|^2$,
where $G = \nabla\Target|_\Params$. In particular, if $\hat X \to \Params$ with
$\hat X - \Params = O_p(r_n)$, then
$\Target(\hat X) - \Target(\Params) = G(\hat X - \Params) + O_p(r_n^2)$.
nodes.name: Expansion of the target function
nodes.label: lem:taylor_rho

nodes.statement:
Condition~\textbf{B} makes $\Target$ twice differentiable near $\Params$, so
Lemma~\ref{lem:taylor_first_order} applies with $y = \Params$; the second
statement follows from the order arithmetic of Lemma~\ref{lem:op_arith}.
nodes.name: Proof of Expansion of the target function
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Taylor lemma at the true parameter and the O_p arithmetic.

nodes.statement:
Let $(M_n)$ be a square-integrable martingale. For $i \ne j$,
$\E[\Delta M_i\, \Delta M_j] = 0$; consequently
$\E[M_n^2] = \sum_{i=1}^n \E[(\Delta M_i)^2]$ when $M_0 = 0$.
nodes.name: Orthogonality of martingale increments
nodes.label: lem:slln_orthogonal

nodes.statement:
For $i < j$, condition on $\filt_{j-1}$: $\E[\Delta M_i \Delta M_j]
= \E[\Delta M_i\, \E[\Delta M_j\mid\filt_{j-1}]] = 0$. Expanding
$M_n^2 = (\sum_i \Delta M_i)^2$ and using orthogonality kills the cross terms.
nodes.name: Proof of Orthogonality of martingale increments
nodes.statement_short: Condition on the later filtration to kill cross terms.

nodes.statement:
Let $(M_n)$ be a square-integrable martingale with $M_0=0$ and
$\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\E[(\Delta M_k)^2]}{k^2} < \infty$. Then
$S_n := \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{\Delta M_k}{k}$ is a square-integrable martingale with
$\sup_n \E[S_n^2] = \sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\E[(\Delta M_k)^2]}{k^2} < \infty$.
nodes.name: Weighted increment martingale is $L^2$-bounded
nodes.label: lem:slln_weighted

nodes.statement:
Each increment $\Delta S_k = \Delta M_k / k$ is $\filt_k$-measurable with
$\E[\Delta S_k\mid\filt_{k-1}] = 0$, so $S_n$ is a martingale. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:slln_orthogonal}, $\E[S_n^2] = \sum_{k\le n}\E[(\Delta M_k)^2]/k^2$,
which is bounded by the convergent series.
nodes.name: Proof of Weighted increment martingale is $L^2$-bounded
nodes.statement_short: Weighted increments are martingale differences; orthogonality gives the L2 bound.

nodes.statement: A martingale $(S_n)$ with $\sup_n \|S_n\|_{L^2} < \infty$ converges a.s.\ to a finite limit.
nodes.name: $L^2$-bounded martingales converge a.s.
conclusions: converges a.s.\ to a finite limit
nodes.label: lem:slln_l2_conv

nodes.statement:
On a probability space $\|\cdot\|_{L^1}\le\|\cdot\|_{L^2}$
(\texttt{eLpNorm\_le\_eLpNorm\_of\_exponent\_le}), so the uniform $L^2$ bound gives a uniform
$L^1$ bound, and $(S_n)$ is an $L^1$-bounded (sub)martingale. The $L^1$ martingale convergence
theorem (Mathlib's \texttt{Submartingale.exists\_ae\_tendsto\_of\_bdd}) then gives a.s.\ convergence
to a finite limit.
nodes.name: Proof of $L^2$-bounded martingales converge a.s.
nodes.statement_short: L2 bound implies L1 bound; Mathlib's martingale convergence theorem.

nodes.statement:
Let $(x_n)$ be reals such that the partial sums $\sum_{k<n} x_k$ converge (to some $s$). Then
$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k<n} k\,x_k \to 0$.
nodes.name: Kronecker's lemma, identity weights
assumptions: Let $(x_n)$ be reals such that the partial sums $\sum_{k<n} x_k$ converge (to some $s$)
nodes.label: lem:kronecker

nodes.statement:
This is the special case $b_k = k$ of Kronecker's lemma, which is the only case used below
(Theorem~\ref{thm:mart_slln}). Write $s_n = \sum_{k<n} x_k \to s$. Summation by parts
(\texttt{Finset.sum\_range\_by\_parts}) gives
$\sum_{k<n} k\,x_k = (n-1)s_n - \sum_{k<n} s_k$, so
$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k<n} k\,x_k = \big(1-\tfrac1n\big)s_n - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k<n} s_k$.
The first term tends to $s$ and the second is a Cesàro average of the convergent sequence $(s_n)$,
hence also tends to $s$ (\texttt{Filter.Tendsto.cesaro}); the difference tends to $0$.
nodes.name: Proof of Kronecker's lemma, identity weights
nodes.statement_short: Summation by parts and Cesaro averages.

nodes.statement:
Let $(b_n)$ be positive and nondecreasing with $b_n\to\infty$, and let $(y_n)$ be reals whose partial
sums $\sum_{k<n} y_k$ converge (to some $s$). Then $\dfrac1{b_n}\sum_{k<n} b_{k+1}\,y_k \to 0$.
nodes.name: Kronecker's lemma, general weights
assumptions: Let $(b_n)$ be positive and nondecreasing with $b_n\to\infty$
nodes.label: lem:kronecker_general

nodes.statement:
Summation by parts: with $S_n=\sum_{k<n}y_k$,
$\sum_{k<n} b_{k+1}y_k = b_n S_n - \sum_{k<n-1}(b_{k+2}-b_{k+1})S_{k+1}$. Dividing by $b_n$, the first
term is $S_n\to s$; the second is a Toeplitz-weighted average of the convergent sequence
$(S_{k+1})$ with nonnegative weights $(b_{k+2}-b_{k+1})/b_n$ summing to $(b_n-b_1)/b_n\to1$, each
tending to $0$. Writing $S_{k+1}=s+\varepsilon_k$ with $\varepsilon_k\to0$ and splitting the sum at a
threshold beyond which $|\varepsilon_k|<\delta$, the weighted average tends to $s$; the difference
tends to $0$.
nodes.name: Proof of Kronecker's lemma, general weights
nodes.statement_short: Summation by parts and a Toeplitz weighted-average argument.

nodes.statement:
For a square-integrable martingale $(M_n)$ with $M_0=0$, the transform
\[
  T_n := \sum_{k<n} \frac{\Delta M_k}{1+\langle M\rangle_{k+1}}
\]
is a martingale (the weights $1/(1+\langle M\rangle_{k+1})$ are $\filt_k$-measurable, as
$\langle M\rangle$ is predictable), and it is $L^2$-bounded:
$\E[T_n^2] = \sum_{k<n} \E\!\big[\tfrac{\Delta\langle M\rangle_k}{(1+\langle M\rangle_{k+1})^2}\big]
\le \E\!\big[\tfrac1{1+\langle M\rangle_0}-\tfrac1{1+\langle M\rangle_n}\big] \le 1$,
using $\E[(\Delta M_k)^2\mid\filt_k]=\Delta\langle M\rangle_k$ and the telescoping bound
$\tfrac{\Delta\langle M\rangle_k}{(1+\langle M\rangle_{k+1})^2}\le
\tfrac1{1+\langle M\rangle_k}-\tfrac1{1+\langle M\rangle_{k+1}}$.
nodes.name: Bracket-weighted transform is $L^2$-bounded
nodes.label: lem:slln_bracket_weighted

nodes.statement:
The martingale property and Itô isometry give
$\E[T_n^2]=\sum_{k<n}\E[(\Delta T_k)^2]=\sum_{k<n}\E[(\Delta M_k)^2/(1+\langle M\rangle_{k+1})^2]$;
pull the $\filt_k$-measurable weight out of the conditional expectation and use
$\E[(\Delta M_k)^2\mid\filt_k]=\Delta\langle M\rangle_k$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:qv_incr}). The telescoping
bound holds because $(1+\langle M\rangle_k)(1+\langle M\rangle_{k+1})\le(1+\langle M\rangle_{k+1})^2$.
nodes.name: Proof of Bracket-weighted transform is $L^2$-bounded
nodes.statement_short: Ito isometry and a telescoping bound on the weighted bracket increments.

nodes.statement:
Let $(M_n)$ be a square-integrable martingale with $M_0=0$. Then almost surely on
$\{\langle M\rangle_n\to\infty\}$, $\dfrac{M_n}{\langle M\rangle_n}\to0$.
nodes.name: Bracket-normalized martingale SLLN
nodes.statement_short: M_n / <M>_n -> 0 a.s. on the event that the bracket diverges.
assumptions: Let $(M_n)$ be a square-integrable martingale with $M_0=0$
nodes.label: thm:mart_slln_bracket

nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:slln_bracket_weighted} the transform $T_n$ is an $L^2$-bounded martingale, so
$T_n\to T_\infty$ a.s.\ (Lemma~\ref{lem:slln_l2_conv}). Apply the general Kronecker lemma
(Lemma~\ref{lem:kronecker_general}) pathwise with $b_k=1+\langle M\rangle_k$ (nondecreasing, and
$\to\infty$ on the event) and $y_k=\Delta M_k/(1+\langle M\rangle_{k+1})=\Delta T_k$:
$\frac1{b_n}\sum_{k<n} b_{k+1}\,y_k=\frac{M_n}{1+\langle M\rangle_n}\to0$, hence
$M_n/\langle M\rangle_n\to0$.
nodes.name: Proof of Bracket-normalized martingale SLLN
nodes.statement_short: L2-bounded transform converges; general Kronecker lemma with weights 1 + <M>.

nodes.statement:
Let $(M_n)$ be a square-integrable martingale with $M_0 = 0$ and
$\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{\E[(\Delta M_k)^2]}{k^2} < \infty$. Then $\frac{M_n}{n}\to 0$
a.s.
nodes.name: Martingale SLLN
nodes.statement_short: Martingale SLLN M_n/n -> 0 under summable normalized increment variances.
assumptions: Let $(M_n)$ be a square-integrable martingale with $M_0 = 0$
nodes.label: thm:mart_slln

nodes.statement:
By Lemmas~\ref{lem:slln_weighted} and \ref{lem:slln_l2_conv}, the series
$S_n = \sum_{k\le n}\Delta M_k/k$ converges a.s. Apply Kronecker's lemma
(Lemma~\ref{lem:kronecker}) pathwise with $b_k = k$ and $x_k = \Delta M_k/k$:
$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k\le n} k\cdot\frac{\Delta M_k}{k} = \frac{M_n}{n}\to 0$ a.s.
nodes.name: Proof of Martingale SLLN
nodes.statement_short: Kolmogorov route: the weighted series converges a.s., then Kronecker's lemma.

nodes.statement:
If $(M_n)$ is a martingale with $M_0=0$ and uniformly bounded increments
$|\Delta M_k| \le c$, then $\frac{M_n}{n}\to 0$ a.s.
nodes.name: Bounded increments
assumptions: $(M_n)$ is a martingale with $M_0=0$ and uniformly bounded increments $|\Delta M_k| \le c$
nodes.label: cor:mart_slln_bounded

nodes.statement:
$\E[(\Delta M_k)^2]\le c^2$, so $\sum_k \E[(\Delta M_k)^2]/k^2 \le c^2\sum_k k^{-2}
< \infty$; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:mart_slln}.
nodes.name: Proof of Bounded increments
nodes.statement_short: Bounded increments give a summable variance series.

nodes.statement:
Let $(M_n)$ be a martingale with $M_0=0$ and increments bounded by
$|\Delta M_i| \le c$. For $|\theta| \le 1/c$, the process
\[
  Z_n(\theta) := \exp\!\Big(\theta M_n - \theta^2 \langle M\rangle_n\Big)
\]
is a supermartingale, where $\langle M\rangle$ is the predictable quadratic
variation (Definition~\ref{def:pred_qv}).
nodes.name: Exponential supermartingale
nodes.label: lem:lil_exp_supermart

nodes.statement:
Using $e^x \le 1 + x + x^2$ for $|x| \le 1$ and $\E[\Delta M_i\mid\filt_{i-1}]=0$,
\[
  \E[e^{\theta\Delta M_i}\mid\filt_{i-1}]
  \le 1 + \theta^2\E[(\Delta M_i)^2\mid\filt_{i-1}]
  \le \exp\!\big(\theta^2(\langle M\rangle_i - \langle M\rangle_{i-1})\big).
\]
Hence $\E[Z_i(\theta)\mid\filt_{i-1}] \le Z_{i-1}(\theta)$.
nodes.name: Proof of Exponential supermartingale
nodes.statement_short: Elementary bound e^x <= 1 + x + x^2 and zero conditional mean.

nodes.statement:
Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_exp_supermart}, for all $\lambda > 0$
and $v > 0$,
\[
  \Prob\!\Big(\exists n:\ M_n \ge \lambda \ \text{and}\ \langle M\rangle_n \le v\Big)
  \le \exp\!\Big(-\frac{\lambda^2}{2(v + c\lambda)}\Big).
\]
The formalized statement \texttt{AlphaRAR.measure\_exists\_ge\_le\_exp} is the pre-optimization,
finite-horizon form: for each $n$ and each admissible $0<\theta\le 1/c$,
$\Prob(\exists k\le n:\ M_k\ge\lambda,\ \langle M\rangle_k\le v)\le \exp(-\theta\lambda+\theta^2 v)$,
obtained from Ville's maximal inequality
(\texttt{AlphaRAR.smul\_measure\_sup\_le\_integral\_zero}) applied to the exponential
supermartingale. Optimizing over $\theta$ and letting $n\to\infty$ recovers the displayed bound.
nodes.name: Freedman-type inequality
nodes.label: lem:lil_freedman

nodes.statement:
Optional stopping applied to the supermartingale $Z_n(\theta)$ at the first time
$M_n\ge\lambda$ with $\langle M\rangle_n\le v$ gives
$\Prob(\cdots)\le \exp(-\theta\lambda + \theta^2 v)$; optimize over
$0<\theta\le 1/c$. Equivalently, this is the Azuma--Hoeffding/Freedman bound that
follows from the conditionally sub-Gaussian MGF machinery of
\texttt{Probability/Moments/SubGaussian.lean}.
nodes.name: Proof of Freedman-type inequality
nodes.statement_short: Optional stopping of the exponential supermartingale and optimization over theta.

nodes.statement:
Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_freedman}, for $\lambda, v > 0$ with the
admissibility condition $\lambda c \le 2v$ (so that the optimizer $\theta=\lambda/(2v)$
satisfies $\theta c\le 1$),
\[
  \Prob\!\Big(\exists n:\ M_n \ge \lambda \ \text{and}\ \langle M\rangle_n \le v\Big)
  \le \exp\!\Big(-\frac{\lambda^2}{4v}\Big).
\]
The variance proxy $2v$ (rather than the sharp $v$) comes from the one-step bound
$e^x\le 1+x+x^2$, costing a factor $\sqrt2$ in the eventual constant.
nodes.name: Optimized Freedman bound
nodes.label: cor:lil_freedman_opt

nodes.statement:
Evaluate Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_freedman} at $\theta=\lambda/(2v)$, giving exponent
$-\theta\lambda+\theta^2 v = -\lambda^2/(4v)$. The finite-horizon events increase to the
event over all $n$, so their measures pass to the limit
(\texttt{measure\_exists\_ge\_le\_exp\_all}).
nodes.name: Proof of Optimized Freedman bound
nodes.statement_short: Evaluate at the optimizer and pass to the infinite-horizon limit.

nodes.statement:
Fix threshold schedules $(v_k)_{k}$, $(\lambda_k)_k$ with $v_k,\lambda_k>0$ and
$\lambda_k c\le 2v_k$, such that $\sum_k \exp(-\lambda_k^2/(4v_k))<\infty$. Then almost
surely only finitely many blocks are ``bad'': for a.e.\ $\omega$, for all large $k$ and
every $n$, $\langle M\rangle_n\le v_k \Rightarrow M_n < \lambda_k$.
nodes.name: Borel--Cantelli over blocks
nodes.label: lem:lil_bc

nodes.statement:
By Corollary~\ref{cor:lil_freedman_opt}, $\Prob(s_k)\le\exp(-\lambda_k^2/(4v_k))$ where
$s_k=\{\exists n:\ M_n\ge\lambda_k,\ \langle M\rangle_n\le v_k\}$. The right-hand sides are
summable, so $\sum_k\Prob(s_k)<\infty$, and the first Borel--Cantelli lemma gives that a.e.\
$\omega$ lies in only finitely many $s_k$.
nodes.name: Proof of Borel--Cantelli over blocks
nodes.statement_short: Optimized Freedman bound per block and the first Borel-Cantelli lemma.

nodes.statement:
Let $(M_n)$ be a martingale with $M_0=0$ and $|\Delta M_i|\le c$, and suppose
$\langle M\rangle_n \to \infty$ a.s. Then
\[
  \limsup_{n\to\infty}
  \frac{M_n}{\sqrt{2\langle M\rangle_n \log\log\langle M\rangle_n}} \le 1
  \quad\text{a.s.},
\]
and in particular $M_n = O\!\big(\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n \log\log\langle M\rangle_n}\big)$
a.s.
nodes.name: One-sided LIL, bounded increments
assumptions: Let $(M_n)$ be a martingale with $M_0=0$ and $|\Delta M_i|\le c$
nodes.label: thm:lil_bounded

nodes.statement:
Fix $\eta>1$ and set $v_k = \eta^k$. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_bc} with
$\lambda_k=(1+\varepsilon)\sqrt{2v_k\log\log v_k}$: the tail bounds
$\exp(-\lambda_k^2/(4v_k))$ are summable in $k$, so a.s.\ only finitely many blocks are
bad. On the block $\{\langle M\rangle_n\in(v_{k-1},v_k]\}$ this yields
$M_n < \lambda_k \le C\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\log\log\langle M\rangle_n}$; letting
$\eta\downarrow1$ and $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ yields the $\limsup$ bound.

\textbf{Formalization status.} The formalized statement
\texttt{AlphaRAR.ae\_eventually\_forall\_lt\_dyadic} is the dyadic-block form: with the schedule
$v_k=2^k$ and $\lambda_k = K\sqrt{v_k(k+1)}$ (where $0<K$ and $Kc\le2$, so admissibility
$\lambda_k c\le 2v_k$ holds for \emph{every} $k$ via $k+1\le 2^k$, and the tail bounds
$\exp(-\lambda_k^2/(4v_k))=\exp(-K^2(k+1)/4)$ form a geometric series), almost surely for all
large $k$ and every $n$, $\langle M\rangle_n\le 2^k \Rightarrow M_n < K\sqrt{2^k(k+1)}$. This is
the complete probabilistic content, built from Ville's inequality, the optimized Freedman bound
(Corollary~\ref{cor:lil_freedman_opt}), and Borel--Cantelli (Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_bc}). Since on the
block $\langle M\rangle_n\in(2^{k-1},2^k]$ one has $\sqrt{2^k(k+1)}\asymp
\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\log\langle M\rangle_n}$, it gives the displayed
$O(\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\log\langle M\rangle_n})$ upper bound, formalized in
Corollary~\ref{cor:lil_upper} below. One deliberate deviation from the displayed statement remains
unformalized: the $\log\log$ (rather than $\log$) rate with sharp constant $1$, which would require
refining the one-step MGF bound $e^x\le1+x+x^2$ to variance proxy $1$ (valid only as the increment
$\to0$). The $\log$ rate already gives $M_n=o(\langle M\rangle_n)$, which suffices for all
downstream uses.
nodes.name: Proof of One-sided LIL, bounded increments
nodes.statement_short: Geometric blocking, Freedman bounds and Borel-Cantelli; then let the block ratio tend to one.

nodes.statement:
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:lil_bounded} (in particular $\langle M\rangle_n\to\infty$
a.s.), there is a deterministic constant $C$ (depending only on $c$) such that almost surely
\[
  M_n \le C\,\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\,\log\langle M\rangle_n}\qquad\text{for all large }n.
\]
This is the consumable $O(\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\log\langle M\rangle_n})$ a.s.\ upper bound used
downstream (Lemma~\ref{lem:U_increment_bound}, via the bounded assignment martingale).
nodes.name: Normalized one-sided upper bound
nodes.label: cor:lil_upper

nodes.statement:
Repackage Theorem~\ref{thm:lil_bounded}: for large $n$ let $k$ be the least index with
$\langle M\rangle_n\le 2^k$. Minimality gives $2^k\le 2\langle M\rangle_n$ and
$k\le\log_2\langle M\rangle_n+1$, so
$K\sqrt{2^k(k+1)}\le C\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\log\langle M\rangle_n}$ with
$C=K\sqrt{2(1/\log 2+2)}$, using $\log\langle M\rangle_n\ge1$ eventually.
nodes.name: Proof of Normalized one-sided upper bound
nodes.statement_short: Repackage the dyadic-block statement via the least block containing <M>_n.

nodes.statement:
Under the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{cor:lil_upper}, almost surely
$M_n \le C\sqrt{n\log n}$ for all large $n$, for a deterministic constant $C$. This is the form
$M_n = O(\sqrt{n\log n})$ a.s.\ used for the bounded assignment martingale
$M_{\cdot,k}$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:U_increment_bound}.
nodes.name: Upper bound at scale $\sqrt{n\log n}$
nodes.label: cor:lil_upper_nat

nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:qv_linear_bound}, $\langle M\rangle_n\le c^2 n$, hence
$\log\langle M\rangle_n\le\log(c^2 n)\le 2\log n$ once $n\ge c^2$. Substituting into
Corollary~\ref{cor:lil_upper} bounds $\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\log\langle M\rangle_n}
\le\sqrt{2c^2}\,\sqrt{n\log n}$.
nodes.name: Proof of Upper bound at scale $\sqrt{n\log n}$
nodes.statement_short: Linear bound on the quadratic variation substituted into the normalized bound.

nodes.statement:
The remaining case is a martingale $M_n = \sum_{i<n}\xi_i D_i$ whose increments are
\emph{not} bounded: $\xi_i$ are i.i.d.\ centered with only $\E[\xi_0^2]=\sigma^2<\infty$,
and $D_i\in\{0,1\}$ is predictable (each $\xi_i$ is independent of the past $\filt_{i-1}$,
while $D_i$ is $\filt_{i-1}$-measurable).
nodes.name: Finite-variance sampled martingale
nodes.statement_short: Martingale of i.i.d. centred finite-variance responses selected by a predictable 0/1 indicator.

nodes.statement:
Then $\langle M\rangle_n=\sigma^2 N_n$ with
$N_n:=\sum_{i<n}D_i$.
nodes.name: Quadratic variation of the sampled martingale

nodes.statement:
Theorem~\ref{thm:lil_bounded} does not apply directly, so we
truncate at level $b_i:=\sqrt{i}$ --- the largest level for which the tail is still
summable under only a second moment --- and control three pieces separately.
nodes.name: Truncation level b_i

nodes.statement:
With $b_i:=\sqrt i$, set
$\xi_i^{\mathrm t}:=\xi_i\indic_{\{|\xi_i|\le b_i\}}$,
$\xi_i^{\mathrm r}:=\xi_i\indic_{\{|\xi_i|> b_i\}}$,
$m_i:=\E[\xi_i^{\mathrm t}]$, $\tilde\xi_i:=\xi_i^{\mathrm t}-m_i$, and
\[
  \tilde M_n:=\sum_{i<n}\tilde\xi_i D_i,\quad
  R_n:=\sum_{i<n}\xi_i^{\mathrm r} D_i,\quad
  \mathrm{Dr}_n:=\sum_{i<n} m_i D_i,\quad
  N_n:=\sum_{i<n} D_i,
\]
so that $M_n=\tilde M_n+R_n+\mathrm{Dr}_n$.
nodes.name: Truncated decomposition
nodes.statement_short: Split the martingale into centred truncated part, tail part and drift at level sqrt(i).
nodes.label: def:lil_trunc

nodes.statement:
$\sum_{i}\Prob(|\xi_i|>\sqrt i)<\infty$. (The formalized statement
\texttt{tsum\_measure\_abs\_sub\_gt\_sqrt\_ne\_top} is the law-level version: for any finite measure
$\rho$ on $\R$ with $\int(x-\theta)^2\,d\rho<\infty$, $\sum_i\rho(|x-\theta|>\sqrt i)<\infty$; apply
it to the reward law $\rho=\nu_k$, $\theta=\theta_k$. This rests on a general-measure layer-cake
bound \texttt{tsum\_measure\_Ioi\_ne\_top}, the $\mu$-general form of Mathlib's
\texttt{tsum\_prob\_mem\_Ioi\_lt\_top}.)
nodes.name: Summable tail probabilities
nodes.label: lem:trunc_tail_summable

nodes.statement:
Since $|\xi_i|>\sqrt i \iff (x-\theta_k)^2>i$, the sum equals $\sum_i\nu_k((\cdot-\theta_k)^2>i)$,
which is finite by the layer-cake bound $\sum_i\mu\{X>i\}\le\int X\,d\mu+\mu(\text{univ})$ applied to
$X=(\cdot-\theta_k)^2$ (integrable, being the arm-$k$ second central moment $\sigma^2$).
nodes.name: Proof of Summable tail probabilities
nodes.statement_short: Layer-cake bound on the second moment.

nodes.statement:
Almost surely $|\xi_i|\le b_i$ for all large $i$; consequently $\xi_i^{\mathrm r}=0$ eventually and
$R_n$ is a.s.\ eventually constant, so $R_n=O(1)$ a.s.

The formalization has two layers. The abstract eventually-bounded clause
\texttt{ae\_eventually\_abs\_le\_of\_tsum\_ne\_top} is stated for a general level sequence $b$ and
takes $\sum_i\Prob(|\xi_i|>b_i)<\infty$ as hypothesis. The sampled version
\texttt{ae\_eventually\_tailRespPart\_const} concludes that the tail remainder
$R_n=Q_n-\tilde M_n-\mathrm{Dr}_n$ (\texttt{tailRespPart}) is a.s.\ eventually constant, via a
\emph{conditional bookkeeping} step: the sampled tail event has
$\Prob(A_i=k,\ \sqrt i\le|Y_i-\theta_k|)\le\nu_k(\sqrt i\le|\cdot-\theta_k|)$
(\texttt{measure\_action\_and\_tail\_le}, by conditioning on $\filtAction_i$ and
\texttt{condExp\_feedback\_comp}), so these probabilities are summable
(\texttt{tsum\_measure\_action\_and\_tail\_ne\_top}, using the closed-window law-level bound
\texttt{tsum\_measure\_abs\_sub\_ge\_sqrt\_ne\_top}).
nodes.name: Tail is eventually zero
nodes.label: lem:trunc_tail_const

nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:trunc_tail_summable} (in the sampled form above) the summability hypothesis holds,
and the first Borel--Cantelli lemma (\texttt{ae\_eventually\_notMem}) gives a.s.\ that for all large
$i$ arm $k$ is not sampled with an off-window response, whence $\xi_i^{\mathrm r}=0$ and the
increments of $R_n$ (\texttt{tailRespPart\_succ\_sub}, where the truncated mean cancels) vanish for
large $i$; a sequence with eventually-vanishing increments is eventually constant.
nodes.name: Proof of Tail is eventually zero
nodes.statement_short: Borel-Cantelli: eventually no sampled off-window response.

nodes.statement:
$|m_i|\le \sigma^2/\sqrt i$ for $i\ge1$. (The formalized statement
\texttt{abs\_integral\_truncation\_le} is the abstract single-variable bound: for a centred $X$
with $X^2$ integrable, $|\E[\operatorname{trunc}(X,A)]|\le \E[X^2]/A$; apply it to $X=\xi_0$ and
$A=\sqrt i$.)
nodes.name: Truncated-mean bound
nodes.label: lem:trunc_mean_bound

nodes.statement:
Since $\E[\xi_0]=0$, $m_i=\E[\operatorname{trunc}(\xi_0,\sqrt i)]
=\E[\operatorname{trunc}(\xi_0,\sqrt i)-\xi_0]$, so by the pointwise bound
$|\operatorname{trunc}(\xi_0,A)-\xi_0|\le\xi_0^2/A$ (the truncation is either $\xi_0$ or, off the
window where $|\xi_0|\ge A$, is $0$ with $|\xi_0|\le\xi_0^2/A$),
$|m_i|\le\E[\xi_0^2]/\sqrt i=\sigma^2/\sqrt i$.
nodes.name: Proof of Truncated-mean bound
nodes.statement_short: Centredness and the pointwise truncation bound.

nodes.statement:
$|\mathrm{Dr}_n|\le 2\sigma^2\sqrt{n}$ (everywhere, with $\sigma^2=V_k$). In particular
$\mathrm{Dr}_n=O(\sqrt n)=o(\sqrt{N_n\log N_n})$ a.s.\ whenever $N_n$ grows linearly (the case of
interest). The sharper bound $|\mathrm{Dr}_n|\le 2\sigma^2\sqrt{N_n}$ holds by reindexing to the
sampled subsequence $i_j\ge j$, but is not needed and not formalized.
nodes.name: Drift is $O(\sqrt{n})$
nodes.label: lem:trunc_drift

nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:trunc_mean_bound}, $|m_i|\le\sigma^2/\sqrt i$ (and $m_0=0$), so
$|\mathrm{Dr}_n|\le\sum_{i<n}|m_i|D_i\le\sum_{i<n}|m_i|\le\sigma^2\sum_{i<n}\tfrac1{\sqrt i}
\le 2\sigma^2\sqrt n$, using $\sum_{i<n}1/\sqrt i\le 2\sqrt n$
(\texttt{sum\_one\_div\_sqrt\_le}).
nodes.name: Proof of Drift is $O(\sqrt{n})$
nodes.statement_short: Sum the truncated-mean bounds.

nodes.statement:
$\tilde M$ is a martingale with $\tilde M_0=0$: $\E[\tilde\xi_i D_i\mid\filt_{i-1}]
=D_i\,\E[\tilde\xi_i\mid\filt_{i-1}]=D_i(\E[\xi_i^{\mathrm t}]-m_i)=0$, using that $\xi_i$ is
independent of $\filt_{i-1}$ and $D_i$ is $\filt_{i-1}$-measurable.
(Formalized in the \texttt{IsAlgEnvSeq}/\texttt{stationaryEnv} framework: $\tilde M$ is the
\emph{truncated response martingale} $\tilde Q_{n,k}=\sum_{i<n}\indic_{\{A_i=k\}}
(\operatorname{trunc}(Y_i-\theta_k,\sqrt i)-m_i)$, a martingale for the action-augmented
filtration $\filtAction$. It is an instance of a general functional response martingale
\texttt{genRespMart} --- of which the response martingale $Q$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:Q_martingale}) is the
$g=\mathrm{id}$ case --- whose martingale property follows from \texttt{condExp\_feedback\_comp}.)
nodes.name: $\tilde M$ is a martingale
nodes.label: lem:trunc_mart

nodes.statement:
Pull out the $\filtAction_i$-measurable indicator $\indic_{\{A_i=k\}}$; the conditional
expectation of $g(Y_i)$ (with $g=\operatorname{trunc}(\cdot-\theta_k,\sqrt i)$) given
$\filtAction_i$ is $(\nu(A_i))[g]=m_i$ on $\{A_i=k\}$ (\texttt{condExp\_feedback\_comp}), so the
centred increment has conditional mean $m_i-m_i=0$.
nodes.name: Proof of $\tilde M$ is a martingale
nodes.statement_short: Pull out the indicator and use the conditional law of the response.

nodes.statement:
$\langle\tilde M\rangle_n=\sum_{i<n}v_i D_i$, where $D_i=\indic_{\{A_i=k\}}$ and
$v_i:=\int(\operatorname{trunc}(x-\theta_k,\sqrt i)-m_i)^2\,d\nu_k$ is the truncated-response
variance of arm $k$.
nodes.name: Quadratic variation of $\tilde M$
nodes.label: lem:trunc_qv

nodes.statement:
Instance of the general functional quadratic variation
\texttt{predQuadVar\_genRespMart\_eq}: the compensator increment is the $\filtAction_i$-conditional
second moment $\E[(\tilde\xi_i D_i)^2\mid\filtAction_i]=v_i D_i$
