lemmas \texttt{TendstoInDistribution.mul\_of\_tendstoInMeasure\_const},
\texttt{TendstoInDistribution.add\_of\_tendstoInMeasure\_const}.
nodes.name: Proof of Per-arm estimator CLT, sparse
nodes.statement_short: Bahadur identity and Slutsky applied to the sparse self-normalized CLT.

nodes.statement:
For an integer $r\ge1$, the \emph{chi-square distribution with $r$ degrees of
freedom} $\chi^2_r$ is the Gamma distribution with shape $r/2$ and rate $1/2$.
nodes.name: Chi-square distribution
nodes.definiendum: chi-square distribution with $r$ degrees of freedom
nodes.label: def:chiSquared

nodes.statement: If $Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ then $Z^2\sim\chi^2_1$.
nodes.name: Square of a standard Gaussian
nodes.label: lem:sq_gaussian_chisq1

nodes.statement:
Compute the law of $Z^2$ by the change of variables $x = z^2$ on the standard
Gaussian density; the resulting density $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi x}}e^{-x/2}$ on
$(0,\infty)$ is the $\mathrm{Gamma}(1/2,1/2)$ density, i.e.\ $\chi^2_1$.
nodes.name: Proof of Square of a standard Gaussian
nodes.statement_short: Change of variables on the Gaussian density.

nodes.statement:
If $U\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(a,\lambda)$ and $V\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(b,\lambda)$ are
independent, then $U+V\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(a+b,\lambda)$.
nodes.name: Additivity of Gamma laws
nodes.label: lem:gamma_add

nodes.statement:
The characteristic function of $\mathrm{Gamma}(a,\lambda)$ is
$(1 - it/\lambda)^{-a}$; by independence the characteristic function of $U+V$ is
the product $(1-it/\lambda)^{-(a+b)}$, which identifies the law by injectivity of
characteristic functions.
nodes.name: Proof of Additivity of Gamma laws
nodes.statement_short: Characteristic functions multiply under independence.

nodes.statement:
If $Z_1,\dots,Z_r\sim\mathcal{N}(0,1)$ are independent, then
$\sum_{i=1}^r Z_i^2\sim\chi^2_r$.
nodes.name: Chi-square as a sum of squares
nodes.label: lem:sum_sq_chisq

nodes.statement:
Each $Z_i^2\sim\chi^2_1=\mathrm{Gamma}(1/2,1/2)$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:sq_gaussian_chisq1}, and by independence and
Lemma~\ref{lem:gamma_add} the sum is $\mathrm{Gamma}(r/2,1/2)=\chi^2_r$.
nodes.name: Proof of Chi-square as a sum of squares
nodes.statement_short: Each square is chi-square(1); additivity of Gamma laws.

nodes.statement:
If $Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_K)$ and $O$ is an orthogonal $K\times K$ matrix, then
$OZ\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_K)$.
nodes.name: Rotation invariance of the standard Gaussian
assumptions: $Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_K)$ and $O$ is an orthogonal $K\times K$ matrix
nodes.label: lem:gaussian_rotation

nodes.name: Proof of Rotation invariance of the standard Gaussian
nodes.statement_short: Gaussian with covariance O O^T = I.

nodes.statement:
An orthogonal projection matrix $P$ of rank $r$ can be written
$P = O^\top \mathrm{diag}(I_r, 0)\, O$ for some orthogonal matrix $O$.
nodes.name: Diagonalization of an orthogonal projection
nodes.label: lem:proj_diag

nodes.statement:
$P$ is symmetric and idempotent, hence diagonalizable in an orthonormal
eigenbasis with eigenvalues in $\{0,1\}$, exactly $r$ of which are $1$. This is
the spectral theorem for symmetric matrices, available in Mathlib.
nodes.name: Proof of Diagonalization of an orthogonal projection
nodes.statement_short: Spectral theorem for symmetric idempotent matrices.

nodes.statement:
Let $Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_K)$ and let $P$ be an orthogonal projection of rank $r$.
Then $Z^\top P Z\sim\chi^2_r$.
nodes.name: Gaussian quadratic form under a projection
assumptions: Let $Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_K)$ and let $P$ be an orthogonal projection of rank $r$
nodes.label: thm:cochran

nodes.statement:
Write $P = O^\top\mathrm{diag}(I_r,0)O$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:proj_diag}) and set
$W = OZ$, which is $\mathcal{N}(0,I_K)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian_rotation}.
Then $Z^\top P Z = W^\top\mathrm{diag}(I_r,0)W = \sum_{i=1}^r W_i^2$, which is
$\chi^2_r$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:sum_sq_chisq}.
nodes.name: Proof of Gaussian quadratic form under a projection
nodes.statement_short: Diagonalize the projection, rotate the Gaussian, sum r squares.

nodes.statement:
\textbf{Application.} In Lemma~\ref{lem:pearson}, $P = I - ss^\top$ is an
orthogonal projection of rank $K-1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}), and the limiting
statistic is $Z^\top P Z$ with $Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_K)$; Theorem~\ref{thm:cochran}
then gives the $\chi^2_{K-1}$ limit.
nodes.name: Cochran's theorem calibrates the Pearson test
Simplex membership and zero deficit give the throttle
nodes.statement:
Membership in $\simplex_K$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:distance_simplex}. For the throttle:
if $N_{m,k}/m > \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$ then $\delta_{m,k} = 0$, so
$p_{m+1,k} = \alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k} \le \alpha \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Simplex membership and zero deficit give the throttle

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes on the normaliser's positivity
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} The design is \texttt{AlphaRAR.distanceProb} (a probability-vector function of
the history) and the algorithm \texttt{AlphaRAR.distanceAlgorithm}; \texttt{AlphaRAR.distanceProb\_
throttle} is the throttle inequality. The only subtlety is that the mixing normaliser $\sum_i
\delta_{m,i}$ is positive whenever some arm is over-sampled: the signed deficits
$N_{m,i}/m - \hat\rho_{m,i}$ sum to $0$ (\texttt{sum\_histProp}, \texttt{sum\_histTarget}), so an
over-sampled arm forces an under-sampled one, giving $\delta_{m,j}>0$ for some $j$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes on the normaliser's positivity

nodes.name: Simplex membership and the throttle by definition
nodes.statement:
Membership in $\simplex_K$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:erade2025_simplex}. For the throttle:
if $N_{m,k}/m > \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$ then $p_{m+1,k} = \alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Simplex membership and the throttle by definition

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.eradeProb}/\texttt{eradeAlgorithm} and
\texttt{AlphaRAR.eradeProb\_throttle}. The simplex identity uses that the mass freed from the
over-sampled arms, $\sum_{j\in S}(1-\alpha)\hat\rho_{m,j}$, is redistributed exactly over the $|T|$
under-sampled arms; the degenerate case $|T|=0$ forces $S=\varnothing$ by mass conservation
(\texttt{sum\_histProp\_le}, \texttt{sum\_histTarget}) --- the proportions never total more than
$1$, which also covers the empty history, where every count is $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes

nodes.name: Lean declarations
nodes.statement:
\texttt{AlphaRAR.eradeProb}/\texttt{eradeAlgorithm} and
\texttt{AlphaRAR.eradeProb\_throttle}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean declarations

nodes.name: Redistribution and degenerate case
nodes.statement:
The simplex identity uses that the mass freed from the
over-sampled arms, $\sum_{j\in S}(1-\alpha)\hat\rho_{m,j}$, is redistributed exactly over the $|T|$
under-sampled arms; the degenerate case $|T|=0$ forces $S=\varnothing$ by mass conservation
(\texttt{sum\_histProp\_le}, \texttt{sum\_histTarget}) --- the proportions never total more than
$1$, which also covers the empty history, where every count is $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Redistribution and degenerate case

nodes.name: Deficit sign argument via counts summing to time
nodes.statement:
Membership in $\simplex_K$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:d_tracking_simplex}.
If $N_{m,k}/m > \hat{\rho}_{m,k}$ then $m\hat{\rho}_{m,k} - N_{m,k} < 0$. Since
$\sum_a (m\hat{\rho}_{m,a} - N_{m,a}) = 0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:counts_sum}, the
maximizing deficit is $\ge 0$, so $k \ne k^\star$ and
$p_{m+1,k} = \alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Deficit sign argument via counts summing to time

nodes.name: Lean formalization of the argmax arm
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} The favoured arm $k^\star=\arg\max_a(m\hat\rho_{m,a}-N_{m,a})$ is
\texttt{argmax} of \texttt{AlphaRAR.dtDeficit} (LeanMachineLearning's measurable finite-tuple
\texttt{argmax}, so the policy kernel is measurable without needing an order on the arms); the
throttle is \texttt{AlphaRAR.dTrackingProb\_throttle}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization of the argmax arm

nodes.name: Introduce the increment and the action-augmented filtration
nodes.statement:
Write $\Delta Q_{n,k} = X_{n,k}(\xi_{n,k} - \theta_k)$, where $X_{n,k}$ is the
indicator that the assignment $A_n$ equals arm $k$. The natural filtration is the
\emph{action-augmented} one $\mathcal{G}_n = \filt_{n-1}\vee\sigma(A_n)$
(\texttt{filtrationAction}): the assignment $X_{n,k}$ is $\mathcal{G}_n$-measurable
(the arm is known) while the response $\xi_{n,k}$ is not (it is revealed afterwards).
nodes.statement_short: Introduce the increment and the action-augmented filtration

nodes.name: Response conditional mean is theta_k, so the increment is centred
nodes.statement:
Conditioning on $\mathcal{G}_n$, the response is drawn from the arm's reward kernel
independently of the past given the arm, so its conditional mean is $\theta_k$;
pulling out the $\mathcal{G}_n$-measurable factor $X_{n,k}$ gives
$\E[\Delta Q_{n,k}\mid\mathcal{G}_n] = X_{n,k}(\theta_k-\theta_k)=0$, so $Q_{\cdot,k}$ is
a $\mathcal{G}$-martingale.
nodes.statement_short: Response conditional mean is theta_k, so the increment is centred

nodes.name: Tower property gives the F-martingale statement
nodes.statement:
Since $Q_{n,k}$ is $\filt_{n-1}\subseteq\mathcal{G}_n$-measurable,
the tower property also gives $\E[\Delta Q_{n,k}\mid\filt_{n-1}] = 0$, the paper's
$\filt$-martingale statement.
nodes.statement_short: Tower property gives the F-martingale statement

nodes.name: Lean framework for the algorithm-environment setting
nodes.statement:
This is formalized in the \texttt{LeanMachineLearning} algorithm--environment
framework: the arm is the action and the response is the feedback of a stationary
environment with per-arm reward kernel $\nu$, and $\theta_k = \int x\,\nu_k(dx)$ is
the kernel mean. The conditional-mean computation is \texttt{condExp\_feedback}
(which handles the first patient and the general step via the two conditional-distribution
fields of the framework), and the filtration $\mathcal{G}$ is \texttt{filtrationAction}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean framework for the algorithm-environment setting

nodes.name: Square of the increment equals indicator times squared deviation
nodes.statement:
Since $X_{n,k}$ is a $\{0,1\}$-indicator, $X_{n,k}^2 = X_{n,k}$ and hence
$(\Delta Q_{n,k})^2 = X_{n,k}(\xi_{n,k}-\theta_k)^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Square of the increment equals indicator times squared deviation

nodes.name: Pull out the indicator and compute the conditional moment
nodes.statement:
The factor $X_{n,k}$ is
$\mathcal{G}_n$-measurable, so it pulls out of the conditional expectation; by the same
conditional-distribution computation as in Lemma~\ref{lem:Q_martingale} --- now applied to
$g(x) = (x-\theta_k)^2$ (\texttt{condExp\_feedback\_comp}) --- the response's conditional
second central moment given $\mathcal{G}_n$ is $\int (x-\theta_k)^2\,\nu_{A_n}(dx)$.
nodes.statement_short: Pull out the indicator and compute the conditional moment

nodes.name: Both cases give X times V_k
nodes.statement:
On the
event $\{A_n = k\}$ this integral equals $V_k$, while off it $X_{n,k}=0$; in either case
the product is $X_{n,k} V_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Both cases give X times V_k

nodes.name: Compensator increments are V_k X; summing gives V_k N
nodes.statement:
Since $Q_{\cdot,k}$ is a martingale for the action-augmented filtration
$\mathcal{G} = \texttt{filtrationAction}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:Q_martingale}), the paper's
$V_k N_{n,k}$ is the \emph{ordinary} predictable quadratic variation of $Q_{\cdot,k}$ for
$\mathcal{G}$ (Definition~\ref{def:pred_qv}): its increment is
$\E[(\Delta Q_{m+1,k})^2\mid\mathcal{G}_m] = V_k X_{m,k}$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:Q_cond_second_moment}), and summing over $m<n$ gives
$V_k\sum_{m<n} X_{m,k} = V_k N_{n,k}$ --- the indicator survives the sum because the current
arm $A_m$ is $\mathcal{G}_m$-measurable.
nodes.statement_short: Compensator increments are V_k X; summing gives V_k N

nodes.name: Martingale property of Q^2 - <Q> from the general lemma
nodes.statement:
That $Q^2-\langle Q\rangle$ is a martingale (for
$\mathcal{G}$) is Lemma~\ref{lem:qv_mart}. The sole hypothesis is finite arm variance
(Condition~\textbf{A}), formalized as $\xi_{\cdot,k}\in L^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Martingale property of Q^2 - <Q> from the general lemma

nodes.name: Shifted martingale, Doob's inequality, orthogonality and tail integration
nodes.statement:
Fix $n$ and set $S_k := M_{n-L+k} - M_{n-L}$ for $0 \le k \le L$, a martingale for
the shifted filtration $\mathcal{G}_k := \filt_{n-L+k}$. First,
$\max_{1\le m\le L}|M_n - M_{n-m}| \le 2\max_{1\le k\le L}|S_k|$ by the triangle
inequality. Since $\{S_k^2\}$ is a submartingale, Doob's maximal inequality gives
$\Prob(\max_k |S_k| \ge x) \le \E[S_L^2]/x^2$. Orthogonality of martingale
increments yields $\E[S_L^2] = \sum_{k=1}^L \E|\Delta M_{n-L+k}|^2 \le L C_0$.
Combining, $\Prob(\max_m |M_n - M_{n-m}| \ge x) \le 4 L C_0 / x^2$, and integrating
the tail,
$\E[\max_m |M_n-M_{n-m}|] \le \int_0^{2\sqrt{LC_0}} 1\,dx
 + 4\int_{2\sqrt{LC_0}}^\infty \frac{LC_0}{x^2}\,dx = 4\sqrt{LC_0}$.
nodes.statement_short: Shifted martingale, Doob's inequality, orthogonality and tail integration

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal} states the equivalent $\int^-$ (lintegral)
bound $\int^- \max_{m\le L}|M_n - M_{n-m}| \le 4\sqrt{C_0 L}$ (the $m=0$ term is $0$, so
$\max_{m\le L}=\max_{1\le m\le L}$), which is the form consumed downstream via
\texttt{isBigOpOne\_of\_lintegral\_le}. The three substantive ingredients are separate reusable
lemmas filling a Mathlib gap: the shifted martingale \texttt{AlphaRAR.martingale\_shift}, Doob's
$L^2$ submartingale \texttt{AlphaRAR.submartingale\_sq}, and the $L^2$ maximal inequality
\texttt{AlphaRAR.lintegral\_sup'\_abs\_le\_two\_mul\_sqrt} (whose analytic core is the tail-to-$L^1$
lemma \texttt{MeasureTheory.lintegral\_le\_two\_mul\_sqrt\_of\_meas\_ge\_le}).
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes

nodes.name: Lean lintegral form
nodes.statement:
\texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal} states the equivalent $\int^-$ (lintegral)
bound $\int^- \max_{m\le L}|M_n - M_{n-m}| \le 4\sqrt{C_0 L}$ (the $m=0$ term is $0$, so
$\max_{m\le L}=\max_{1\le m\le L}$), which is the form consumed downstream via
\texttt{isBigOpOne\_of\_lintegral\_le}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean lintegral form

nodes.name: Reusable ingredients
nodes.statement:
The three substantive ingredients are separate reusable
lemmas filling a Mathlib gap: the shifted martingale \texttt{AlphaRAR.martingale\_shift}, Doob's
$L^2$ submartingale \texttt{AlphaRAR.submartingale\_sq}, and the $L^2$ maximal inequality
\texttt{AlphaRAR.lintegral\_sup'\_abs\_le\_two\_mul\_sqrt} (whose analytic core is the tail-to-$L^1$
lemma \texttt{MeasureTheory.lintegral\_le\_two\_mul\_sqrt\_of\_meas\_ge\_le}).
nodes.statement_short: Reusable ingredients

nodes.name: Dyadic blocking and geometric sum
nodes.statement:
Split the range $[L,n]$ into dyadic blocks $2^{j-1} \le m < 2^j$. On such a block
$\frac1m \le \frac{2}{2^j}$, so
$\E[\max_{L\le m\le n}\frac{|M_n-M_{n-m}|}{m}]
 \le \sum_{j \ge \log_2 L} \frac{2}{2^j}\, \E[\max_{m<2^j}|M_n-M_{n-m}|]
 \le \sum_{j\ge\log_2 L} \frac{2}{2^j}\, 4\sqrt{C_0 2^j}
 = 8\sqrt{C_0}\sum_{j\ge\log_2 L} 2^{-j/2}$
by Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal}. The geometric sum
$\sum_{j\ge\log_2 L} 2^{-j/2} = (2+\sqrt2)\,2^{-\lceil\log_2 L\rceil/2} \le 4/\sqrt L$
(using $\tfrac1{1-1/\sqrt2} = 2+\sqrt2 \le 4$ and $2^{\lceil\log_2 L\rceil}\ge L$), giving the bound
$32\sqrt{C_0/L}$.
nodes.statement_short: Dyadic blocking and geometric sum

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal\_dyadic} states the equivalent $\int^-$
(lintegral) bound $\int^- \max_{L\le m\le n}\frac{|M_n-M_{n-m}|}{m} \le 32\sqrt{C_0/L}$ (the
constant $32 = 8(2+\sqrt2)$ rounded up, which suffices for the downstream $o_p$; the exact
constant is immaterial). The dyadic index of $m$ is $\lfloor\log_2 m\rfloor+1$ (\texttt{Nat.log}),
the per-scale bound is Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal} applied at $L' = \min(2^j-1,n)$, and the
geometric series is bounded via \texttt{geom\_sum\_eq} with ratio $1/\sqrt2 \le 3/4$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes

nodes.name: Lean lintegral form and constant
nodes.statement:
\texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal\_dyadic} states the equivalent $\int^-$
(lintegral) bound $\int^- \max_{L\le m\le n}\frac{|M_n-M_{n-m}|}{m} \le 32\sqrt{C_0/L}$ (the
constant $32 = 8(2+\sqrt2)$ rounded up, which suffices for the downstream $o_p$; the exact
constant is immaterial).
nodes.statement_short: Lean lintegral form and constant

nodes.name: Dyadic index and geometric series in Lean
nodes.statement:
The dyadic index of $m$ is $\lfloor\log_2 m\rfloor+1$ (\texttt{Nat.log}),
the per-scale bound is Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal} applied at $L' = \min(2^j-1,n)$, and the
geometric series is bounded via \texttt{geom\_sum\_eq} with ratio $1/\sqrt2 \le 3/4$.
nodes.statement_short: Dyadic index and geometric series in Lean

nodes.name: Reduce to coordinatewise scalar bounds
nodes.statement:
By the $\ell^2\le\ell^1$ inequality $\|v\| = \sqrt{\sum_k v_k^2}\le\sum_k|v_k|$, the running maximum of
the norm is bounded by $\sum_k$ of the coordinatewise running maxima (maximum of a sum $\le$ sum of
maxima), and each coordinate is controlled by Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal} (resp.\
Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal_dyadic}). Summing the $K$ scalar bounds gives the factor $K$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to coordinatewise scalar bounds

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal\_pi} and
\texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal\_dyadic\_pi} state the $\int^-$ forms with the norm written as
$\sqrt{\sum_k(M_{n,k}-M_{n-m,k})^2}$. The coordinate interchange uses \texttt{Finset.sup'\_le} and
\texttt{Finset.le\_sup'}; the $\ell^2\le\ell^1$ step is \texttt{sum\_sq\_le\_sq\_sum\_of\_nonneg};
integration term-by-term is \texttt{lintegral\_finsetSum}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes

nodes.name: Lean statements
nodes.statement:
\texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal\_pi} and
\texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal\_dyadic\_pi} state the $\int^-$ forms with the norm written as
$\sqrt{\sum_k(M_{n,k}-M_{n-m,k})^2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean statements

nodes.name: Lean coordinate interchange
nodes.statement_short: Lean coordinate interchange

nodes.name: Short gap: bounded by the small-window maximum
nodes.statement:
Let $d := n - \ell$. If $d < L$, then $\|Q_n - Q_\ell\| = \|Q_n - Q_{n-d}\| \le
\max_{m<L}\|Q_n-Q_{n-m}\|$.
nodes.statement_short: Short gap: bounded by the small-window maximum

nodes.name: Long gap: bounded by the normalized maximum times the gap
nodes.statement_short: Long gap: bounded by the normalized maximum times the gap

nodes.name: Combine the two cases
nodes.statement: Taking the larger of the two bounds proves the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the two cases

nodes.name: Embed the event in a squared shifted event
nodes.statement:
For $\alpha > 0$, $\{\max_k X_k \ge \lambda\} \subseteq
\{\max_k (X_k+\alpha)^2 \ge (\lambda+\alpha)^2\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Embed the event in a squared shifted event

nodes.name: Doob's inequality bounds the probability
nodes.statement:
As $\{(X_k+\alpha)^2\}$ is a
submartingale, Doob's inequality gives
$\Prob(\max_k(X_k+\alpha)^2 \ge (\lambda+\alpha)^2)
 \le \frac{\E[(X_n+\alpha)^2]}{(\lambda+\alpha)^2}
 = \frac{\Var(X_n)+\alpha^2}{(\lambda+\alpha)^2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Doob's inequality bounds the probability

nodes.name: Optimize the shift
nodes.statement:
Optimizing at $\alpha = \Var(X_n)/\lambda$ gives
$\frac{\Var(X_n)}{\Var(X_n)+\lambda^2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Optimize the shift

nodes.name: Variance equals A'' at the natural parameter
nodes.statement:
For the natural family, $\E_\eta[Y] = A'(\eta)$ and $\Var_\eta(Y) = A''(\eta)$.
With $\theta_k = A'(\eta_k)$ one has $\Var(\xi_{1,k}) = A''(\eta_k)$.
nodes.statement_short: Variance equals A'' at the natural parameter

nodes.name: Reparameterize Fisher information to get 1/A''
nodes.statement:
By the
reparameterization formula for Fisher information,
$I_k(\theta_k) = I_{\eta_k}(\eta_k)\big(\frac{d\eta_k}{d\theta_k}\big)^2
 = A''(\eta_k)\big(\frac{1}{A''(\eta_k)}\big)^2 = \frac{1}{A''(\eta_k)}$,
so $\Var(\xi_{1,k}) = I_k(\theta_k)^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reparameterize Fisher information to get 1/A''

nodes.name: Bounded time change: the limit is -alpha v <= 0
nodes.statement:
If $(a_n)$ is bounded, it is eventually constant, so $X_{a_n}/n \to 0$ and
$\varepsilon_n + \frac{X_n - X_{a_n}}{n} \to -\alpha v \le 0$, whence the positive
part tends to $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded time change: the limit is -alpha v <= 0

nodes.name: Diverging time change: bound the subtracted term
nodes.statement:
If $a_n \to \infty$, then $X_{a_n}/a_n \to -\alpha v$; for
$\varepsilon>0$ and $n$ large, $-\frac{X_{a_n}}{n} \le (\varepsilon + \alpha v)\frac{a_n}{n}
 \le \varepsilon + \alpha v$ (using $a_n \le n$), so
$\varepsilon_n + \frac{X_n - X_{a_n}}{n} \le \varepsilon_n + \frac{X_n}{n} + \varepsilon + \alpha v$.
nodes.statement_short: Diverging time change: bound the subtracted term

nodes.name: Limsup at most epsilon, epsilon arbitrary
nodes.statement:
Since $\frac{X_n}{n} + \alpha v \to 0$ and $\limsup \varepsilon_n \le 0$, the
limsup of the left side is $\le \varepsilon$; as $\varepsilon$ is arbitrary the
positive part tends to $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Limsup at most epsilon, epsilon arbitrary

nodes.name: After burn-in the deviation is nonpositive
nodes.statement:
If $\ell_{n,k} \ge Km_0+1$, then by definition of the hitting time
$N_{\ell_{n,k},k}/\ell_{n,k} \le \hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k}$, so the difference is
$\le 0$.
nodes.statement_short: After burn-in the deviation is nonpositive

nodes.name: Before burn-in the deviation is at most Km_0
nodes.statement:
If $\ell_{n,k} < Km_0+1$, then $N_{\ell_{n,k},k} \le \ell_{n,k} \le Km_0$,
so the difference is $\le Km_0$.
nodes.statement_short: Before burn-in the deviation is at most Km_0

nodes.name: A constant bound is o(sqrt n)
nodes.statement:
Either way it is bounded by the constant $Km_0$,
which is $o(\sqrt n)$.
nodes.statement_short: A constant bound is o(sqrt n)

nodes.name: Discharge conditions (i)-(iii) by the three lemmas
nodes.statement:
Condition (i) is Lemma~\ref{lem:hitting_basic}, condition (ii) is
Lemma~\ref{lem:preliminary_ineq}, and condition (iii) is
Lemma~\ref{lem:preliminary_small}.
nodes.statement_short: Discharge conditions (i)-(iii) by the three lemmas

nodes.name: Lean packaging and the boundary summand
nodes.statement:
(The Lean lemmas
\texttt{generic\_ineq\_of\_hitting} and \texttt{generic\_small\_of\_hitting} package
Lemmas~\ref{lem:preliminary_ineq}--\ref{lem:preliminary_small} at the last under-sampling time
$\ell_{n,k}$ into the operational forms \eqref{eq:generic_ineq}--\eqref{eq:generic_small},
given the $\aRTS$ throttle $\neg P_m \Rightarrow p_{m}\le\alpha\hat\rho_m$ (patient $m$ throttled
by the target at the same index $m$). A single boundary summand $p_{\ell,k}-\alpha\hat\rho_{\ell,k}$
is uncontrolled by the throttle, so the constant in \eqref{eq:generic_ineq} is $1$. No lower bound
on $\ell_{n,k}$ is needed: the telescoping identity holds at $\ell_{n,k}=0$ as well (the
$\alpha\hat\rho$ sum of $U$ grows at every step), so the $0$-indexed edge case is automatic. The
remaining step is to verify that a concrete $\aRTS$ design's selection probabilities satisfy the
throttle — this is Definition~\ref{def:aRTS_alg} and Corollary~\ref{cor:aRTS_alg_consistency}.)
nodes.statement_short: Lean packaging and the boundary summand

nodes.name: Instantiate the generic theorem
nodes.statement:
Instantiate Theorem~\ref{thm:generic_main} with the assignment indicators
$Y_{n,k}=\mathbf 1\{A_n=k\}$, the selection probabilities
$p_{n,k}=P[\mathbf 1\{A_n=k\}\mid\filt_{n-1}]$, the plug-in target
$\hat\rho_{n,k}=\Target(\estParams_n)_k$, and $\ell_{n,k}$ the last under-sampling time.
nodes.statement_short: Instantiate the generic theorem

nodes.name: Discharge hypotheses by earlier results
nodes.statement:
The generic
conditions are discharged by Proposition~\ref{prop:aRTS_generic} (the throttle is the stated design
hypothesis); the vanishing normalized assignment martingale $M_{n,k}/n\to0$ is
Lemma~\ref{lem:M_lln}, and the plug-in-target convergence $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to v_k$ is
Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_converges}.
nodes.statement_short: Discharge hypotheses by earlier results

nodes.name: Identify the common limit
nodes.statement: The common limit $v_k$ is that of $\hat\rho_{\cdot,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Identify the common limit

nodes.name: Quadratic variation of Q is V_k N
nodes.statement:
The response martingale $Q_{\cdot,k}$ has predictable quadratic variation
$\langle Q_k\rangle_n = V_k N_{n,k}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:Q_quad_var}).
nodes.statement_short: Quadratic variation of Q is V_k N

nodes.name: Apply bracket-normalized SLLN
nodes.statement:
If $V_k>0$, then on
$\{N_{n,k}\to\infty\}$ the bracket $\langle Q_k\rangle_n = V_k N_{n,k}\to\infty$, so the
bracket-normalized strong law (Theorem~\ref{thm:mart_slln_bracket}) gives
$Q_{n,k}/\langle Q_k\rangle_n\to0$, whence
$Q_{n,k}/N_{n,k} = V_k\,(Q_{n,k}/\langle Q_k\rangle_n)\to0$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply bracket-normalized SLLN

nodes.name: Zero variance forces Q = 0
nodes.statement:
If $V_k=0$, then
$\E[Q_{n,k}^2] = V_k\,\E[N_{n,k}] = 0$, so $Q_{n,k}=0$ a.s.\ for every $n$ and the ratio is
identically $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Zero variance forces Q = 0

nodes.name: Write the error via Q
nodes.statement:
By the exact error identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator_bahadur}),
$\hat\theta_{n,k}-\theta_k = (Q_{n,k}+(\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k))/(N_{n,k}+1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Write the error via Q

nodes.name: Offset vanishes and Q/N -> 0
nodes.statement:
On
$\{N_{n,k}\to\infty\}$ the constant offset is $O(N_{n,k}^{-1})\to0$, while
$\frac{Q_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}+1} = \frac{Q_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}}\cdot\frac{N_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}+1}\to0\cdot1=0$
by Lemma~\ref{lem:respMart_div_count_slln}.
nodes.statement_short: Offset vanishes and Q/N -> 0

nodes.name: Conclude convergence
nodes.statement: Hence $\hat\theta_{n,k}\to\theta_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude convergence

nodes.name: Infinite branch by SLLN, finite branch eventually constant
nodes.statement:
On $\{N_{n,k}\to\infty\}$, the estimator converges a.s.\ to $\theta_k$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_limit_infinite} (the martingale strong law applied to $Q_{\cdot,k}$). On
$\{\sup_n N_{n,k}<\infty\}$, only finitely many responses on arm $k$ are ever
observed, so $\hat{\theta}_{n,k}$ is eventually constant with a value in
$V_k^{\mathrm{att}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Infinite branch by SLLN, finite branch eventually constant

nodes.name: Closure form of the attainable set
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization} (\texttt{AlphaRAR.estimator\_limit\_mem\_attainableSet}). With the closure form
of $I_k$ (Definition~\ref{def:attainable}) the case split is unnecessary:
nodes.statement_short: Closure form of the attainable set

nodes.name: Any pointwise limit lies in the closure of the range
nodes.statement:
\emph{any} pointwise limit
of $\hat{\theta}_{\cdot,k}$ is a limit of values in the range of the estimator, hence lies in the
closure of that range, i.e.\ in $I_k$ (Mathlib's \texttt{mem\_closure\_of\_tendsto}).
nodes.statement_short: Any pointwise limit lies in the closure of the range

nodes.name: Continuity and Condition B give a limit in (0,1)^K
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_converges_cont} (with $\Target$ continuous on $\hilb$ by Condition~\textbf{B})
and Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_limit_dichotomy}, $\estParams_n \to z$ a.s.\ with
$z \in I_1\times\dots\times I_K$. By Condition~\textbf{B}, $\Target$ is
continuous on the open set $\hilb \supseteq I_1\times\dots\times I_K$ and maps
$I_1\times\dots\times I_K$ into $(0,1)^K$; hence
$\estTarget_n = \Target(\estParams_n) \to \Target(z) =: u \in (0,1)^K$.
nodes.statement_short: Continuity and Condition B give a limit in (0,1)^K

nodes.name: Lean form of the positivity hypothesis
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization} (\texttt{AlphaRAR.rho\_converges\_pos}). Condition~\textbf{B}'s non-sparsity
enters as the hypothesis \texttt{hTpos}: $\Target$ maps the product of the attainable sets
(Definition~\ref{def:attainable}) into the positive orthant. With $z$ the a.s.\ estimator-vector
limit (\texttt{estimator\_ae\_tendsto\_pi}), each $z_k\in I_k$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_limit_dichotomy}), so \texttt{hTpos} gives $u_k=\Target(z)_k>0$ while
continuity of $\Target$ gives $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to u_k$. The formalized conclusion is the positivity
$u_k>0$ (the non-sparsity used downstream in Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_consistent}); the matching upper
bound $u_k<1$ is the immediate consequence of the simplex constraint $\sum_k\Target(z)_k=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean form of the positivity hypothesis

nodes.name: Expand U/n
nodes.statement_short: Expand U/n

nodes.name: Each term converges
nodes.statement_short: Each term converges

nodes.name: Combine the limits
nodes.statement:
Hence
$\frac{U_{n,k}}{n} \to \alpha u_k - u_k = -(1-\alpha)u_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the limits

nodes.name: Set up the analytic lemma with X = U, a = ell
nodes.statement:
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:convergence} with $X_n := U_{n,k}$, $a_n := \ell_{n,k}$
(non-decreasing, $\le n$ by the generic conditions), and
$\varepsilon_n := \frac1n + \frac{N_{\ell_{n,k},k}-\ell_{n,k}\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k},k}}{n}$,
which satisfies $\limsup\varepsilon_n \le 0$ by \eqref{eq:generic_small}.
nodes.statement_short: Set up the analytic lemma with X = U, a = ell

nodes.name: The lemma yields the positive part vanishing
nodes.statement:
Since
$\frac{U_{n,k}}{n}\to -(1-\alpha)u_k$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:U_over_n}), the lemma yields
$\big(\varepsilon_n + \frac{U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_{n,k},k}}{n}\big)^+ \to 0$.
nodes.statement_short: The lemma yields the positive part vanishing

nodes.name: Transfer to the proportion-target gap
nodes.statement:
Combined
with the generic inequality \eqref{eq:generic_ineq}, which bounds
$\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k}$ by that quantity, we get
$\big(\frac{N_{n,k}}{n}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k}\big)^+\to0$.
nodes.statement_short: Transfer to the proportion-target gap

nodes.name: Infinite sampling, continuity and matching identify the limit
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:all_arms_infinite} every arm is sampled infinitely often, so
the first branch of Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_limit_dichotomy} applies to every $k$:
$\hat{\theta}_{n,k}\to\theta_k$. Continuity of $\Target$ gives
$\hat{\rho}_n\to\Target(\Params)=v$, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:match} the limit $u$ of
$N_n/n$ equals $v$.
nodes.statement_short: Infinite sampling, continuity and matching identify the limit
nodes.section: 6.4 Identification of the limit and consistency

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.theta\_consistent\_pi\_of\_condB} discharges this from the
\emph{joint} consistency (a common a.s.\ limit $u$ with both $N_{n,k}/n\to u_k$ and
$\hat\rho_{n,k}\to u_k$) plus Condition~\textbf{B}: since $\hat\rho_{n,k}=\Target(\estParams_n)_k\to
\Target(z)_k$ ($z$ the estimator-vector limit) the shared limit is $u=\Target(z)$, which
Condition~\textbf{B}'s non-sparsity (\texttt{hTpos}, Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_converges}) makes positive;
positivity gives $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ (\texttt{all\_arms\_infinite}), so the dichotomy's infinite branch
(\texttt{estimator\_ae\_tendsto\_of\_pullCount\_atTop}) identifies each limit as the arm mean. For an
aRTS design the joint consistency is exactly \texttt{aRTS\_consistency\_of\_isARTS} (whose plug-in
target \texttt{aRTSTarget} is by definition $\Target(\estParams_n)$), giving the fully discharged
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_theta\_consistent}: $\estParams_n\to\Params$ a.s.\ under only the aRTS design
hypotheses and Condition~\textbf{B}. (\texttt{AlphaRAR.theta\_consistent} is the per-arm core taking
the positive proportion as hypothesis.)
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes
nodes.section: 6.4 Identification of the limit and consistency

nodes.name: Lean discharge from joint consistency
nodes.statement:
\texttt{AlphaRAR.theta\_consistent\_pi\_of\_condB} discharges this from the
\emph{joint} consistency (a common a.s.\ limit $u$ with both $N_{n,k}/n\to u_k$ and
$\hat\rho_{n,k}\to u_k$) plus Condition~\textbf{B}: since $\hat\rho_{n,k}=\Target(\estParams_n)_k\to
\Target(z)_k$ ($z$ the estimator-vector limit) the shared limit is $u=\Target(z)$, which
Condition~\textbf{B}'s non-sparsity (\texttt{hTpos}, Lemma~\ref{lem:rho_converges}) makes positive;
positivity gives $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ (\texttt{all\_arms\_infinite}), so the dichotomy's infinite branch
(\texttt{estimator\_ae\_tendsto\_of\_pullCount\_atTop}) identifies each limit as the arm mean.
nodes.statement_short: Lean discharge from joint consistency
nodes.section: 6.4 Identification of the limit and consistency

nodes.name: Fully discharged aRTS version
nodes.statement:
For an
aRTS design the joint consistency is exactly \texttt{aRTS\_consistency\_of\_isARTS} (whose plug-in
target \texttt{aRTSTarget} is by definition $\Target(\estParams_n)$), giving the fully discharged
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_theta\_consistent}: $\estParams_n\to\Params$ a.s.\ under only the aRTS design
hypotheses and Condition~\textbf{B}. (\texttt{AlphaRAR.theta\_consistent} is the per-arm core taking
the positive proportion as hypothesis.)
nodes.statement_short: Fully discharged aRTS version
nodes.section: 6.4 Identification of the limit and consistency

nodes.name: Exact error identity
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator_bahadur} the error is exactly
$\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\theta_k = (Q_{n,k}+(\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k))/(N_{n,k}+1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Exact error identity

nodes.name: Subsampled LIL bounds Q
nodes.statement:
Optional skipping turns
$Q_{\cdot,k}$ into a predictably subsampled i.i.d.\ partial sum, so the subsampled Hartman--Wintner
LIL (Corollary~\ref{cor:subsampled_lil}) gives $|Q_{n,k}| = O(\sqrt{N_{n,k}\log\log N_{n,k}})$ a.s.;
since $N_{n,k}\sim v_k n$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:match}), eventually $N_{n,k}\le 2v_k n$ and
$\log\log N_{n,k}\le 2\log\log n$, whence $|Q_{n,k}| = O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$
(\texttt{ae\_eventually\_abs\_respMart\_le\_sqrt\_nat\_mul\_loglog}).
nodes.statement_short: Subsampled LIL bounds Q

nodes.name: Divide by the linearly growing count
nodes.statement:
Dividing by $N_{n,k}+1
\gtrsim (v_k/2)n$ bounds $|\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\theta_k| \le
(2/v_k)(C+|\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k|)\sqrt{n\log\log n}/n = O(\sqrt{\log\log n / n})$, via the shared
deterministic core \texttt{abs\_estimator\_sub\_le\_rate\_gen}.
nodes.statement_short: Divide by the linearly growing count

nodes.name: Alternative log-rate route
nodes.statement:
The coarser $\log$-rate route through
the truncation LIL (Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_truncation}, \texttt{abs\_estimator\_sub\_le\_rate\_ae})
remains available.
nodes.statement_short: Alternative log-rate route

nodes.name: Delta method from the estimator rate
nodes.statement:
A first-order Taylor expansion of $\Target$ around $\Params$ (twice
differentiable by Condition~\textbf{B}) gives
$\hat{\rho}_n - v = G(\estParams_n-\Params) + O(\|\estParams_n-\Params\|^2)$
with $G := \nabla\Target|_\Params$. Both terms are
$O(\sqrt{\log\log n / n})$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_LIL}.
nodes.statement_short: Delta method from the estimator rate

nodes.name: Lean delta-method core and aRTS discharge
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} The delta-method core is formalized as \texttt{AlphaRAR.rho\_rate}: for a target
map $\Target$ merely \emph{differentiable} at $\Params$ (the first-order part of Condition~\textbf{B};
the second-order term is unnecessary for the $O$-rate), if the estimator vector converges,
$\estParams_n\to\Params$ a.s.\ (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_consistent}), with each coordinate at the rate
$\hat\theta_{n,k}-\theta_k = O(r_n)$ a.s.\ (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_LIL}, $r_n=\sqrt{\log\log n/n}$),
then every coordinate of the plug-in target satisfies $\hat\rho_{n,k}-v_k = O(r_n)$ a.s. The
mechanism is the generic estimate \texttt{AlphaRAR.isBigO\_target\_sub\_of\_tendsto}: a differentiable
map sends $\estParams_n-\Params$ to $\Target(\estParams_n)-\Target(\Params)$ of the same big-$O$ order
(\texttt{AlphaRAR.isBigO\_sub\_comp\_of\_differentiableAt}, from \texttt{HasFDerivAt.isBigO\_sub}),
combined coordinatewise via \texttt{isBigO\_pi}. For a concrete aRTS design this is fully discharged in
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_rho\_rate}: consistency $\estParams_n\to\Params$ is
\texttt{aRTS\_theta\_consistent} (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_consistent}) and the coordinatewise rate is the
subsampled loglog LIL (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_LIL}), fed through the positive allocation proportion, so
the only remaining hypotheses are Condition~\textbf{B} (differentiability and non-sparsity) and the
Condition~\textbf{A} moments.
nodes.statement_short: Lean delta-method core and aRTS discharge

nodes.name: Algebraic regrouping and Cesaro o(1) terms
nodes.statement:
Expanding $U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_n,k}$ from Definition~\ref{def:U} and grouping the
target terms around $v_k$,
$U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_n,k}
 = (n-\ell_n)\big[-(1-\alpha)v_k - (\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-v_k)
   + \frac{\alpha}{n-\ell_n}\sum_{m=\ell_n}^{n-1}(\hat{\rho}_{m,k}-v_k)\big]
   + M_{n,k}-M_{\ell_n,k} + \ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n,k}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k})$.
By Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN}, $\hat{\rho}_n\to v$, so both $\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-v_k$ and
the Cesàro average $\frac1{n-\ell_n}\sum_{m=\ell_n}^{n-1}(\hat{\rho}_{m,k}-v_k)$
are $o(1)$ (treating separately the bounded and diverging cases of $\ell_n$).
nodes.statement_short: Algebraic regrouping and Cesaro o(1) terms

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.diff\_U\_decomp}. The exact $M$-explicit identity is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.auxU\_sub}; the $o(1)$ remainder $\alpha\sum_{[\ell_n,n)}(\hat\rho_m-v)
-(n-\ell_n)(\hat\rho_n-v)$ is made rigorous as ``for every $\varepsilon>0$, eventually
$|\cdot|\le\varepsilon(n-\ell_n)$'', its first term controlled by the windowed Cesàro bound
\texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_sum\_Ico\_sub\_le\_of\_tendsto} (valid for an arbitrary window, bounded or
diverging) and its second by $\hat\rho_n\to v$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes

nodes.name: Lean declaration
nodes.statement: \texttt{AlphaRAR.diff\_U\_decomp}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean declaration

nodes.name: Lean form of the o(1) remainder
nodes.statement:
The exact $M$-explicit identity is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.auxU\_sub}; the $o(1)$ remainder $\alpha\sum_{[\ell_n,n)}(\hat\rho_m-v)
-(n-\ell_n)(\hat\rho_n-v)$ is made rigorous as ``for every $\varepsilon>0$, eventually
$|\cdot|\le\varepsilon(n-\ell_n)$'', its first term controlled by the windowed Cesàro bound
\texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_sum\_Ico\_sub\_le\_of\_tendsto} (valid for an arbitrary window, bounded or
diverging) and its second by $\hat\rho_n\to v$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean form of the o(1) remainder

nodes.name: Taylor expansion and splitting estimator differences
nodes.statement:
By Corollary~\ref{cor:mart_Op}, $Q_{n,k}=O_p(\sqrt n)$, hence
$\hat{\theta}_{n,k}-\theta_k = Q_{n,k}/N_{n,k} + o_p(N_{n,k}^{-1/2}) = O_p(n^{-1/2})$
using $N_{n,k}\sim v_k n$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_error_Q}). The Taylor expansion of
$\Target$ gives $\hat{\rho}_n - v = G(\estParams_n-\Params)+O_p(1/n)$ and similarly
at $\ell_n$; subtracting,
$\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)
 = \ell_n G(\estParams_{\ell_n}-\estParams_n) + O_p(1)$, so
$|\ell_n(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_n}-\hat{\rho}_n)| \le C\ell_n\|\estParams_{\ell_n}-\estParams_n\| + O_p(1)$.
Writing the estimator difference through $Q$ (splitting into the increment
$\sum_{j=\ell_n+1}^n$ and the reweighting of $\sum_{j\le\ell_n}$) and bounding
each piece using $N_{n,k}-N_{\ell_n,k}\le n-\ell_n$ and the SLLN, the three
resulting terms are respectively $C\|Q_n-Q_{\ell_n}\|$, $o(1)(n-\ell_n)$ and
$o_p(\sqrt n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Taylor expansion and splitting estimator differences

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.ell\_rho\_control} produces the bound in the shape
$\ell_n|\hat\rho_{\ell_n,k}-\hat\rho_{n,k}| \le V_\rho(n-\ell_n)+W_\rho$ with $V_\rho=o_p(1)$,
$W_\rho=o_p(\sqrt n)$, which is what the drift-sign step consumes. The Condition-\textbf{B} input
enters as the single hypothesis \texttt{hlip} (the target is Lipschitz near $\Params$, so
$|\hat\rho_{\ell,k}-\hat\rho_{n,k}|\le L\sum_{k'}|\hat\theta_{\ell,k'}-\hat\theta_{n,k'}|$
eventually) --- mirroring how \texttt{clt\_rho} takes the derivative as a hypothesis. The
estimator-increment control $\ell|\hat\theta_{\ell,k'}-\hat\theta_{n,k'}|\le g_{k'}(n-\ell)+h_{k'}
|Q_{n,k'}-Q_{\ell,k'}|$ is \texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_estimator\_diff\_le}; the coefficients are
$g_{k'}=o_p(1)$ (from the Doob-maximal bound \texttt{isBigOpOne\_sup'\_abs\_div\_sqrt} and the a.s.\
bound \texttt{isBigOpOne\_of\_ae\_bounded}) and the reweighting coefficient
$h_{k'}=\ell_n/(N_{n,k'}+1)$, which is only \emph{bounded in probability} ($O_p(1)$, converging a.s.\
to $1/v_{k'}$, again via \texttt{isBigOpOne\_of\_ae\_bounded}), not by a uniform constant; it
therefore enters the $o_p$ bookkeeping through $O_p\cdot o_p=o_p$
(\texttt{IsBigOpOne.mul\_littleOp}). The $Q$-increment control
$|Q_{n,k'}-Q_{\ell,k'}|\le Q_v(n-\ell)+Q_w$ is \texttt{qm\_increments\_resp}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes

nodes.name: Lean bound shape
nodes.statement:
\texttt{AlphaRAR.ell\_rho\_control} produces the bound in the shape
$\ell_n|\hat\rho_{\ell_n,k}-\hat\rho_{n,k}| \le V_\rho(n-\ell_n)+W_\rho$ with $V_\rho=o_p(1)$,
$W_\rho=o_p(\sqrt n)$, which is what the drift-sign step consumes.
nodes.statement_short: Lean bound shape

nodes.name: Lipschitz hypothesis and O_p/o_p bookkeeping
nodes.statement:
The Condition-\textbf{B} input
enters as the single hypothesis \texttt{hlip} (the target is Lipschitz near $\Params$, so
$|\hat\rho_{\ell,k}-\hat\rho_{n,k}|\le L\sum_{k'}|\hat\theta_{\ell,k'}-\hat\theta_{n,k'}|$
eventually) --- mirroring how \texttt{clt\_rho} takes the derivative as a hypothesis. The
estimator-increment control $\ell|\hat\theta_{\ell,k'}-\hat\theta_{n,k'}|\le g_{k'}(n-\ell)+h_{k'}
|Q_{n,k'}-Q_{\ell,k'}|$ is \texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_estimator\_diff\_le}; the coefficients are
$g_{k'}=o_p(1)$ (from the Doob-maximal bound \texttt{isBigOpOne\_sup'\_abs\_div\_sqrt} and the a.s.\
bound \texttt{isBigOpOne\_of\_ae\_bounded}) and the reweighting coefficient
$h_{k'}=\ell_n/(N_{n,k'}+1)$, which is only \emph{bounded in probability} ($O_p(1)$, converging a.s.\
to $1/v_{k'}$, again via \texttt{isBigOpOne\_of\_ae\_bounded}), not by a uniform constant; it
therefore enters the $o_p$ bookkeeping through $O_p\cdot o_p=o_p$
(\texttt{IsBigOpOne.mul\_littleOp}). The $Q$-increment control
$|Q_{n,k'}-Q_{\ell,k'}|\le Q_v(n-\ell)+Q_w$ is \texttt{qm\_increments\_resp}.
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz hypothesis and O_p/o_p bookkeeping

nodes.name: Maximal bounds give o_p terms; plug into increment control
nodes.statement:
Pick $L_n\to\infty$ with $L_n = o(n)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal_dyadic} bound the two maximal quantities
$\E[\max_{m\le L_n}\|Q_n-Q_{n-m}\|]\le 2\sqrt{L_n C_0}$ and
$\E[\max_{L_n\le m<n}\frac{\|Q_n-Q_{n-m}\|}{m}]\le 3\sqrt{C_0/L_n}$; by
Lemma~\ref{lem:expectation_to_O} these are $O_p(\sqrt{L_n})=o_p(\sqrt n)$ and
$O_p(1/\sqrt{L_n})=o_p(1)$ respectively. Plugging into the deterministic
inequality of Lemma~\ref{lem:increment_control} gives the bound for $Q$; the same
argument applied to $M$ gives the second bound.
nodes.statement_short: Maximal bounds give o_p terms; plug into increment control

nodes.name: Lean window sequences and vector maximal bounds
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} The two maximal quantities are formalized as \texttt{wmaxSeq} and
\texttt{vmaxSeq} (with the concrete window $L_n=\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor$), and the two $o_p$ statements
are \texttt{AlphaRAR.isLittleOpOne\_wmaxSeq\_div\_sqrt} ($o_p(\sqrt n)$) and
\texttt{AlphaRAR.isLittleOpOne\_vmaxSeq} ($o_p(1)$), proved from the \emph{vector} maximal bounds
(Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_maximal_pi}) and Markov's inequality. The deterministic increment control is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.norm\_increment\_le\_vmaxSeq\_wmaxSeq}. For $Q$ (the response martingale, a
square-integrable family) the $o_p$ statements are \texttt{AlphaRAR.qm\_increments\_resp}; for the
scalar assignment martingale $M$ (bounded increments $|\Delta M|\le1$) they are
\texttt{AlphaRAR.qm\_increments\_of\_bdd} (via the singleton family $\{M\}$).
nodes.statement_short: Lean window sequences and vector maximal bounds

nodes.name: Control the target-change term
nodes.statement:
From Lemma~\ref{lem:ell_rho_control} and the $Q$-bound of
Lemma~\ref{lem:QM_increments},
$|\ell_{n,k}(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k}}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k})| \le o_p(1)(n-\ell_{n,k}) + o_p(\sqrt n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Control the target-change term

nodes.name: Nonpositive drift gives the o_p bound
nodes.statement:
Substituting this and the $M$-bound into the decomposition of
Lemma~\ref{lem:diff_U_decomp},
$U_{n,k}-U_{\ell_{n,k},k} = (n-\ell_{n,k})[-(1-\alpha)v_k+o_p(1)] + o_p(\sqrt n)
 \le o_p(\sqrt n)$, since the drift coefficient is $\le0$ and $n-\ell_{n,k}\ge0$.
nodes.statement_short: Nonpositive drift gives the o_p bound

nodes.name: LIL rates give the a.s. bound
nodes.statement:
For the a.s.\ bound, Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN} gives $n(\hat{\rho}_n-v)=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$,
hence $\ell_{n,k}(\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k}}-\hat{\rho}_{n,k})=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$,
and the LIL for the martingale $M$ gives $M_{n,k}=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$; the same
substitution yields the second inequality.
nodes.statement_short: LIL rates give the a.s. bound

nodes.name: One-sided upper bounds
nodes.statement:
The generic inequality \eqref{eq:generic_ineq} together with
\eqref{eq:generic_small} and Lemma~\ref{lem:U_increment_bound} gives the one-sided
bounds $N_{n,k}-n\hat{\rho}_{n,k} \le o_p(\sqrt n)$ and $\le O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$
a.s.
nodes.statement_short: One-sided upper bounds

nodes.name: Reverse bound via sum-to-zero
nodes.statement:
The reverse inequality follows from $\sum_j N_{n,j}=n$, $\sum_j\hat{\rho}_{n,j}=1$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:counts_sum}): $n\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-N_{n,k}=\sum_{j\ne k}(N_{n,j}-n\hat{\rho}_{n,j})$,
which inherits the same one-sided bounds.
nodes.statement_short: Reverse bound via sum-to-zero

nodes.name: Absolute-value bounds; add the target rate
nodes.statement:
Combining gives the absolute-value
statements. The last line adds $n(\hat{\rho}_{n,k}-v_k)=O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ from
Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN}.
nodes.statement_short: Absolute-value bounds; add the target rate

nodes.name: Cramer-Wold, martingale CLT, Slutsky
nodes.statement:
Normalize arm $k$ by the \emph{deterministic} $\sqrt{c_{k,n}}$. By the Cramér--Wold device it
suffices to treat a scalar projection $\sum_k w_k Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{c_{k,n}}$; since the arm indicators
are disjoint, this is again a single martingale-difference array (row $n$ has increments
$\sum_k (w_k/\sqrt{c_{k,n}})X_{i,k}(\xi_{i,k}-\theta_k)$), whose predictable variation is
$\sum_k w_k^2 V_k N_{n,k}/c_{k,n}\to\sum_k w_k^2V_k$ by regularity, and which satisfies the
conditional Lindeberg condition since $c_{k,n}\to\infty$. Theorem~\ref{thm:mart_clt} and
Cramér--Wold give $(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{c_{k,n}})_k\eqdist\mathcal N(0,\mathrm{diag}(V_k))$. The
coordinatewise scaling $\sqrt{c_{k,n}/N_{n,k}}\to1$ in probability, so multivariate Slutsky
transfers the limit to the self-normalized vector $(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{N_{n,k}})_k$. Finally the Bahadur
identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator_bahadur}) and one more Slutsky step give the statement for
$D_n(\estParams_n-\Params)$.
nodes.statement_short: Cramer-Wold, martingale CLT, Slutsky
nodes.section: 7.3 Joint central limit theorem for the estimators

nodes.name: Lean weighted array and why the Anscombe route does not jointify
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.estimatorError\_joint\_tendsto\_multivariateGaussian}. The key
device is that the weighted martingale array \texttt{AlphaRAR.wArray} carries \emph{row-dependent}
weights $w^{(n)}_k = w_k/\sqrt{c_{k,n}}$, so one array covers both a common normalizer and per-arm
ones; the Cramér--Wold projection is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.wLinComb\_scaled\_tendsto\_gaussianReal}. Taking $c_{k,n}=n$ (with
$N_{n,k}/n\to v_k>0$) recovers Corollary~\ref{cor:mart_clt_componentwise}; taking per-arm $c_{k,n}$
with limit $1$ gives the sparse form used in Chapter~\ref{chap:forced}. Note that a linear
combination of \emph{random-time} sums is not itself a random-time sum, so the Anscombe route
(Lemma~\ref{lem:anscombe_clt}) does not jointify; the martingale-array route above does, precisely
because the arm indicators are disjoint.
nodes.statement_short: Lean weighted array and why the Anscombe route does not jointify
nodes.section: 7.3 Joint central limit theorem for the estimators

nodes.name: Same route as the componentwise corollary
nodes.statement:
Exactly as in Corollary~\ref{cor:mart_clt_componentwise}, but with the deterministic
normalization $\sqrt n$ in place of $D_n=\mathrm{diag}(\sqrt{N_{n,k}})$.
nodes.statement_short: Same route as the componentwise corollary

nodes.name: Write coordinates through Q
nodes.statement:
By the Bahadur
identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator_bahadur}), coordinate $k$ of
$\sqrt n(\estParams_n-\Params)$ is
$(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{N_{n,k}})\cdot\sqrt{nN_{n,k}}/(N_{n,k}+1)
 + (\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k)\sqrt n/(N_{n,k}+1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Write coordinates through Q

nodes.name: Joint CLT and limits of the factors
nodes.statement:
The self-normalized martingale vector
$(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{N_{n,k}})_k$ converges to $\mathcal N(0,\mathrm{diag}(V_k))$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_clt_joint_selfnorm}); the multiplicative factor tends to $1/\sqrt{v_k}$ and
the additive one to $0$ in probability.
nodes.statement_short: Joint CLT and limits of the factors

nodes.name: Rescale the Gaussian
nodes.statement:
Multivariate Slutsky then gives the diagonal rescaling
$\mathrm{diag}(1/\sqrt{v_k})$ of the Gaussian, whose covariance is $\mathrm{diag}(V_k/v_k)=V$.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale the Gaussian

nodes.name: Taylor expansion and Slutsky
nodes.statement:
By the Taylor expansion (as in Lemma~\ref{lem:ell_rho_control}),
$\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v)=G\sqrt n(\estParams_n-\Params)+O_p(1/\sqrt n)$. Apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_theta} and Slutsky.
nodes.statement_short: Taylor expansion and Slutsky

nodes.name: Lean delta-method assembly
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} The delta method is assembled in
\texttt{AlphaRAR.clt\_rho}. First, Mathlib's product-space Slutsky lemma
(\texttt{TendstoInDistribution.continuous\_comp\_prodMk\_of\_tendstoInMeasure\_const}) with
$g(x,r)=Gx+r$ combines the estimator
CLT (Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_theta}) with the fact that the first-order remainder
$\sqrt n(\Target(\estParams_n)-\Target(\Params))-G\sqrt n(\estParams_n-\Params)=\sqrt n\,\varphi(\estParams_n-\Params)$
tends to $0$ in probability, and the limiting law is the linear pushforward of the estimator's Gaussian
(\texttt{AlphaRAR.multivariateGaussian\_map\_matrix}, giving the covariance $GVG^\top$). The
remainder-in-probability is discharged by \texttt{MeasureTheory.tendstoInMeasure\_smul\_littleO\_of\_tight}
(an abstract $\varepsilon$--$\delta$ lemma: if $X_n=a_n\cdot S_n$ is tight, $S_n\to0$ in probability and
$\varphi=o(\|\cdot\|)$ at the origin, then $a_n\cdot\varphi(S_n)\to0$ in probability), whose tightness
input is supplied from the estimator CLT via
\texttt{MeasureTheory.tight\_of\_tendsto\_probabilityMeasure} (portmanteau plus continuity from above of
the limit Gaussian over $\{\|x\|\ge j\}\downarrow\emptyset$). The differentiability of $\Target$ at
$\Params$ (Jacobian $G$; Condition~\textbf{B}) and the a.s.\ consistency $\estParams_n\to\Params$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN}) enter as the hypotheses \texttt{hTderiv} and \texttt{hcons}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean delta-method assembly

nodes.name: Part (i) from the deviation lemma
nodes.statement: Part (i) is Lemma~\ref{lem:prop_dev}.
nodes.statement_short: Part (i) from the deviation lemma

nodes.name: Joint CLT via asymptotic equality and Slutsky
nodes.statement:
For (ii), the marginal CLT for
$\estParams_n$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_theta}. By part (i),
$\sqrt n(N_n/n-\hat{\rho}_n)=o_p(1)$, so $\sqrt n(N_n/n-v)$ and
$\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v)$ have the same limit $\mathcal{N}(0,GVG^\top)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_rho}) and are asymptotically equal; the joint vector
$(\sqrt n(N_n/n-v),\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v))$ therefore equals
$(\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v),\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v))+o_p(1)$, which converges to
$\mathcal{N}(0,\Omega)$ by Slutsky.
nodes.statement_short: Joint CLT via asymptotic equality and Slutsky

nodes.name: Lean formalization of both parts
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} Part (ii) is fully formalized for the $\aRTS$ design. The generic joint
statement is \texttt{AlphaRAR.clt\_joint}: it takes the proportion-deviation fact
$\sqrt n(N_n/n-\hat{\rho}_n)\to_p 0$ of part (i) as a hypothesis and assembles the joint CLT from
\texttt{AlphaRAR.clt\_rho}. The joint vector is the image of $\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v)$ under the
duplication map $x\mapsto(x,x)$ (the stacked matrix $[I;I]$) up to an $o_p(1)$ remainder, so the
same product-space Slutsky lemma as in Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_rho} applies, and the limiting covariance
$[I;I]\,GVG^\top\,[I;I]^\top$ is the block matrix $\Omega$ via the rectangular Gaussian pushforward
\texttt{AlphaRAR.multivariateGaussian\_map\_matrix}. The self-contained $\aRTS$ instantiation is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_clt\_joint}: from the same design bundle as \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev} plus the
Condition-\textbf{B} differentiability of $\Target$ at $\Params$ (Jacobian $G$, exactly the
\texttt{clt\_rho} input), it \emph{discharges} the proportion-deviation hypothesis of
\texttt{clt\_joint} from \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_prop\_dev} --- via the generic bridge
\texttt{AlphaRAR.tendstoInMeasure\_toLp\_of\_forall\_isLittleOpOne} (coordinatewise $o_p(1)$ gives
vector convergence in measure) and the $\sqrt n$-scaling identity
$\sqrt n(N_{n,k}/n-v_k)-\sqrt n(\hat\rho_{n,k}-v_k)=(N_{n,k}-n\hat\rho_{n,k})/\sqrt n$ --- and derives
the $\mathrm{thm{:}LLN}$ consistencies as in \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev}. Part (i) is fully formalized:
the $o_p(\sqrt n)$ statement is \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev} and the two a.s.\ $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$
statements are \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev\_ae} and \texttt{aRTS\_count\_sub\_smul\_ae}
(Lemma~\ref{lem:prop_dev}). Both parts of the theorem are therefore complete for the $\aRTS$ design.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization of both parts

nodes.name: Lean formalization of part (ii)
nodes.statement:
Part (ii) is fully formalized for the $\aRTS$ design. The generic joint
statement is \texttt{AlphaRAR.clt\_joint}: it takes the proportion-deviation fact
$\sqrt n(N_n/n-\hat{\rho}_n)\to_p 0$ of part (i) as a hypothesis and assembles the joint CLT from
\texttt{AlphaRAR.clt\_rho}. The joint vector is the image of $\sqrt n(\hat{\rho}_n-v)$ under the
duplication map $x\mapsto(x,x)$ (the stacked matrix $[I;I]$) up to an $o_p(1)$ remainder, so the
same product-space Slutsky lemma as in Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_rho} applies, and the limiting covariance
$[I;I]\,GVG^\top\,[I;I]^\top$ is the block matrix $\Omega$ via the rectangular Gaussian pushforward
\texttt{AlphaRAR.multivariateGaussian\_map\_matrix}. The self-contained $\aRTS$ instantiation is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_clt\_joint}: from the same design bundle as \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev} plus the
Condition-\textbf{B} differentiability of $\Target$ at $\Params$ (Jacobian $G$, exactly the
\texttt{clt\_rho} input), it \emph{discharges} the proportion-deviation hypothesis of
\texttt{clt\_joint} from \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTS\_prop\_dev} --- via the generic bridge
\texttt{AlphaRAR.tendstoInMeasure\_toLp\_of\_forall\_isLittleOpOne} (coordinatewise $o_p(1)$ gives
vector convergence in measure) and the $\sqrt n$-scaling identity
$\sqrt n(N_{n,k}/n-v_k)-\sqrt n(\hat\rho_{n,k}-v_k)=(N_{n,k}-n\hat\rho_{n,k})/\sqrt n$ --- and derives
the $\mathrm{thm{:}LLN}$ consistencies as in \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization of part (ii)

nodes.name: Lean formalization of part (i)
nodes.statement:
Part (i) is fully formalized:
the $o_p(\sqrt n)$ statement is \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev} and the two a.s.\ $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$
statements are \texttt{aRTS\_prop\_dev\_ae} and \texttt{aRTS\_count\_sub\_smul\_ae}
(Lemma~\ref{lem:prop_dev}). Both parts of the theorem are therefore complete for the $\aRTS$ design.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization of part (i)

nodes.name: Neither disjunct holds after the hitting time
nodes.statement:
By maximality of $\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}}$, neither disjunct in
Definition~\ref{def:hitting_fe} holds at such $m$.
nodes.statement_short: Neither disjunct holds after the hitting time

nodes.name: Forced-exploration step gives probability zero
nodes.statement:
If $\mathbf{U}_m\ne\emptyset$
then $k\notin\argmin_{j\in\mathbf{U}_m}N_{m,j}$, so \eqref{eq:fe_phase} gives
$p_{m+1,k}=0\le\alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Forced-exploration step gives probability zero

nodes.name: Otherwise the throttle applies
nodes.statement:
If $\mathbf{U}_m=\emptyset$ then
\eqref{eq:fe_otherwise} and the over-sampling $N_{m,k}/m>\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$ give
$p_{m+1,k}\le\alpha\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Otherwise the throttle applies

nodes.name: Condition (i)
nodes.statement: (i) Monotonicity and $\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}}\le n$ are immediate.
nodes.statement_short: Condition (i)

nodes.name: Condition (ii) via telescoping and the sign lemma
nodes.statement:
(ii) The
telescoping identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:U_telescope}, whose proof only uses the
increment of $U$) combined with Lemma~\ref{lem:hitting_fe_sign} — every
intermediate $p_{m,k}-\alpha\hat{\rho}_{m-1,k}\le0$ — gives inequality
\eqref{eq:generic_ineq}.
nodes.statement_short: Condition (ii) via telescoping and the sign lemma

nodes.name: Condition (iii) by the two disjuncts
nodes.statement:
(iii) At $m=\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}}$, either
$N_{m,k}/m\le\hat{\rho}_{m,k}$, giving $N_{m,k}-m\hat{\rho}_{m,k}\le0$, or $k$ is
least-sampled in $\mathbf{U}_m$, giving
$N_{\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}},k}-\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}}\hat{\rho}_{\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}},k}
 \le N_{\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}},k}\le h(\ell_{n,k}^{\mathrm{FE}})=o(n)$
by Definition~\ref{def:exploration_schedule}. (The paper bounds this by $o(\sqrt n)$ using
condition (ii); $o(n)$ is all the consistency direction needs, and the $\sqrt n$-scaled direction
gets a sharper bound from Remark~\ref{rem:sparse_clt_fix}.)
nodes.statement_short: Condition (iii) by the two disjuncts

nodes.name: Reduce to the generic theorem
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:preliminary_fe} the $\aRTSFE$ design satisfies the generic
conditions with $\ell^{\mathrm{FE}}$; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:generic_main}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the generic theorem

nodes.name: Lean reuse of abstract-hitting-time theorems
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} Both directions are \emph{direct reuses} of abstract-hitting-time theorems
with the forced-exploration hitting predicate \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFEUnder}
(``under-sampled or under-explored''); the design enters as the history-level predicate
\texttt{AlphaRAR.IsARTSFE} (Definition~\ref{def:aRTSFE}), whose throttle field is transported to
the process by \texttt{AlphaRAR.throttle\_of\_isARTSFE}, and the only new ingredients are the
forced-exploration smallness lemmas. So each of the five declarations mentions only the design, the
environment and the schedule --- no process-level throttle hypothesis --- exactly as on the
$\aRTS$ side. The consistency direction
($N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$, $\hat\rho_{n,k}\to v_k$) is \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_proportion\_tendsto}
(reusing \texttt{AlphaRAR.consistency\_of\_hitting}), whose smallness is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_smallness} ($N_\ell-\ell\hat\rho_\ell\le(h(\ell))^+=o(n)$). The
asymptotic-normality direction (Theorem~\ref{thm:normality}) is: the $o_p(\sqrt n)$ deviation
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_prop\_dev} (reusing \texttt{AlphaRAR.prop\_dev\_of\_hitting}, smallness
\texttt{aRTSFE\_smallness\_op}), the a.s.\ $O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ deviations
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_prop\_dev\_ae} and \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_count\_sub\_smul\_ae} (reusing
\texttt{prop\_dev\_ae\_of\_hitting}/\texttt{count\_sub\_smul\_ae\_of\_hitting}, smallness
\texttt{aRTSFE\_smallness\_upper}), and the joint CLT \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_clt\_joint} (reusing
\texttt{AlphaRAR.clt\_joint\_of\_hitting}). Each abstract-hitting-time theorem is the generalisation
of the corresponding \texttt{aRTS} theorem to an arbitrary measurable hitting predicate, with the
throttle and smallness taken as hypotheses.

Neither $\sqrt n$-scaled smallness lemma uses condition (ii): under Condition~\textbf{B} forced
exploration eventually stops firing (\texttt{AlphaRAR.eventually\_sched\_lt\_pullCount}, the single-arm
form of \texttt{AlphaRAR.underExplored\_eventually\_empty}), so past that time the hitting predicate
can only fire through its under-sampling clause and the gap is bounded by a path constant
(\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_gap\_le\_sum\_of\_not\_underExplored}) --- which is $o(\sqrt n)$ and
$O(\sqrt{n\log\log n})$ for free. The Condition~\textbf{B} input is the consistency direction of
this same theorem, so there is no circularity: it needs only $h(n)=o(n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean reuse of abstract-hitting-time theorems

nodes.name: Stalled arm forces a strictly decreasing nonnegative potential
nodes.statement:
Suppose for contradiction that some arm $i$ stalls: $N_{n,i}=M$ for all $n\ge N$.
Since $h(n)\to\infty$, enlarge $N$ so that $h(n)\ge M$ for $n\ge N$. Then for
$n\ge N$, $N_{n,i}\le h(n)$ gives $i\in\mathbf{U}_n\ne\emptyset$, so the arm
$I_{n+1}$ selected by forced exploration is a least-sampled arm of $\mathbf{U}_n$,
whence $N_{n,I_{n+1}}\le N_{n,i}=M$ and $N_{n+1,I_{n+1}}\le M+1$. The potential
$D(n):=\sum_j (M+1-N_{n,j})^+$ then satisfies $D(n+1)-D(n)=-1$ for all $n\ge N$,
so $D$ becomes negative, contradicting $D\ge0$. Hence every arm is sampled
infinitely often.
nodes.statement_short: Stalled arm forces a strictly decreasing nonnegative potential

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_no\_starvation}, whose deterministic potential-function
core is \texttt{AlphaRAR.no\_starvation\_pathwise}. It weakens ``$i$ stalls at $M$'' to ``$N_{n,i}<B$
for all $n$'' (arm $k$ monotone but bounded), and the action-level forced-exploration rule enters as
the a.s.\ hypothesis \texttt{hfe} (when some arm is under-explored, $A_m$ is a least-sampled
under-explored arm). The potential $D(n)=\sum_j(B+1-N_{n,j})$ is $\N$-valued (truncated subtraction is
the positive part), so $D(n+1)+1=D(n)$ for $n\ge N_1$ forces $t\le D(N_1)$ for all $t$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes

nodes.name: Lean declaration
nodes.statement:
\texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_no\_starvation}, whose deterministic potential-function
core is \texttt{AlphaRAR.no\_starvation\_pathwise}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean declaration

nodes.name: Lean pathwise potential argument
nodes.statement:
It weakens ``$i$ stalls at $M$'' to ``$N_{n,i}<B$
for all $n$'' (arm $k$ monotone but bounded), and the action-level forced-exploration rule enters as
the a.s.\ hypothesis \texttt{hfe} (when some arm is under-explored, $A_m$ is a least-sampled
under-explored arm). The potential $D(n)=\sum_j(B+1-N_{n,j})$ is $\N$-valued (truncated subtraction is
the positive part), so $D(n+1)+1=D(n)$ for $n\ge N_1$ forces $t\le D(N_1)$ for all $t$, a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Lean pathwise potential argument

nodes.name: Combine no-starvation, matching and the LIL
nodes.statement:
The first statement is Lemma~\ref{lem:fe_no_starvation}. Given it, every arm's
estimator converges: $\hat{\theta}_{n,k}\to\theta_k$ by the SLLN, so
$\hat{\rho}_n\to v$ by continuity of $\Target$; the matching argument (as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:match}, using Lemma~\ref{lem:convergence} and the generic
inequality valid by Lemma~\ref{lem:preliminary_fe}) gives $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$,
allowing $v_k=0$. The rate is the LIL for the martingale $Q_{\cdot,k}$ scaled by
its own sample size $N_{n,k}$, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:theta_LIL} but without
dividing by $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine no-starvation, matching and the LIL

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_sparse\_rate}. All three statements flow from
no-starvation (\texttt{aRTSFE\_no\_starvation}, $N_{n,k}\to\infty$): it makes every arm sampled
infinitely often, so $\hat\theta\to\theta$ (\texttt{estimator\_ae\_tendsto\_of\_pullCount\_atTop},
\emph{no positivity}), whence $\hat\rho\to T(\theta)$, and the matching
\texttt{consistency\_of\_hitting} (which never uses positivity, so allows $v_k=0$) gives
$N_{n,k}/n\to T(\theta)_k$. The $N$-scaled rate is \texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_estimator\_sub\_le\_rate\_loglog\_N},
which combines the exact Bahadur identity \texttt{estimator\_sub\_eq} with the subsampled loglog LIL
\texttt{abs\_respMart\_le\_sqrt\_nat\_mul\_loglog} (this uses \emph{only} $N_{n,k}\to\infty$).
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes

nodes.name: Lean declaration
nodes.statement: \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_sparse\_rate}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean declaration

nodes.name: Lean assembly
nodes.statement:
All three statements flow from
no-starvation (\texttt{aRTSFE\_no\_starvation}, $N_{n,k}\to\infty$): it makes every arm sampled
infinitely often, so $\hat\theta\to\theta$ (\texttt{estimator\_ae\_tendsto\_of\_pullCount\_atTop},
\emph{no positivity}), whence $\hat\rho\to T(\theta)$, and the matching
\texttt{consistency\_of\_hitting} (which never uses positivity, so allows $v_k=0$) gives
$N_{n,k}/n\to T(\theta)_k$. The $N$-scaled rate is \texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_estimator\_sub\_le\_rate\_loglog\_N},
which combines the exact Bahadur identity \texttt{estimator\_sub\_eq} with the subsampled loglog LIL
\texttt{abs\_respMart\_le\_sqrt\_nat\_mul\_loglog} (this uses \emph{only} $N_{n,k}\to\infty$).
nodes.statement_short: Lean assembly

nodes.name: Apply the componentwise CLT
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:fe_no_starvation}, $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ for all $k$. Given the regularity of the
pull counts, Lemma~\ref{lem:componentwise} applies and gives the statement.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the componentwise CLT

nodes.name: Lean split of arms by FE-feeding
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_sparse\_clt}. Arms are split by a predicate
$\mathrm{FEfed}$:
\begin{itemize}
  \item if arm $k$ is eventually fed \emph{only} by forced exploration, then its count is regular
    against the \emph{deterministic} schedule, $N_{n,k}/h(n)\to1$
    (\texttt{AlphaRAR.pullCount\_div\_sched\_tendsto\_one});
  \item otherwise arm $k$ has a positive limiting proportion $v_k>0$ with $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$, so it
    is regular against $v_kn$.
\end{itemize}
Both are then covered by the single per-arm normalizer $c_{k,n}=h(n)$ or $v_kn$, which is what
\texttt{estimatorError\_joint\_tendsto\_multivariateGaussian} consumes (at $v\equiv1$). The split is
unavoidable: not every arm can be forced-exploration-fed, since $\sum_kN_{n,k}=n$ while
$K\,h(n)=o(n)$.

The regularity for a forced-exploration-fed arm comes from a two-sided bound. \emph{Upper}
(\texttt{pullCount\_le\_sched\_of\_fe\_only}): at a forced-exploration round the selected arm is
itself under-explored, so one pull leaves it at $h(m)+1\le h(n)+1$. \emph{Lower}
(\texttt{pullCount\_ge\_min\_sched\_of\_fe}): the selected arm is a \emph{least-sampled}
under-explored arm, hence sits at the global minimum, so the potential
$D(m)=\sum_j(L-N_{m,j})^+$ drops by exactly one per round while the minimum stays below $L$; since
$D\le K L$ this can persist for at most $KL$ rounds, so within any longer window the minimum has
reached $L$ or forced exploration stopped firing (which already means every count exceeds $h$). This
is the same potential-function device as Lemma~\ref{lem:fe_no_starvation}. A mild regularity of $h$
itself is assumed (\texttt{hshift}: shifting the argument by the $O(h(n))$ catch-up window does not
change $h$ to first order), satisfied by $h(n)=(n^{1/3}-K/2)^+$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean split of arms by FE-feeding

nodes.name: Lean declaration
nodes.statement: \texttt{AlphaRAR.aRTSFE\_sparse\_clt}.
nodes.statement_short: Lean declaration

nodes.name: Split arms by whether they are fed only by forced exploration
nodes.statement:
Arms are split by a predicate
$\mathrm{FEfed}$:
\begin{itemize}
  \item if arm $k$ is eventually fed \emph{only} by forced exploration, then its count is regular
    against the \emph{deterministic} schedule, $N_{n,k}/h(n)\to1$
    (\texttt{AlphaRAR.pullCount\_div\_sched\_tendsto\_one});
  \item otherwise arm $k$ has a positive limiting proportion $v_k>0$ with $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$, so it
    is regular against $v_kn$.
nodes.statement_short: Split arms by whether they are fed only by forced exploration

nodes.name: FE-fed arm regular against the schedule
nodes.statement_short: FE-fed arm regular against the schedule

nodes.name: Other arms regular against v_k n
nodes.statement:
otherwise arm $k$ has a positive limiting proportion $v_k>0$ with $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$, so it
    is regular against $v_kn$.
nodes.statement_short: Other arms regular against v_k n

nodes.name: Single per-arm normalizer; split unavoidable
nodes.statement:
Both are then covered by the single per-arm normalizer $c_{k,n}=h(n)$ or $v_kn$, which is what
\texttt{estimatorError\_joint\_tendsto\_multivariateGaussian} consumes (at $v\equiv1$). The split is
unavoidable: not every arm can be forced-exploration-fed, since $\sum_kN_{n,k}=n$ while
$K\,h(n)=o(n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Single per-arm normalizer; split unavoidable

nodes.name: Two-sided bound for FE-fed arms
nodes.statement:
The regularity for a forced-exploration-fed arm comes from a two-sided bound. \emph{Upper}
(\texttt{pullCount\_le\_sched\_of\_fe\_only}): at a forced-exploration round the selected arm is
itself under-explored, so one pull leaves it at $h(m)+1\le h(n)+1$. \emph{Lower}
(\texttt{pullCount\_ge\_min\_sched\_of\_fe}): the selected arm is a \emph{least-sampled}
under-explored arm, hence sits at the global minimum, so the potential
$D(m)=\sum_j(L-N_{m,j})^+$ drops by exactly one per round while the minimum stays below $L$; since
$D\le K L$ this can persist for at most $KL$ rounds, so within any longer window the minimum has
reached $L$ or forced exploration stopped firing (which already means every count exceeds $h$). This
is the same potential-function device as Lemma~\ref{lem:fe_no_starvation}. A mild regularity of $h$
itself is assumed (\texttt{hshift}: shifting the argument by the $O(h(n))$ catch-up window does not
change $h$ to first order), satisfied by $h(n)=(n^{1/3}-K/2)^+$.
nodes.statement_short: Two-sided bound for FE-fed arms

nodes.name: Upper bound on the count
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound on the count

nodes.name: Lower bound via the potential function
nodes.statement:
\emph{Lower}
(\texttt{pullCount\_ge\_min\_sched\_of\_fe}): the selected arm is a \emph{least-sampled}
under-explored arm, hence sits at the global minimum, so the potential
$D(m)=\sum_j(L-N_{m,j})^+$ drops by exactly one per round while the minimum stays below $L$; since
$D\le K L$ this can persist for at most $KL$ rounds, so within any longer window the minimum has
reached $L$ or forced exploration stopped firing (which already means every count exceeds $h$). This
is the same potential-function device as Lemma~\ref{lem:fe_no_starvation}. A mild regularity of $h$
itself is assumed (\texttt{hshift}: shifting the argument by the $O(h(n))$ catch-up window does not
change $h$ to first order), satisfied by $h(n)=(n^{1/3}-K/2)^+$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound via the potential function

nodes.name: Standardized Y_n is asymptotically standard normal
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:componentwise}, $\frac{1}{\sqrt{\theta(1-\theta)}}Y_n
\eqdist\mathcal{N}(0,I_K)$ (Bernoulli variance $V_k=\theta(1-\theta)$ under
$\mathcal{H}_0$).
nodes.statement_short: Standardized Y_n is asymptotically standard normal

nodes.name: Weights converge to a rank K-1 projection
nodes.statement:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:LLN}, $\tilde{\theta}_n\to\theta$ and
$s_n\to s=(\sqrt{v_1},\dots,\sqrt{v_K})$, so $I-s_ns_n^\top\to I-ss^\top$, an
orthogonal projection of rank $K-1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:projection}.
nodes.statement_short: Weights converge to a rank K-1 projection

nodes.name: Slutsky gives the chi-square limit
nodes.statement:
Slutsky's
lemma and Lemma~\ref{lem:pearson_quadform} give
$\mathcal{X}_n\eqdist Z^\top(I-ss^\top)Z$ with $Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I_K)$, which is
$\chi^2_{K-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Slutsky gives the chi-square limit

nodes.name: Taylor formula with integral remainder
nodes.statement:
Apply the mean-value / Taylor formula to $t \mapsto f(y + t(x-y))$ on $[0,1]$:
$f(x) - f(y) - \mathrm{D}f(y)(x-y)
= \int_0^1 (1-t)\, \mathrm{D}^2 f(y + t(x-y))[x-y, x-y]\, dt$, and bound the
integrand by $C\|x-y\|^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Taylor formula with integral remainder

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.norm\_sub\_fderiv\_le\_mul\_sq} states the equivalent bound
$\|f(x)-f(y)-\mathrm{D}f(y)(x-y)\| \le K\|x-y\|^2$ under the (weaker, and here more convenient)
hypothesis that the derivative is $K$-Lipschitz relative to $y$ on a convex set,
$\|\mathrm{D}f(z)-\mathrm{D}f(y)\| \le K\|z-y\|$ --- which the second-derivative bound
$\|\mathrm{D}^2 f\|\le C$ supplies with $K = C$ by the mean value inequality. The proof applies the
mean value inequality \texttt{Convex.norm\_image\_sub\_le\_of\_norm\_hasFDerivWithin\_le'} on the
segment $[y,x]$, where $\|\mathrm{D}f(z)-\mathrm{D}f(y)\|\le K\|z-y\|\le K\|x-y\|$ gives the constant.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes

nodes.name: Lean form via Lipschitz derivative
nodes.statement:
\texttt{AlphaRAR.norm\_sub\_fderiv\_le\_mul\_sq} states the equivalent bound
$\|f(x)-f(y)-\mathrm{D}f(y)(x-y)\| \le K\|x-y\|^2$ under the (weaker, and here more convenient)
hypothesis that the derivative is $K$-Lipschitz relative to $y$ on a convex set,
$\|\mathrm{D}f(z)-\mathrm{D}f(y)\| \le K\|z-y\|$ --- which the second-derivative bound
$\|\mathrm{D}^2 f\|\le C$ supplies with $K = C$ by the mean value inequality.
nodes.statement_short: Lean form via Lipschitz derivative

nodes.name: Mean value inequality on the segment
nodes.statement:
The proof applies the
mean value inequality \texttt{Convex.norm\_image\_sub\_le\_of\_norm\_hasFDerivWithin\_le'} on the
segment $[y,x]$, where $\|\mathrm{D}f(z)-\mathrm{D}f(y)\|\le K\|z-y\|\le K\|x-y\|$ gives the constant.
nodes.statement_short: Mean value inequality on the segment

nodes.name: Identity-weight special case
nodes.statement:
This is the special case $b_k = k$ of Kronecker's lemma, which is the only case used below
(Theorem~\ref{thm:mart_slln}).
nodes.statement_short: Identity-weight special case

nodes.name: Summation by parts
nodes.statement:
Write $s_n = \sum_{k<n} x_k \to s$. Summation by parts
(\texttt{Finset.sum\_range\_by\_parts}) gives
$\sum_{k<n} k\,x_k = (n-1)s_n - \sum_{k<n} s_k$, so
$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k<n} k\,x_k = \big(1-\tfrac1n\big)s_n - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k<n} s_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Summation by parts

nodes.name: Both terms tend to s
nodes.statement:
The first term tends to $s$ and the second is a Cesàro average of the convergent sequence $(s_n)$,
hence also tends to $s$ (\texttt{Filter.Tendsto.cesaro}); the difference tends to $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Both terms tend to s

nodes.name: Summation by parts
nodes.statement:
Summation by parts: with $S_n=\sum_{k<n}y_k$,
$\sum_{k<n} b_{k+1}y_k = b_n S_n - \sum_{k<n-1}(b_{k+2}-b_{k+1})S_{k+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Summation by parts

nodes.name: Toeplitz weighted average
nodes.statement:
Dividing by $b_n$, the first
term is $S_n\to s$; the second is a Toeplitz-weighted average of the convergent sequence
$(S_{k+1})$ with nonnegative weights $(b_{k+2}-b_{k+1})/b_n$ summing to $(b_n-b_1)/b_n\to1$, each
tending to $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Toeplitz weighted average

nodes.name: Split at a threshold to conclude
nodes.statement:
Writing $S_{k+1}=s+\varepsilon_k$ with $\varepsilon_k\to0$ and splitting the sum at a
threshold beyond which $|\varepsilon_k|<\delta$, the weighted average tends to $s$; the difference
tends to $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Split at a threshold to conclude

nodes.name: Block Borel-Cantelli argument
nodes.statement:
Fix $\eta>1$ and set $v_k = \eta^k$. Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_bc} with
$\lambda_k=(1+\varepsilon)\sqrt{2v_k\log\log v_k}$: the tail bounds
$\exp(-\lambda_k^2/(4v_k))$ are summable in $k$, so a.s.\ only finitely many blocks are
bad. On the block $\{\langle M\rangle_n\in(v_{k-1},v_k]\}$ this yields
$M_n < \lambda_k \le C\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\log\log\langle M\rangle_n}$; letting
$\eta\downarrow1$ and $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ yields the $\limsup$ bound.
nodes.statement_short: Block Borel-Cantelli argument

nodes.name: Formalized dyadic-block form at the log rate
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Formalization status.} The formalized statement
\texttt{AlphaRAR.ae\_eventually\_forall\_lt\_dyadic} is the dyadic-block form: with the schedule
$v_k=2^k$ and $\lambda_k = K\sqrt{v_k(k+1)}$ (where $0<K$ and $Kc\le2$, so admissibility
$\lambda_k c\le 2v_k$ holds for \emph{every} $k$ via $k+1\le 2^k$, and the tail bounds
$\exp(-\lambda_k^2/(4v_k))=\exp(-K^2(k+1)/4)$ form a geometric series), almost surely for all
large $k$ and every $n$, $\langle M\rangle_n\le 2^k \Rightarrow M_n < K\sqrt{2^k(k+1)}$. This is
the complete probabilistic content, built from Ville's inequality, the optimized Freedman bound
(Corollary~\ref{cor:lil_freedman_opt}), and Borel--Cantelli (Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_bc}). Since on the
block $\langle M\rangle_n\in(2^{k-1},2^k]$ one has $\sqrt{2^k(k+1)}\asymp
\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\log\langle M\rangle_n}$, it gives the displayed
$O(\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\log\langle M\rangle_n})$ upper bound, formalized in
Corollary~\ref{cor:lil_upper} below. One deliberate deviation from the displayed statement remains
unformalized: the $\log\log$ (rather than $\log$) rate with sharp constant $1$, which would require
refining the one-step MGF bound $e^x\le1+x+x^2$ to variance proxy $1$ (valid only as the increment
$\to0$). The $\log$ rate already gives $M_n=o(\langle M\rangle_n)$, which suffices for all
downstream uses.
nodes.statement_short: Formalized dyadic-block form at the log rate

nodes.name: Variance decomposition
nodes.statement: $v_i=\E[(\xi_i^{\mathrm t})^2]-m_i^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Variance decomposition

nodes.name: Limits of the second moment and the mean
nodes.statement:
As $\sqrt i\to\infty$, $\E[(\xi_i^{\mathrm t})^2]
=\int\operatorname{trunc}(x-\theta_k,\sqrt i)^2\,d\nu_k\to\int(x-\theta_k)^2\,d\nu_k=\sigma^2$
by monotone/dominated convergence, and $m_i\to0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:trunc_mean_bound}), so
$v_i\to\sigma^2$. The upper bound $v_i\le\sigma^2$ is immediate from
$|\operatorname{trunc}(\xi_i,\sqrt i)|\le|\xi_i|$.
nodes.statement_short: Limits of the second moment and the mean

nodes.name: Freedman on the stopped martingale
nodes.statement:
Apply the Freedman inequality (Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_freedman}) to the martingale stopped at time
$2^k$ --- whose increments are bounded by $c_k=2\sqrt{2^k}$, so $\theta_k c_k=1$ is admissible ---
with $\theta=\theta_k$, $\lambda=\lambda_k$, $v=\sigma^2 2^k$.
nodes.statement_short: Freedman on the stopped martingale
nodes.section: 12.3.4 Core: the growing-increment LIL for $\tilde M$

nodes.name: Compute the exponent
