nodes.statement:
The exponent is
$-\theta_k\lambda_k+\theta_k^2\sigma^2 2^k=-\tfrac C2\sqrt k+\tfrac{\sigma^2}4$, since
$\theta_k\lambda_k=\tfrac{C\sqrt{2^k k}}{2\sqrt{2^k}}=\tfrac C2\sqrt k$ and
$\theta_k^2\sigma^2 2^k=\tfrac{\sigma^2 2^k}{4\cdot2^k}=\tfrac{\sigma^2}4$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute the exponent
nodes.section: 12.3.4 Core: the growing-increment LIL for $\tilde M$

nodes.name: Why stopping is needed
nodes.statement:
Stopping at $2^k$ is
needed so the increment bound holds up to the horizon; on the event only times $m\le 2^k$ occur,
where the stopped process agrees with $\tilde M$.
nodes.statement_short: Why stopping is needed
nodes.section: 12.3.4 Core: the growing-increment LIL for $\tilde M$

nodes.name: Lean horizon-local Freedman device
nodes.statement:
The formalization packages the stopping into a reusable device
\texttt{AlphaRAR.measure\_exists\_ge\_le\_exp\_horizon}: a version of the pre-optimization Freedman
bound (Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_freedman}) whose increment bound $|\Delta M_i|\le c$ is required only for
$i<N$, and whose event is restricted to $m\le N$. It is proved by applying
Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_freedman} to the deterministically stopped process
$M^N_m:=M_{\min(m,N)}$ (Mathlib's \texttt{stoppedProcess} at the constant time $N$), which is a martingale
(\texttt{martingale\_stoppedProcess\_const}), whose increments vanish past $N$ hence are globally bounded by
$c$, and whose predictable quadratic variation agrees with $\langle M\rangle$ below the horizon
(\texttt{predQuadVar\_stoppedProcess\_const\_of\_le}). Here it is used with $N=2^k$, $c=c_k=2\sqrt{2^k}$, the
constrained $\theta_k=1/c_k$, and the increment bound $|\Delta\tilde M_i|\le2\sqrt i\le c_k$ for
$i<2^k$ (\texttt{abs\_truncRespMart\_increment\_le}).
nodes.statement_short: Lean horizon-local Freedman device
nodes.section: 12.3.4 Core: the growing-increment LIL for $\tilde M$

nodes.name: Block Borel-Cantelli and repackaging
nodes.statement:
Borel--Cantelli over the blocks (Lemmas~\ref{lem:trunc_block}--\ref{lem:trunc_block_summable})
gives that a.s.\ for all large $k$ and every $m\le 2^k$, $\langle\tilde M\rangle_m\le\sigma^2 2^k
\Rightarrow \tilde M_m<\lambda_k$ (formalized as
\texttt{ae\_eventually\_truncRespMart\_lt\_block}, the summable first Borel--Cantelli step). To
bound a fixed time $n$, take the \emph{least} $k$ with $n\le 2^k$; then $2^k\le 2n$ and
$k\le\log_2 n+1$, and the quadratic-variation bound $\langle\tilde M\rangle_n\le V_k N_{n,k}\le V_k
n\le V_k 2^k$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:trunc_qv_le}) supplies the block hypothesis at $m=n\le 2^k$, giving
$\tilde M_n<\lambda_k=C\sqrt{2^k k}\le C'\sqrt{n\log n}$.
nodes.statement_short: Block Borel-Cantelli and repackaging
nodes.section: 12.3.4 Core: the growing-increment LIL for $\tilde M$

nodes.name: Time scale versus variance scale
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Scale.} Because the increment bound $|\Delta\tilde M_i|\le2\sqrt i$ \emph{grows}, the block
horizon $m\le 2^k$ forces the least admissible $k$ to satisfy $2^k\ge n$, so time-blocking delivers
the \emph{time} scale $O(\sqrt{n\log n})$ rather than the variance scale
$O(\sqrt{\langle\tilde M\rangle_n\log\langle\tilde M\rangle_n})=O(\sqrt{N_n\log N_n})$ of the
displayed statement. The two coincide when arm $k$ is sampled a positive fraction of the time
($N_{n,k}\asymp n$, the regime of interest); the sharper variance-scale bound would require blocking
by the quadratic variation rather than by the natural time, and is not formalized. The time-scale
form is exactly parallel to the bounded-increment Corollary~\ref{cor:lil_upper_nat}
(\texttt{ae\_eventually\_le\_sqrt\_nat\_mul\_log}).
nodes.statement_short: Time scale versus variance scale
nodes.section: 12.3.4 Core: the growing-increment LIL for $\tilde M$

nodes.name: Decompose M
nodes.statement: By Definition~\ref{def:lil_trunc}, $M_n=\tilde M_n+R_n+\mathrm{Dr}_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose M

nodes.name: Bound the three pieces
nodes.statement:
The main term is
$O(\sqrt{n\log n})$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:trunc_mart_lil}); the tail is $O(1)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:trunc_tail_const}); the drift is $O(\sqrt{n})$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:trunc_drift}).
nodes.statement_short: Bound the three pieces

nodes.name: Remainders are negligible
nodes.statement: Both remainders are $o(\sqrt{n\log n})$, so $M_n=O(\sqrt{n\log n})$.
nodes.statement_short: Remainders are negligible

nodes.name: Relation to the variance scale
nodes.statement:
In the regime of interest
$N_{n,k}\asymp n$, this is the $O(\sqrt{N_n\log N_n})=O(\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\log\langle
M\rangle_n})$ rate (using $\langle M\rangle_n=\sigma^2 N_n$) required downstream.
nodes.statement_short: Relation to the variance scale

nodes.name: Per-block bounds
nodes.statement:
As in Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_bc}, for indices $k$ where admissibility holds the optimized
Freedman bound (Corollary~\ref{cor:lil_freedman_opt}, infinite-horizon form
\texttt{measure\_exists\_ge\_le\_exp\_all}) gives
$\Prob(s_k)\le\exp(-\lambda_k^2/(4v_k))$, where
$s_k=\{\exists n:\ M_n\ge\lambda_k,\ \langle M\rangle_n\le v_k\}$; for the finitely many
remaining $k$ use the trivial bound $\Prob(s_k)\le1$.
nodes.statement_short: Per-block bounds

nodes.name: Borel-Cantelli
nodes.statement:
The total $\sum_k\Prob(s_k)$ is
still finite, so the first Borel--Cantelli lemma (\texttt{ae\_eventually\_notMem})
places a.e.\ $\omega$ in only finitely many $s_k$; the complement is the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Borel-Cantelli

nodes.name: Relation to the earlier lemma
nodes.statement:
This is
Lemma~\ref{lem:lil_bc} with its ``$\forall k$'' admissibility weakened to
``$\forall^\infty k$''.
nodes.statement_short: Relation to the earlier lemma

nodes.name: Eventual admissibility
nodes.statement:
Eventual admissibility: $\lambda_k c\le 2v_k$ reads
$\kappa c\sqrt{\log\log\eta^k/\eta^k}\le2$, which holds for large $k$ because
$\log\log\eta^k/\eta^k\to0$ (in the formalization, $\lambda_k c\le2\cdot2^k$ reduces to
$(\kappa c)^2\log(k+2)\le4\cdot2^k$, eventual since $\log(k+2)=o(2^k)$).
nodes.statement_short: Eventual admissibility

nodes.name: Summability by the p-series lemma
nodes.statement:
Summability:
$\exp(-\lambda_k^2/(4v_k))=\exp(-\tfrac{\kappa^2}{4}\log\log\eta^k)$ is summable by
Lemma~\ref{lem:llil_tail_summable}.
nodes.statement_short: Summability by the p-series lemma

nodes.name: Apply the Borel-Cantelli lemma
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:llil_evt_adm}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Borel-Cantelli lemma

nodes.name: Choose block parameters
nodes.statement:
Pick $\eta>1$ and $\kappa\in(2,C/\sqrt\eta)$ (possible once $\eta<(C/2)^2$), and use
Lemma~\ref{lem:llil_bounded_block}.
nodes.statement_short: Choose block parameters

nodes.name: Repackage via the least block
nodes.statement:
For large $n$ let $k$ be the least index with
$\langle M\rangle_n\le\eta^k$; minimality gives $\eta^k\le\eta\langle M\rangle_n$, and
$\langle M\rangle_n\to\infty$ makes $\log\log\eta^k\le\log\log(\eta\langle M\rangle_n)
\le(1+o(1))\log\log\langle M\rangle_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Repackage via the least block

nodes.name: Conclude the bound
nodes.statement:
Hence
$M_n<\kappa\sqrt{\eta^k\log\log\eta^k}\le\kappa\sqrt\eta\,(1+o(1))
\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n\log\log\langle M\rangle_n}\le C\sqrt{\langle M\rangle_n
\log\log\langle M\rangle_n}$ for large $n$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the bound

nodes.name: tau is a stopping time
nodes.statement:
Predictability of $\langle M\rangle$ gives $\{\tau_v\ge n+1\}=\{\langle M\rangle_{n+1}
\le v\}\in\filt_n$, so $\tau_v$ is a stopping time (constructible with Mathlib's
\texttt{hittingBtwn}, the stopping-time API already used in the proof of Ville's
inequality).
nodes.statement_short: tau is a stopping time
nodes.section: 13.2 The general hypothesis: small increments on the LIL scale

nodes.name: Stopped martingale and increment bound
nodes.statement:
That $M^{\tau_v}$ is a martingale is Mathlib's
\texttt{Submartingale.stoppedProcess} applied to $\pm M$; the increment bound uses
monotonicity of $\langle M\rangle$ and \textbf{(H)}.
nodes.statement_short: Stopped martingale and increment bound
nodes.section: 13.2 The general hypothesis: small increments on the LIL scale

nodes.name: New quadratic-variation identity
nodes.statement:
The only genuinely new ingredient is
the quadratic-variation identity $\langle M^{\tau_v}\rangle=\langle M\rangle_{\cdot\wedge
\tau_v}$, the stopping-time analogue of the \emph{formalized} deterministic-horizon
\texttt{predQuadVar\_stoppedProcess\_const\_of\_le} of Chapter~\ref{chap:pre_lil}.
nodes.statement_short: New quadratic-variation identity
nodes.section: 13.2 The general hypothesis: small increments on the LIL scale

nodes.name: Event inclusion
nodes.statement:
For the inclusion: if
$\langle M\rangle_n\le v$ then $n\le\tau_v$, so $M^{\tau_v}_n=M_n$ and
$\langle M^{\tau_v}\rangle_n=\langle M\rangle_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Event inclusion
nodes.section: 13.2 The general hypothesis: small increments on the LIL scale

nodes.name: Stop and bound increments
nodes.statement:
Stop at $\tau_{v_k}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:llil_qv_stop}); the stopped increments are bounded
by $C(v_k)=A\sqrt{v_k/\log\log v_k}$ (or by the fixed $c$).
nodes.statement_short: Stop and bound increments

nodes.name: Admissibility of the optimizer
nodes.statement:
The optimizer
$\theta_k=\lambda_k/((1+\delta)v_k)=\sqrt{2(1+\varepsilon)\log\log v_k/v_k}/(1+\delta)$
satisfies $\theta_k C(v_k)=A\sqrt{2(1+\varepsilon)}/(1+\delta)$, which is $\le\eta_\delta$
for $A$ small (bounded case: $\theta_k c\to0$).
nodes.statement_short: Admissibility of the optimizer

nodes.name: Summable bounds and Borel-Cantelli
nodes.statement:
Lemma~\ref{lem:llil_refined_freedman}
gives $\Prob(s_k)\le\exp(-\lambda_k^2/(2(1+\delta)v_k))
=\exp(-\tfrac{1+\varepsilon}{1+\delta}\log\log v_k)$, summable by
Lemma~\ref{lem:llil_tail_summable}'s argument since $(1+\varepsilon)/(1+\delta)>1$.
Borel--Cantelli finishes.
nodes.statement_short: Summable bounds and Borel-Cantelli

nodes.name: Sharp block lemma for a countable parameter family
nodes.statement:
Fix a countable family $\eta_j\downarrow1$, $\varepsilon_j\downarrow0$ with
$\varepsilon_j>\delta_j>0$. For each $j$, Lemma~\ref{lem:llil_sharp_block} and the
repackaging of Theorem~\ref{thm:llil_bounded} give, a.s.,
$\limsup_n M_n/\sqrt{2\langle M\rangle_n\log\log\langle M\rangle_n}\le
\sqrt{(1+\varepsilon_j)\eta_j}$.
nodes.statement_short: Sharp block lemma for a countable parameter family

nodes.name: Intersect and pass to the limit
nodes.statement:
Intersect the countably many a.s.\ events and let
$j\to\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Intersect and pass to the limit

nodes.name: Geometric blocking with refined Freedman bounds
nodes.statement:
Fix $\beta>1$ and block with the geometric horizons $N_j=\lceil\rho^j\rceil$ for
$\rho=1+(\beta-1)/2\downarrow1$ and $\delta=(\beta-1)/2$, so $(1+\delta)\rho=\rho^2<\beta^2$.
Over each block the increments are bounded by $g(N_j)$, and condition \textbf{(H)} transfers
to the block form $g(N_j)\sqrt{\log(j+2)/N_j}\to0$ because
$\log(j+2)\le(\log K+1)\,L(N_j)$ with $K=1/\log\rho+2$ (from $j\le\log N_j/\log\rho$), so the
block quantity is $\le\sqrt{\log K+1}\,g(N_j)\sqrt{L(N_j)/N_j}\to0$. The refined per-block
Freedman bound (Lemma~\ref{lem:llil_sharp_block}) with the near-optimal
$\theta_j=\alpha\sqrt{\log(j+2)/N_j}$, $\alpha=C/((1+\delta)v)$, gives a summable
$p$-series tail; repackaging via the least $j$ with $n\le N_j$ (so $N_j\le\rho n+1$ and
additively $\log(j+2)\le D_\rho+L(n)$) yields the constant $\beta$.
nodes.statement_short: Geometric blocking with refined Freedman bounds

nodes.name: Linear bound replaces random stopping
nodes.statement:
\emph{No random
stopping time}: the linear bound $\langle M\rangle_n\le v\,n$ lets the deterministic horizon
$N_j$ play the role of quadratic-variation stopping (contrast the general \textbf{(H)}
Theorem~\ref{thm:llil_sharp}, whose constant-\textbf{(H)} increments would require it).
nodes.statement_short: Linear bound replaces random stopping

nodes.name: Countable intersection and two-sided step
nodes.statement:
Countable intersection over $\beta_m=1+1/(m+1)\downarrow1$ and the two-sided step (apply to
$-M$) give the $\limsup$ form.
nodes.statement_short: Countable intersection and two-sided step

nodes.name: Adaptedness and integrability
nodes.statement: $S_n$ is $\filt_n$-measurable (a sum of $Y_0,\dots,Y_{n-1}$) and integrable.
nodes.statement_short: Adaptedness and integrability

nodes.name: Independence gives the martingale property
nodes.statement:
For the increment,
$\E[S_{n+1}\mid\filt_n]=S_n+\E[Y_n\mid\filt_n]=S_n+\E Y_n=S_n$, because $Y_n$ is independent of the
past $\filt_n=\sigma(Y_0,\dots,Y_{n-1})$.
nodes.statement_short: Independence gives the martingale property

nodes.name: Lean ingredients and indexing
nodes.statement:
Mathlib's $\log\log$-free
\texttt{condExp\_indep\_eq} supplies $\E[Y_n\mid\filt_n]=\E Y_n$; the ``strictly before'' index is
what makes $S_0=0$ (unlike \texttt{Filtration.natural}, which would force $S_0=Y_0$).
nodes.statement_short: Lean ingredients and indexing

nodes.name: Martingale with linear quadratic variation
nodes.statement_short: Martingale with linear quadratic variation

nodes.name: Apply the bounded-increment LIL
nodes.statement:
The bounded-increment loglog LIL
(Corollary~\ref{cor:llil_nat}) applies directly.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the bounded-increment LIL

nodes.name: Relation to Hartman-Wintner
nodes.statement:
This is the special case of
Theorem~\ref{thm:hw} where no truncation is needed, and is already fully formalized.
nodes.statement_short: Relation to Hartman-Wintner

nodes.name: Increment bound and condition (H)
nodes.statement:
$|\Delta\tilde S_j|=|Y_j^{\mathrm L}-\E Y_j^{\mathrm L}|\le2b_j$
(\texttt{abs\_truncation\_sub\_integral\_le}), with $j\mapsto b_j$ monotone and
nonnegative; the base-independent condition \textbf{(H)} $2b_n\sqrt{L(n)/n}=
2\sqrt{L(n)/\log(n+2)}\to0$ holds because $L(n)/\log(n+2)\to0$.
nodes.statement_short: Increment bound and condition (H)

nodes.name: Linear quadratic-variation bound
nodes.statement:
The martingale $\tilde S$
(\texttt{martingale\_centeredTruncation}) has the linear quadratic-variation bound
$\langle\tilde S\rangle_m\le\sigma^2 m$ (\texttt{predQuadVar\_centeredTruncation\_le}, via
\texttt{integral\_truncation\_sub\_integral\_sq\_le} for $\Var(Y^{\mathrm L})\le\sigma^2$).
nodes.statement_short: Linear quadratic-variation bound

nodes.name: Apply the sharp growing-increment engine
nodes.statement:
These three feed the sharp growing-increment engine
(\texttt{ae\_eventually\_abs\_le\_sqrt\_nat\_mul\_loglog\_of\_growth\_sharp\_all}) with growth
$g=2b$; the block scheme uses deterministic horizons $N_j=\lceil\rho^j\rceil$ with $\rho\downarrow1$,
so \emph{no random stopping time} is needed --- the linear bound $\langle\tilde S\rangle\le\sigma^2 m$
lets a deterministic time horizon play the role of quadratic-variation stopping.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the sharp growing-increment engine

nodes.name: Sharpness remark
nodes.statement:
The upper bound uses
only $\langle\tilde S\rangle_m\le\sigma^2 m$; that $\Var(Y_j^{\mathrm L})\to\sigma^2$ (so
$\langle\tilde S\rangle_m/(\sigma^2 m)\to1$) is not needed for $\limsup\le1$, but confirms the
constant is sharp.
nodes.statement_short: Sharpness remark

nodes.name: Tonelli and inner harmonic sum bound
nodes.statement:
$\Var(Y_j^{\mathrm M})\le\E[(Y_j^{\mathrm M})^2]=\E[Y^2\indic_{\{b_j<|Y|\le\sqrt j\}}]$,
so by Tonelli
\[
  \sum_{j\ge3}\frac{\Var(Y_j^{\mathrm M})}{j\,L(j)}\ \le\
  \E\Big[Y^2\!\!\sum_{j:\,b_j<|Y|\le\sqrt j}\frac{1}{j\,L(j)}\Big].
\]
Fix $y=|Y|$. With the log-level cutoff $b_j=\sqrt{j/\log(j+2)}$ the condition
$b_j<y\le\sqrt j$ means $y^2\le j$ and $j/\log(j+2)<y^2$; as $t\mapsto t/\log(t+2)$ is
increasing the latter is $j<j_0(y)$, where $j_0(y)/\log(j_0(y)+2)=y^2$, so
$j_0(y)\asymp y^2\log(y^2)$. Thus $j$ runs over $[y^2,j_0(y))$, an interval of
multiplicative width $\asymp\log(y^2)$ on which $L(j)\asymp L(y^2)$; hence
\[
  \sum_{y^2\le j<j_0(y)}\frac{1}{j\,L(j)}\ \asymp\
  \frac{1}{L(y^2)}\log\frac{j_0(y)}{y^2}\ \asymp\
  \frac{\log\log(y^2)}{L(y^2)}\ =\ O(1),
\]
bounded uniformly in $y$. The inner factor being bounded, the double sum is
$\le C\,\E[Y^2]<\infty$. The mechanism: the medium band is only a $\log$-factor wide, so
the harmonic inner sum is $O(\log\log/\log\log)=O(1)$; this is exactly where the bare
second moment suffices. (The LIL-scale low cutoff $\sqrt{j/L(j)}$ would make the band a
mere $\log\log$-factor wide and the inner sum $\to0$; the log-level cutoff trades that
slack for the sharp-constant condition \textbf{(H)}$\to0$ of the low part, and $O(1)$
still gives convergence.)
nodes.statement_short: Tonelli and inner harmonic sum bound

nodes.name: Lean inner-sum bound and wrapper
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} Both the analytic heart and the measure-theoretic wrapper are formalized.
The uniform inner-sum bound $\sum_{j:\,t\le j<t\log(j+2)}1/(j\,L(j))\le C$ (with $t=y^2$) is
\texttt{AlphaRAR.medium\_inner\_tsum\_le}, built from \texttt{AlphaRAR.medium\_sum\_Icc\_big} (the
$t\ge9$ estimate: pull out $1/L(\lceil t\rceil)$ and bound the harmonic sum by
$\log(B/A)\le\log(5\log t)=\log5+L(t)$) via the range bounds \texttt{medium\_crude} ($j<8t^2$) and
\texttt{medium\_tight} ($j<t(\log9+2\log t)$), the harmonic comparison
\texttt{sum\_Icc\_one\_div\_le}, and \texttt{loglog\_le\_loglog}. The wrapper
\texttt{AlphaRAR.medium\_variance\_series\_le} turns it into the second-moment series: by finite-sum
linearity $\sum_{j<n}\big(\int X^2\indic_{\{b_j<|X|\le\sqrt j\}}\big)/(j\,L(j))=\int X^2\sum_{j<n}
\indic_{\{\dots\}}/(j\,L(j))$, the inner sum is $\le C$ pointwise (at $t=X(\omega)^2$, using
$b_j<|x|\le\sqrt j\iff x^2\le j<x^2\log(j+2)$), so each partial sum is $\le C\,\E[X^2]$ and
$\sum'_j(\dots)\le C\,\E[X^2]$ with the series summable. The reduction
$\Var(X\indic_{\{b_j<|X|\le\sqrt j\}})\le\E[(X\indic_{\{\dots\}})^2]=\E[X^2\indic_{\{\dots\}}]$
(\texttt{variance\_le\_expectation\_sq}, $(X\indic_S)^2=X^2\indic_S$) plus comparison of nonnegative
series (\texttt{Summable.of\_nonneg\_of\_le}) gives \texttt{AlphaRAR.medium\_variance\_summable}:
$\sum_{j\ge3}\Var(X\indic_{\{b_j<|X|\le\sqrt j\}})/(j\,L(j))<\infty$. Taking $X=Y_0$ and using
$\Var(Y_j^{\mathrm M})=\Var(Y_0\indic_{\{b_j<|Y_0|\le\sqrt j\}})$ (identical distribution) is the
stated series.
nodes.statement_short: Lean inner-sum bound and wrapper

nodes.name: Weighted partial sums form an L2-bounded martingale
nodes.statement:
Put $a_j:=\sqrt{2\,j\,L(j)}$, positive nondecreasing with $a_j\to\infty$. The partial
sums of the independent, mean-zero terms $(Y_j^{\mathrm M}-\E Y_j^{\mathrm M})/a_{j+1}$
form an $L^2$-bounded martingale, since by independence and Lemma~\ref{lem:hw_medium_var}
\[
  \int\Big(\sum_{j<n}\tfrac{Y_j^{\mathrm M}-\E Y_j^{\mathrm M}}{a_{j+1}}\Big)^2
  =\sum_{j<n}\frac{\Var(Y_j^{\mathrm M})}{a_{j+1}^2}
  \le\tfrac12\sum_{j}\frac{\Var(Y_j^{\mathrm M})}{j\,L(j)}<\infty .
\]
nodes.statement_short: Weighted partial sums form an L2-bounded martingale

nodes.name: Convergence plus Kronecker
nodes.statement:
Hence $\sum_j(Y_j^{\mathrm M}-\E Y_j^{\mathrm M})/a_{j+1}$ converges a.s.\ by the $L^2$
martingale convergence theorem (Lemma~\ref{lem:slln_l2_conv}), and Kronecker's lemma with
weights $b_j=a_j$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:kronecker_general}, whose conclusion
$a_m^{-1}\sum_{j<m}a_{j+1}y_j\to0$ with $y_j=(Y_j^{\mathrm M}-\E Y_j^{\mathrm M})/a_{j+1}$
is exactly $a_m^{-1}\sum_{j<m}(Y_j^{\mathrm M}-\E Y_j^{\mathrm M})\to0$) gives
$W_m=o(a_m)=o(\sqrt{m\,L(m)})$ a.s.
nodes.statement_short: Convergence plus Kronecker

nodes.name: Pattern of the martingale SLLN
nodes.statement:
This is the Kolmogorov-convergence-plus-Kronecker
pattern of the martingale SLLN (Chapter~\ref{chap:pre_slln}); both ingredients are
already formalized.
nodes.statement_short: Pattern of the martingale SLLN

nodes.name: Bound each truncated mean
nodes.statement:
Each summand $\E[Y_j\indic_{\{|Y_j|\le\sqrt j\}}]$ is the mean of the truncation of the
centred $Y_j$ at level $\sqrt j$, so the already-formalized centred truncated-mean bound
$|\!\int\operatorname{trunc}(X,A)|\le\E[X^2]/A$
(\texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_integral\_truncation\_le}, about Mathlib's
\texttt{MeasureTheory.truncation}) gives $|\E[Y_j\indic_{\{|Y_j|\le\sqrt j\}}]|\le
\sigma^2/\sqrt j$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound each truncated mean

nodes.name: Sum the bounds
nodes.statement:
Summing with $\sum_{j\le m}1/\sqrt j\le2\sqrt m$
(\texttt{AlphaRAR.sum\_one\_div\_sqrt\_le}, also formalized) gives $|D_m|\le2\sigma^2
\sqrt m$; and $\sqrt m/\sqrt{m\,L(m)}\to0$, so $D_m=o(\sqrt{m\,L(m)})$.
nodes.statement_short: Sum the bounds

nodes.name: Same bounds as the log-rate route
nodes.statement:
Both cited bounds
are exactly those used for the drift in the existing (log-rate) truncation route
(Lemmas~\ref{lem:trunc_mean_bound}--\ref{lem:trunc_drift}), applied here at level
$\sqrt j$ instead of $\sqrt i$.
nodes.statement_short: Same bounds as the log-rate route

nodes.name: Decompose and bound each part
nodes.statement:
By Definition~\ref{def:hw_trunc}, $S_m=\tilde S_m+W_m+H_m+D_m$, and the three remainders
are $o(\sqrt{m\,L(m)})$: $H_m=O(1)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:hw_high}), $W_m=o(\sqrt{m\,L(m)})$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:hw_medium}) and $D_m=o(\sqrt m)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:hw_drift}). Hence
$\limsup_m S_m/\sqrt{2\sigma^2 m\,L(m)}=\limsup_m\tilde S_m/\sqrt{2\sigma^2 m\,L(m)}\le1$
by the sharp low-part bound (Lemma~\ref{lem:hw_low_H}). No $A_0\to0$ limit (as in
de~Acosta's LIL-scale truncation) is needed: the log-level cutoff $b_j\to\infty$ already
gives $\Var(Y_j^{\mathrm L})\to\sigma^2$, so the constant is sharp. The two-sided statement
applies this to $-Y$.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose and bound each part

nodes.name: Lean handling of the boundary atom and coboundedness
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization} (\texttt{AlphaRAR.iid\_hartmanWintner\_limsup\_le\_one}). Because Mathlib's
\texttt{truncation} is half-open $(-b_j,b_j]$, the pointwise identity $Y_j=Y_j^{\mathrm L}+
Y_j^{\mathrm M}+Y_j^{\mathrm H}$ fails only at the single boundary atom $\{Y_j=-b_j\}$, where the
uncovered mass is $-b_j\le0$; \emph{dropping} it gives the one-sided pointwise bound $Y_j\le
Y_j^{\mathrm L}+Y_j^{\mathrm M}+Y_j\indic_{\{|Y_j|>\sqrt j\}}$ (\texttt{le\_lowMedHigh}), enough for the
upper half. The drift picks up the atom in expectation, controlled by $\sum_j b_j\,\Prob(Y_j=-b_j)\le
\E|Y_0|<\infty$ (\texttt{sum\_atom\_le}, using that the distinct $-b_j$ index disjoint events).
A coboundedness-free core (\texttt{hw\_eventually}) proves ``a.s.\ $\forall\beta>1$ eventually
$S_m\le\beta\sqrt{2\sigma^2 m\,L(m)}$''; applying it to $-Y$ gives the matching lower bound
$S_m\ge-\beta\sqrt{2\sigma^2 m\,L(m)}$, which supplies the coboundedness needed to pass to the
$\limsup$. The nondegeneracy $\sigma^2>0$ is used so the weight is eventually positive.
nodes.statement_short: Lean handling of the boundary atom and coboundedness

nodes.name: Product formula by induction over pulls
nodes.statement:
The classical optional-skipping argument, with the selector $D_j=\indic_{\{A_j=k\}}$. Decompose over
the value $j$ of the $m$-th pull time $\tau_m$: the event $\{\tau_m=j\}$ coincides a.s.\ with the
predictable hit event $\{N_j=m,\ A_j=k\}$ (where $N_j=\#\{i<j:A_i=k\}$), which is measurable for the
action-augmented $\sigma$-algebra at time $j$, and on it the conditional law of $Y_j$ is the constant
$\nu_k$ (\texttt{condExp\_feedback}). Hence, for any prefix and measurable sets $E_i$,
$\Prob\!\big(\bigcap_{i<N}Y_{\tau_i}^{-1}E_i\big)=\prod_{i<N}\nu_k(E_i)$ by induction on $N$, peeling
the newest sample and summing over its a.s.-covering, pairwise-disjoint pull events; this is
independence together with each marginal $=\nu_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Product formula by induction over pulls
nodes.section: 13.6 Optional skipping and the response martingale

nodes.name: Lean generic sampled-sequence result
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} The combinatorial core is generic (\texttt{AlphaRAR.iIndepFun\_sampledSeq},
\texttt{map\_sampledSeq\_eq}): for a predictable $\{0,1\}$-selector $D$ and a process $Y$ whose value
is $\rho$-fresh given the current $\sigma$-algebra on $\{D_j=1\}$
(\texttt{hfact}: $\mu(Y_j^{-1}E\cap S)=\rho(E)\,\mu(S)$ for $S\subseteq\{D_j=1\}$), the samples at the
hit times of $D$ are i.i.d.\ $\rho$. The hit time $\tau_m$ is \texttt{Nat.nth}, and the honestly
$\sigma$-algebra-measurable hit events replace the (absent from Mathlib) random stopping-time
$\sigma$-algebra. The freshness \texttt{hfact} is discharged for the response process
(\texttt{hfact\_stationaryEnv}) from the stationary-environment conditional distribution. This
general statement is not yet in Mathlib and is a worthwhile contribution.
nodes.statement_short: Lean generic sampled-sequence result
nodes.section: 13.6 Optional skipping and the response martingale

nodes.name: Reindex and apply Hartman-Wintner
nodes.statement:
Reindexing the nonzero summands, $\sum_{j<n}D_j(Y_j-\theta_k)=S_{N_n}$ with
$S_m:=\sum_{i<m}(Y_{\tau_i}-\theta_k)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:opt_skip} the $(Y_{\tau_i})$ are i.i.d.\ with
law $\nu_k$, so $S$ is an i.i.d.\ centred sum with variance $V$; since $N_n\to\infty$ a.s.,
Theorem~\ref{thm:hw} (two-sided) gives $|S_{N_n}|=O(\sqrt{N_n\log\log N_n})$.
nodes.statement_short: Reindex and apply Hartman-Wintner
nodes.section: 13.6 Optional skipping and the response martingale

nodes.name: Lean sharp two-sided form
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization} (\texttt{AlphaRAR.abs\_respMart\_le\_sqrt\_nat\_mul\_loglog}). The formalized
statement is the sharp two-sided form: a.s., for every $\beta>1$, eventually
$|Q_{n,k}|\le\beta\sqrt{2V\,N_{n,k}\log\log N_{n,k}}$. The reindexing $Q_{n,k}=S_{N_{n,k}}$
(\texttt{respMart\_eq\_sum\_sampledSeq}) is an exact pointwise identity proved by induction on $n$
(a pull advances the sample rank via \texttt{Nat.nth\_count}). Hartman--Wintner is applied through
the coboundedness-free \emph{eventually} core (\texttt{hw\_eventually}) to the centred samples and
their negatives; the time-change $N_{n,k}\to\infty$ (\texttt{hitCount\_tendsto\_atTop}) transports
the eventual bound. The i.i.d.\ hypotheses and law $\nu_k$ of the samples come from
Lemma~\ref{lem:opt_skip}; the moments are transported to $\nu_k$ by change of variables. Requires
$\int x\,d\nu_k$, $\int x^2\,d\nu_k$ finite and $V=\Var(\nu_k)>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean sharp two-sided form
nodes.section: 13.6 Optional skipping and the response martingale

nodes.name: Integral tower
nodes.statement:
Both bounds follow from a short integral tower for the map $x\mapsto e^{ix}$,
using $\tfrac{d}{dx}e^{ix}=ie^{ix}$ and the fundamental theorem of calculus.
nodes.statement_short: Integral tower

nodes.name: First-order bound
nodes.statement: First $\|e^{ix}-1\|=\|\int_0^x i e^{is}\,ds\|\le|x|$.
nodes.statement_short: First-order bound

nodes.name: Second-order bound
nodes.statement:
Integrating,
$\|e^{ix}-1-ix\|=\|\int_0^x i(e^{is}-1)\,ds\|\le\int_0^{|x|}s\,ds=x^2/2$.
nodes.statement_short: Second-order bound

nodes.name: Cubic bound
nodes.statement:
Integrating once more,
$\|e^{ix}-1-ix+\tfrac{x^2}{2}\|=\|\int_0^x i(e^{is}-1-is)\,ds\|
\le\int_0^{|x|}\tfrac{s^2}{2}\,ds=|x|^3/6$, which is the cubic bound.
nodes.statement_short: Cubic bound

nodes.name: Quadratic bound
nodes.statement:
The
quadratic bound is $\|e^{ix}-1-ix\|+\tfrac{x^2}{2}\le x^2/2+x^2/2=x^2$.
The specific constant $1/6$ is not used downstream; any fixed constant on the
cubic term suffices.
nodes.statement_short: Quadratic bound

nodes.name: Sign of the quantity and the elementary bound
nodes.statement:
As above $\big|e^{y}(1-y)-1\big|=g(y)=1-e^{y}(1-y)\ge0$. Since $1-y+y^2\ge0$ and
$e^{y}\ge1+y$, we get $e^{y}(1-y+y^2)\ge(1+y)(1-y+y^2)=1+y^3\ge1$, i.e.
$e^{y}(1-y)+y^2e^{y}\ge1$, which rearranges to $g(y)\le y^2 e^{y}$.
nodes.statement_short: Sign of the quantity and the elementary bound

nodes.name: Why the unbounded form is needed
nodes.statement:
This form is
valid for all $y\ge0$ (not only $y\le1$); the factor $e^{y}$ is what is needed when
$y=\tfrac{t^2}{2}v_{n,i}$ is only known to be bounded, not $\le1$.
nodes.statement_short: Why the unbounded form is needed

nodes.name: Pointwise expansion
nodes.statement:
Apply the conditional expectation to the pointwise identity
$e^{it\Delta} = 1 + it\Delta - \tfrac{t^2}{2}\Delta^2
 + \big(e^{it\Delta}-1-it\Delta+\tfrac{t^2}{2}\Delta^2\big)$.
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise expansion

nodes.name: Linear and quadratic terms
nodes.statement:
The linear term
vanishes since $\E[\Delta_{n,i}\mid\filt_i]=0$ (conditional expectation commutes
with the coercion $\R\to\mathbb{C}$), and the quadratic term is $-\tfrac{t^2}{2}v_{n,i}$ by
definition of $v_{n,i}$.
nodes.statement_short: Linear and quadratic terms

nodes.name: Remainder bound
nodes.statement:
The remainder $r_{n,i}$ is the conditional expectation of
the last bracket, whose modulus is bounded pointwise by
$\min(2t^2\Delta^2,\,|t|^3|\Delta|^3)$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_exp_bound} applied to
$x=t\Delta$; conditional Jensen (\texttt{norm\_condExp\_le}) gives the stated bound.
nodes.statement_short: Remainder bound

nodes.name: Part (i): still a martingale difference array
nodes.statement:
Since $v_{n,l}$ is $\filt_l$-measurable and $l\le i$ for $l$ appearing in
$V_{n,i+1}$, the indicator $\indic_{\{V_{n,i+1}\le B\}}$ is $\filt_i$-measurable;
multiplying $\Delta_{n,i}$ by it therefore preserves both the $\filt_{i+1}$-
measurability and the martingale-difference property
($\E[\bar\Delta_{n,i}\mid\filt_i]=\indic_{\{V_{n,i+1}\le B\}}\E[\Delta_{n,i}\mid\filt_i]=0$),
and $\bar v_{n,i}=\E[\bar\Delta_{n,i}^2\mid\filt_i]=\indic_{\{V_{n,i+1}\le B\}}v_{n,i}$,
proving (i).
nodes.statement_short: Part (i): still a martingale difference array

nodes.name: Part (ii): no overshoot
nodes.statement:
For (ii): because $V$ is nondecreasing, the retained indices
$\{i:V_{n,i+1}\le B\}$ form a prefix $\{0,\dots,m\}$, and
$\bar V_n=\sum_{i\le m}v_{n,i}=V_{n,m+1}\le B$ by the choice of $m$ --- there is no
overshoot.
nodes.statement_short: Part (ii): no overshoot

nodes.name: Parts (iii)-(iv)
nodes.statement:
For (iii): on $\{V_n\le B\}$ every indicator equals $1$, so $\bar
V_n=V_n$ and $\bar S_n=S_n$; since $P(V_n\le B)\to1$ (as
$V_n\xrightarrow{\Prob}\sigma^2<B$), both $\bar V_n\xrightarrow{\Prob}\sigma^2$ and
(iv) follow, and the Lindeberg sum only decreases under truncation
($\bar\Delta_{n,i}^2\le\Delta_{n,i}^2$, $\{|\bar\Delta|>\varepsilon\}\subseteq\{|\Delta|>\varepsilon\}$).
nodes.statement_short: Parts (iii)-(iv)

nodes.name: Characteristic functions differ by at most twice the coupling probability
nodes.statement:
The final claim uses
$\|\charFun(\mathrm{law}\,S_n)(t)-\charFun(\mathrm{law}\,\bar S_n)(t)\|\le
2P(S_n\ne\bar S_n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Characteristic functions differ by at most twice the coupling probability

nodes.name: Split the conditional variance
nodes.statement:
Split $v_{n,i}=\E[\Delta_{n,i}^2\indic_{\{|\Delta_{n,i}|\le\varepsilon\}}\mid\filt_i]
+\E[\Delta_{n,i}^2\indic_{\{|\Delta_{n,i}|>\varepsilon\}}\mid\filt_i]$.
nodes.statement_short: Split the conditional variance

nodes.name: Bound both pieces
nodes.statement:
The first
conditional expectation is $\le\varepsilon^2$ (its integrand is $\le\varepsilon^2$
pointwise); the second is the $i$-th summand of $L_n(\varepsilon)$, hence
$\le L_n(\varepsilon)$ since every summand is nonnegative (conditional expectation
of a nonnegative function). The stated per-cell bound follows.
nodes.statement_short: Bound both pieces

nodes.name: Factor the increment
nodes.statement:
The one-step increment factorises as
$Z_{n,j+1}-Z_{n,j}=Z_{n,j}\big(\exp(it\Delta_{n,j}+\tfrac{t^2}{2}v_{n,j})-1\big)$,
where the factor $Z_{n,j}$ is $\filt_j$-measurable.
nodes.statement_short: Factor the increment

nodes.name: Conditional characteristic expansion
nodes.statement:
Taking conditional
expectation and using Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_cond_char},
\[
  \E[Z_{n,j+1}-Z_{n,j}\mid\filt_j]
  = Z_{n,j}\Big(e^{(t^2/2)v_{n,j}}\big(1-\tfrac{t^2}{2}v_{n,j}+r_{n,j}\big)-1\Big).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Conditional characteristic expansion

nodes.name: Bound the bracket
nodes.statement:
Writing $y=\tfrac{t^2}{2}v_{n,j}\ (\le\tfrac{t^2}{2}B')$, the bracket splits as
$\big(e^{y}(1-y)-1\big)+e^{y}r_{n,j}$; by
Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_real_exp_bound_pos}, $|e^{y}(1-y)-1|\le y^2 e^{y}
=\tfrac{t^4}{4}v_{n,j}^2\,e^{y}$. Hence the modulus is
$\le|Z_{n,j}|\,e^{(t^2/2)B'}\big(\tfrac{t^4}{4}v_{n,j}^2+\|r_{n,j}\|\big)$.
(The unbounded form of the elementary bound is essential here: $y$ is only bounded,
not $\le1$.)
nodes.statement_short: Bound the bracket

nodes.name: Telescope with the tower property
nodes.statement:
Summing over $j$, telescoping and using the tower property
$\E[Z_{n,k_n}-Z_{n,0}]=\sum_j\E\big[\E[Z_{n,j+1}-Z_{n,j}\mid\filt_j]\big]$,
\[
  \big|\E[Z_{n,k_n}]-1\big|
  \le e^{(t^2/2)B'}\,\E\!\Big[\tfrac{t^4}{4}\textstyle\sum_j v_{n,j}^2
      + e^{(t^2/2)B'}\sum_j\|r_{n,j}\|\Big].
\]
nodes.statement_short: Telescope with the tower property

nodes.name: Bounded convergence
nodes.statement:
Both sums tend to $0$ in probability
(Lemmas~\ref{lem:clt_sum_var_sq},~\ref{lem:clt_sum_rem}) and are uniformly
bounded, so by bounded convergence the expectations tend to $0$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded convergence

nodes.name: Reduce to bounded variance
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_truncation} we may assume $V_n\le B'$ a.s.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to bounded variance

nodes.name: Split the difference
nodes.statement:
Then
$e^{itS_n}=Z_{n,k_n}e^{-(t^2/2)V_n}$, so
\[
  \E[e^{itS_n}] - \exp(-\tfrac{t^2}{2}\sigma^2)
  = \E\big[Z_{n,k_n}\big(e^{-(t^2/2)V_n}-e^{-(t^2/2)\sigma^2}\big)\big]
    + e^{-(t^2/2)\sigma^2}\big(\E[Z_{n,k_n}]-1\big).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Split the difference

nodes.name: Second term vanishes
nodes.statement: The second term $\to0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:clt_Z_expectation}.
nodes.statement_short: Second term vanishes

nodes.name: First term vanishes by bounded convergence
nodes.statement:
In the first,
$|Z_{n,k_n}|\le e^{(t^2/2)B'}$ is bounded and
$e^{-(t^2/2)V_n}-e^{-(t^2/2)\sigma^2}\xrightarrow{\Prob}0$ (continuity of $\exp$
and $V_n\xrightarrow{\Prob}\sigma^2$), so bounded convergence gives $\to0$.
nodes.statement_short: First term vanishes by bounded convergence

nodes.name: Identify the Gaussian characteristic function
nodes.statement:
The target $\exp(-\sigma^2 t^2/2)$ is the characteristic function of
$\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$ (\texttt{charFun\_gaussianReal}).
nodes.statement_short: Identify the Gaussian characteristic function

nodes.name: Levy continuity theorem
nodes.statement:
Pointwise convergence
of characteristic functions to that of a fixed probability measure implies weak
convergence of the laws by the L\'evy continuity theorem
(\texttt{ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto\_of\_tendsto\_charFun}); injectivity is
\texttt{Measure.ext\_of\_charFun}. Together these give convergence in distribution
to $\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Levy continuity theorem

nodes.name: Deterministic normalization gives an MDA satisfying the hypotheses
nodes.statement:
Normalize $Q_{n,k}$ by the \emph{deterministic} $\sqrt{V_k v_k n}$: the increments
$\Delta_{m}=X_{m,k}(\xi_{m,k}-\theta_k)/\sqrt{V_k v_k n}$ form a martingale-difference array (for the
action-augmented filtration) whose predictable variation is $N_{n,k}/(v_k n)\xrightarrow{\Prob}1$
(consistency) and which satisfies the conditional Lindeberg condition, because the sampled responses
are i.i.d.\ with finite variance $V_k$ (each cell contributes
$\indic\{A_m=k\}\,V_k^{-1}v_k^{-1}n^{-1}\E[(\xi-\theta_k)^2\indic\{|\xi-\theta_k|>\varepsilon\sqrt{V_k v_k n}\}]$
and the truncated moment vanishes by dominated convergence).
nodes.statement_short: Deterministic normalization gives an MDA satisfying the hypotheses

nodes.name: Martingale CLT
nodes.statement:
Theorem~\ref{thm:mart_clt} then gives
$Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{V_k v_k n}\eqdist\mathcal N(0,1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Martingale CLT

nodes.name: Slutsky to random normalizer
nodes.statement:
Finally
$\sqrt{V_k v_k n}/\sqrt{V_k N_{n,k}}=\sqrt{v_k n/N_{n,k}}\xrightarrow{\Prob}1$, so Slutsky yields the
stated random-normalizer limit.
nodes.statement_short: Slutsky to random normalizer

nodes.name: Cramer-Wold reduction
nodes.statement:
By the Cramér--Wold device it suffices to prove that every scalar projection converges: for each
$w\in\R^K$, $\langle w, Q_n/\sqrt n\rangle = \big(\sum_k w_k Q_{n,k}\big)/\sqrt n$.
nodes.statement_short: Cramer-Wold reduction

nodes.name: Projection is an MDA with converging variation
nodes.statement:
The increments
$\sum_k w_k X_{i,k}(\xi_{i,k}-\theta_k)$ form a single martingale-difference array (the arm indicators
are disjoint, so the conditional square is $\sum_k w_k^2\indic\{A_i=k\}V_k$, giving predictable
variation $\sum_k w_k^2 V_k N_{n,k}/n\to\sum_k w_k^2 v_kV_k$; the conditional Lindeberg condition
holds arm-by-arm by dominated convergence).
nodes.statement_short: Projection is an MDA with converging variation

nodes.name: Martingale CLT for each projection
nodes.statement:
Theorem~\ref{thm:mart_clt} yields
$\big(\sum_k w_k Q_{n,k}\big)/\sqrt n\eqdist\mathcal N(0,\sum_k w_k^2 v_kV_k)$, which is precisely the
projection $\langle w,\cdot\rangle$ of the diagonal Gaussian (whose covariance is
$\mathrm{diag}(v_kV_k)$ by orthogonality of the coordinates, Lemma~\ref{lem:qv_orthogonal}).
nodes.statement_short: Martingale CLT for each projection

nodes.name: Joint limit
nodes.statement:
Cramér--Wold
then gives the joint limit.
nodes.statement_short: Joint limit

nodes.name: Factor and apply the joint CLT
nodes.statement:
Write $Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{N_{n,k}}=(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt n)\cdot\sqrt{n/N_{n,k}}$. The deterministic-normalizer
joint limit (Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_clt_joint}) gives
$(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt n)_k\eqdist\mathcal N(0,\mathrm{diag}(v_kV_k))$, and the coordinatewise scaling
vector $(\sqrt{n/N_{n,k}})_k\to(v_k^{-1/2})_k$ in probability (from $N_{n,k}/n\to v_k$ and
$v_k>0$).
nodes.statement_short: Factor and apply the joint CLT

nodes.name: Diagonal rescaling
nodes.statement:
Multivariate Slutsky (a continuous coordinatewise product against a constant limit) then
sends the product to the image of $\mathcal N(0,\mathrm{diag}(v_kV_k))$ under the diagonal scaling
$\mathrm{diag}(v_k^{-1/2})$, which is $\mathcal N(0,\mathrm{diag}(V_k))$.
nodes.statement_short: Diagonal rescaling

nodes.name: Exact identity
nodes.statement:
By the exact Bahadur identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator_bahadur}),
$\hat\theta_{n,k}-\theta_k=(Q_{n,k}+(\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k))/(N_{n,k}+1)$, so
\[
  \sqrt{N_{n,k}}(\hat\theta_{n,k}-\theta_k)
    = \frac{Q_{n,k}}{\sqrt{N_{n,k}}}\cdot\frac{N_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}+1}
      + (\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k)\frac{\sqrt{N_{n,k}}}{N_{n,k}+1}.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Exact identity

nodes.name: Joint CLT and factor limits
nodes.statement:
The self-normalized martingale vector $(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{N_{n,k}})_k$ converges jointly to
$\mathcal N(0,\mathrm{diag}(V_k))$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_clt_joint_selfnorm}), while the two
coordinatewise scaling factors tend to $1$ and $0$ in probability (as $N_{n,k}\to\infty$).
nodes.statement_short: Joint CLT and factor limits

nodes.name: Slutsky
nodes.statement:
Multivariate Slutsky (a continuous coordinatewise affine map against the constant limit $(1,0)$)
therefore leaves the Gaussian limit unchanged.
nodes.statement_short: Slutsky

nodes.name: Decomposition and three limits
nodes.statement:
Decompose
$S_{\tau_n}/\sqrt{\tau_n}=(S_{c_n}/\sqrt{c_n})\cdot\sqrt{c_n/\tau_n}+(S_{\tau_n}-S_{c_n})/\sqrt{\tau_n}$.
The base term $S_{c_n}/\sqrt{c_n}\eqdist\mathcal N(0,v)$ is the i.i.d.\ central limit theorem
(Theorem~\ref{thm:mart_clt}, in the form of the Lindeberg--L\'evy theorem) precomposed with the
deterministic subsequence $c_n$; the scaling $\sqrt{c_n/\tau_n}\to1$ in probability by regularity, so
Slutsky preserves the limit; and the window remainder $(S_{\tau_n}-S_{c_n})/\sqrt{\tau_n}\to0$ in
probability, since on the event $|\tau_n-c_n|\le\varepsilon c_n$ (of probability $\to1$) the increment
is bounded by the maximal increment over a window of length $\varepsilon c_n$, which is
$O(\sqrt{\varepsilon c_n})$ in $L^1$ by Doob's maximal inequality; letting $\varepsilon\to0$ gives the
claim.
nodes.statement_short: Decomposition and three limits

nodes.name: Lean formalization notes
nodes.statement:
\emph{Formalization.} \texttt{AlphaRAR.tendstoInDistribution\_anscombe\_iid}, assembled from the
base CLT along a subsequence (\texttt{tendstoInDistribution\_clt\_comp}, wrapping Mathlib's
\texttt{tendstoInDistribution\_inv\_sqrt\_mul\_sum\_sub}), the negligibility of the window remainder
(\texttt{AlphaRAR.tendstoInMeasure\_window}, via the Doob maximal inequality
\texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal} on the i.i.d.-sum martingale \texttt{AlphaRAR.martingale\_iidSum}),
and two Slutsky steps (\texttt{TendstoInDistribution.mul\_of\_tendstoInMeasure\_const},
Mathlib's \texttt{TendstoInDistribution.add\_of\_tendstoInMeasure\_const}). The regularity
$\tau_n/c_n\to1$ is
essential: for a general adaptive $\tau_n\to\infty$ the statement is false (one can freeze the
self-normalized martingale above its typical value by pausing the index near a level crossing, using
the law of the iterated logarithm). This lemma is the standalone martingale-CLT ingredient that
Lemma~\ref{lem:componentwise} calls for, and the missing piece for the sparse componentwise CLT
(Corollary~\ref{cor:sparse_clt}): with the per-arm regularity $N_{n,k}/c_{n,k}\to1$ supplied, applying
it coordinatewise to the sampled response martingale $Q_{\cdot,k}$ yields
$Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{N_{n,k}}\eqdist\mathcal N(0,V_k)$ even when $v_k=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization notes

nodes.name: Lean assembly
nodes.statement:
\texttt{AlphaRAR.tendstoInDistribution\_anscombe\_iid}, assembled from the
base CLT along a subsequence (\texttt{tendstoInDistribution\_clt\_comp}, wrapping Mathlib's
\texttt{tendstoInDistribution\_inv\_sqrt\_mul\_sum\_sub}), the negligibility of the window remainder
(\texttt{AlphaRAR.tendstoInMeasure\_window}, via the Doob maximal inequality
\texttt{AlphaRAR.mart\_maximal} on the i.i.d.-sum martingale \texttt{AlphaRAR.martingale\_iidSum}),
and two Slutsky steps (\texttt{TendstoInDistribution.mul\_of\_tendstoInMeasure\_const},
Mathlib's \texttt{TendstoInDistribution.add\_of\_tendstoInMeasure\_const}).
nodes.statement_short: Lean assembly

nodes.name: Why regularity is essential
nodes.statement:
The regularity
$\tau_n/c_n\to1$ is
essential: for a general adaptive $\tau_n\to\infty$ the statement is false (one can freeze the
self-normalized martingale above its typical value by pausing the index near a level crossing, using
the law of the iterated logarithm). This lemma is the standalone martingale-CLT ingredient that
Lemma~\ref{lem:componentwise} calls for, and the missing piece for the sparse componentwise CLT
(Corollary~\ref{cor:sparse_clt}): with the per-arm regularity $N_{n,k}/c_{n,k}\to1$ supplied, applying
it coordinatewise to the sampled response martingale $Q_{\cdot,k}$ yields
$Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{N_{n,k}}\eqdist\mathcal N(0,V_k)$ even when $v_k=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Why regularity is essential

nodes.name: Reindex and apply Anscombe
nodes.statement:
The sampled responses of arm $k$ are i.i.d.\ with mean $\theta_k$ and variance $V_k$
(a globally i.i.d.\ representative is \texttt{AlphaRAR.sampledClean}), and reindexing the pulls gives
$Q_{n,k}=\sum_{i<N_{n,k}}(\xi_i-\theta_k)=S_{N_{n,k}}$ (\texttt{respMart\_eq\_sum\_sampledSeq}). Apply
the Anscombe random-time CLT (Lemma~\ref{lem:anscombe_clt}) with $\tau_n=N_{n,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reindex and apply Anscombe

nodes.statement: \emph{Formalization.}
nodes.statement_short: Lean formalization heading

nodes.statement:
\texttt{AlphaRAR.respMart\_selfNorm\_anscombe\_tendsto}: the clean-sample setup
mirrors the LIL development (\texttt{iIndepFun\_sampledResponse}, \texttt{map\_sampledResponse\_eq},
\texttt{sampledSeq\_ae\_eq\_sampledClean}), supplying the i.i.d.\ hypotheses of
Lemma~\ref{lem:anscombe_clt}, and the almost-everywhere identity
$S_{N_{n,k}}=Q_{n,k}$ transfers the limit law to $(\sqrt{N_{n,k}})^{-1}Q_{n,k}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lean declarations

nodes.name: Bahadur identity and Slutsky
nodes.statement:
By the exact Bahadur identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator_bahadur}),
$\sqrt{N_{n,k}}(\hat\theta_{n,k}-\theta_k)=(Q_{n,k}/\sqrt{N_{n,k}})\cdot\frac{N_{n,k}}{N_{n,k}+1}
 + (\theta_{0,k}-\theta_k)\frac{\sqrt{N_{n,k}}}{N_{n,k}+1}$; the scaling factors tend to $1$ and $0$
in probability (as $N_{n,k}\to\infty$), and Slutsky applied to
Lemma~\ref{lem:mart_clt_selfnorm_arm_sparse} gives the claim.
nodes.statement_short: Bahadur identity and Slutsky
